[189] St report no. 16 (1992-93) Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period

[190] Recommendation from the Ministry of Defence dated 8 January 1993, approved by the Cabinet on the same day

[191] The announcement heralds the transition to a new defense structure

[192] In this report, the Government presents proposals for main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities and development for the period

[193] In formulating the main guidelines of this report, the Ministry has based itself in particular on

[194] Recommendation from the Defence Commission of 1990 (NOU

[195] The Chief of Defence's principled view of the Armed Forces' needs and development

[196] The government's renewal program for state activities

[197] In addition, the Defence Study 91 has been included as an important material during the consideration of defence-related considerations and priorities

[198] The Ministry aims to first describe the security and defense policy basis and the economic framework conditions for the peace organization and war structure that are the goal of the restructuring process

[199] Next, the Ministry will specify which measures are considered necessary to achieve this goal

[200] The consideration of building a more flexible organization, better able to meet uncertain and unstable framework conditions, will be given importance

[201] The period covered by the years leading up to the turn of the millennium will be a transitional period

[202] International changes and a more difficult socio-economic basis make it necessary to make adjustments and reductions in the organization and activities of the Armed Forces

[203] The period 1994-98 will represent the transition from the defense structure built up throughout the 1970s and 1980s to a leaner, modernized structure, without this structure being fully realized in 1998, at the end of the period

[204] The choices and decisions made during this period in relation to the design of the Armed Forces will have a significant impact on the defense that Norway will be able to have after the year

[205] While throughout the 1970s and 1980s it was possible to rely on steady budget growth and predictable international framework conditions, the situation changed significantly in the first half of the 1990s

[206] The Armed Forces are facing a restructuring process that will clarify both their role and tasks, and the activities and structure that support them

[207] The restructuring process will lead to a new force structure adapted to new international framework conditions and current budget levels

[208] This process will determine the future place of the Armed Forces in Norwegian society, and the significance this will have for Norway's place in and connection to the international community

[209] The use of military force and the role and function of the Armed Forces in Europe in the 1990s were characterized by unstable international developments and the new possibilities for conflict that were emerging

[210] Structural objectives for the year 2000 and in the long term

[211] To ensure good economic use of resources and targeted and coordinated development of the Armed Forces, it is of great importance to establish certain long-term fundamentals for both structural development and operations

[212] Due to the fundamental uncertainty that exists in the long term, however, it is also necessary to ensure flexibility and freedom of action in defense planning

[213] Planning under uncertainty and ongoing adaptations of the Armed Forces' activities and development to variable framework conditions will therefore have to characterise the coordination and decision-making process to a greater extent than before

[214] The challenge is to plan under uncertain framework conditions

[215] It is becoming more important to be able to assess the consequences of uncertainty and unpredictability for how the Armed Forces should be designed

[216] If the design of a defense is to be carried out in light of uncertainty, the organization must be made more flexible

[217] The extent of the uncertainty must be clarified and included in the planning

[218] It will be an important task to assess how the defense organization can best be structured in accordance with the need for increased flexibility

[219] This requires, among other things, greater consistency and balance between operations and investment

[220] For a period as long as the period up to the year 2000, no government can guarantee stable development conditions

[221] This becomes all the more difficult when one seeks to establish guidelines for the years after this period

[222] In order to achieve appropriate and good utilization of allocated resources, it is also important that the Armed Forces are given a management basis with a sufficient time horizon and with the greatest possible degree of coherence and stability in the ongoing short-term and long-term management basis

[223] The report should therefore be a necessary management basis for the restructuring of the Armed Forces, but must be based on the fact that developments in several areas make it very difficult to establish stable planning assumptions

[224] To give the restructuring process a somewhat longer time perspective than the validity period of this report, the Ministry is basing its decision on the war structure recommended by the majority of the Defence Commission of 1990 (FK

[225] However, the Commission itself assumed that this recommended structure could only be realized in the period

[226] As part of the implementation of this long-term goal, the Government wishes to define the structure that will be realized through the report

[227] This structure will at this point have only to a lesser extent achieved the quality requirements that the majority of FK90's assumed for their recommended war structure

[228] At the next five-year report in 1997, the Ministry will, as part of the long-term follow-up of the Commission majority's recommended structure, consider in more detail what consequences changes in international, economic and technological framework conditions will have for the further development of the Armed Forces up to the year 2000 and in the period that follows

[229] This means that, given the greater uncertainty regarding future developments in the framework conditions, the Ministry will have to consider in more detail whether actual developments in the coming years may make it appropriate to view the actual implementation of FK90's structure in a different light

[230] It would be unrealistic to tie the development of the defense structure as it should be in 2008 to the unstable situation as it exists

[231] So much can happen along the way

[232] that the goal of realizing the Commission's long-term structure must be assessed on an ongoing basis and designed in relation to the level of ambition that will be used as the basis for determining the tasks of the Armed Forces

[233] In this process, the Ministry will be open to the possibility that a new defense concept may prove to be both relevant, desirable and necessary during the period

[234] It is therefore necessary to assess what consequences continued changes in security policy, economic and technological framework conditions may have for the longer term design of the Armed Forces and for the Armed Forces' function and tasks in a longer time perspective

[235] Both for the concrete, short-term planning related to the period 1994-98 and for the more uncertain, long-term investigation of alternative design strategies for the following years, certain main guidelines must form the basis

[236] It is necessary to look more closely at how the security policy, socio-economic and technological foundations interact at both the defense structure and budget level

[237] The security policy and socio-economic situation and developments affect what funds the Armed Forces receive, the security policy framework conditions and challenges affect what the Government wants from these funds, and technological developments affect how much of the equipment the Armed Forces can obtain that is considered desirable and necessary

[238] BACKGROUND AND BASIS FOR THE ANNOUNCEMENT Throughout the 1970s and 1980s, the Armed Forces have been able to rely on predictable, steady budget growth

[239] This has made it possible to maintain a credible defense that has been able to fulfill its assigned tasks

[240] Despite a steady budget development, an increasing imbalance has arisen during the period between budget funds on the one hand and the force structure and scope of the activities on the other

[241] This has resulted in the operating share of defense budgets being higher than it should be, at the expense of necessary material procurement

[242] In line with the recommendation from the majority in FK90, the level of ambition for the Armed Forces will be the ability to repel an invasion attempt, limited to one part of the country

[243] This requires a balanced defense, consisting of all the main components of a modern defense

[244] Against the background of the extensive changes in international politics since 1989, the threat landscape for Norwegian security has changed

[245] Norway is not currently facing any direct military threat, but instead faces several new challenges created by a completely new situation, especially in Europe and the former Soviet Union

[246] Developments in Europe and elsewhere in the world are characterized by uncertainty, instability and unpredictability

[247] An unclear situation can create many unexpected challenges that, at a later date, could develop into threats to Norwegian security interests

[248] There is therefore still a need to have a balanced defense with anti-invasion capabilities

[249] This level of ambition has direct consequences for the force structure the Armed Forces must have

[250] The aim of this report is to describe in more detail the war structure that must be established to maintain this level of ambition

[251] The war structure must govern the peace organization and peace activities

[252] In this context, the announcement represents the beginning of a new phase in the development of the Armed Forces

[253] While it has previously been pointed out that there is a mismatch between budget funds and structure/activity, this report will indicate how this mismatch can and should be removed

[254] This is done by describing the starting point for the proposed war structure, and assessing and pointing out specific restructuring measures that must be implemented to achieve the desired consistency between the planning period's budget framework and the war strategy

[255] The notification is therefore primarily a restructuring notification, in which the basis for, the selection and implementation of necessary restructuring measures are described with a view to necessary operational reductions, also against the background of a more difficult economic situation

[256] The report will therefore present the choices the Armed Forces now face

[257] The Government wishes to ensure that these roadmaps provide a high degree of freedom of action, in the sense that important decisions related to the roadmap can be made during the planning period on the basis of the developments that have occurred up to that point and the developments that can then be predicted

[258] The background is the significant uncertainty of a security policy, economic and military-technological nature that still prevails

[259] The government wants to provide the necessary freedom of action for such later decisions

[260] This gives the Government and the Storting, during the period 1995-98, the opportunity to decide on what level of ambition, with associated tasks and defense concept, should be the basis for the long-term design of the war structure

[261] During this period, major investment decisions will have to be made to realize the planned structure

[262] To avoid major misinvestments, these decisions should not be made until the issue of the defense concept and structural goals has been clarified

[263] GENERAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE DEFENCE COMMISSION OF

[264] This report is based on the assessments and recommended structure presented by the 1990 Defence Commission in its report submitted in March

[265] FC90's assessments and recommendations therefore appear as a starting point for the transformation and restructuring process that the Armed Forces are now facing

[266] The Commission's assessments were made during a period that was markedly characterized by changes in international framework conditions

[267] This process of change has continued and in many areas has increased in scope and strength

[268] Some aspects of the development seem to be fairly clear, while other aspects are still open

[269] The consequences for European security and stability of the international upheavals appear, in the Government's opinion, even greater after the recommendation was made

[270] New forms of security policy cooperation and participation appear to be growing in importance

[271] At the same time, uncertainty factors have become more numerous and stronger

[272] Europe will change, but it has become more difficult to have a qualified opinion about the direction the changes will take and how quickly the changes will occur

[273] Socio-economic development has been very rapid since Fiscal Year 1990 made its recommendation

[274] The basis for budget development, as it appeared at the beginning of 1992, has changed significantly by the end

[275] In its recommendation, the Defence Commission places great emphasis on both a broad security policy review and a more detailed description of the defence basis - including technological and societal factors - that should influence the design of the Defence Forces in the period

[276] until the year

[277] In the recommendation, the Commission assesses factors that may hinder stability and predictability in international politics and explains why uncertainty and uncertainty characterize international developments, particularly in Europe

[278] The Commission also reviews important foreign and security policy developments of significance to Norwegian security and the design of Norway's defense

[279] Based on these extensive international changes, it makes recommendations related to key points for Norwegian defense and security policy

[280] Based on such a foundation, the Commission discusses the design of future Norwegian defense

[281] The commission reviews key guidelines for this, and discusses which tasks should be given to the Armed Forces in the coming years

[282] The conscription system is discussed, as well as the quality requirements that should be set for a modern defense, and what consequences this may have for the size, design and quality of the Armed Forces' war structure

[283] The relationship between operations and investments is given crucial importance in this context

[284] The Commission considers in more detail what requirements a desired qualitative level sets for the investment framework and sees this in direct connection with the savings potential that can be linked to the operating budget

[285] The Chief of Defence's study (Defence Study 91) is discussed in more detail

[286] The study has provided important conditions and impetus for the Commission's work

[287] On this basis, the Commission makes a fundamental assessment of and recommendation for the future design of Norway's defense, in which a main economic course and a recommended war structure are presented and described in more detail

[288] The economic main course is based on zero growth through the period until 2008, starting from SEK III

[289] The Commission's recommended structure assumes continuation of this budget level throughout the planning period, and is based on annual operating savings of 1 percent from 1992-2002, which then level off

[290] The recommendation is also based partly on a closer assessment of the different branches of defense, taking into account the requirement to have a balanced defense, partly on a more detailed regional prioritization, and partly on consideration of Norway's relationship with the country's allies and reinforcement issues

[291] The recommendation from the majority of FKD90 involves a sharp reduction in the war structure, and an adaptation of the peace organization to this

[292] The commission touches on how the changes may affect Norway's need for allied reinforcements

[293] According to the Commission, this need is not only a function of the defense capabilities of Norway itself, but also of international developments and the challenges this creates for Norway and the ability of Norway's allies to send reinforcements

[294] Reductions in the military forces of important allied countries could lead to a situation where reductions in Norway's defense occur in parallel with the weakening of allied countries' capacity to send reinforcements

[295] The majority of the Defence Commission has presented a proposal for a future defence structure that it believes can be realised if given assumptions, including annual operational savings, are met

[296] The Commission emphasizes that it is the specified structure that represents its recommendation, not the recommended budget level

[297] In the Government's opinion, both the majority's consensus regarding the description of the security policy and defense basis for the design of the Armed Forces and the recommendation on future defense structure, in addition to the individual special statements, contain all key assessments and viewpoints

[298] The Commission's assessment of the pace at which adjustments must be implemented in order to achieve the necessary consistency between the budget level on the one hand and the organization and activities on the other

[299] is of significant importance as a basis for this report

[300] However, the Commission has not shown how this can be achieved

[301] The Government aims to make this concrete with this announcement

[302] The majority of the Commission believes that the regional political consequences of changes in the Armed Forces' peacekeeping operations must be assessed in relation to the trade-off between operations and investment

[303] The consideration of an efficient organization that is able to solve the tasks assigned to it to the greatest possible extent must be the guiding principle here

[304] The Commission points out that the international situation can change rapidly

[305] The need to maintain competence and knowledge and an organization that functions effectively in relation to the assigned tasks becomes all the more important

[306] Technological developments and requirements for education and training levels mean that it is becoming increasingly difficult and requires longer to rebuild sufficient military capacity and expertise, if these have already declined too far or have been lost

[307] The Government believes that it is of considerable value that the Commission's recommendation provides a broad cross-political basis for the continuation of Norwegian defense and security policy

[308] Broad agreement on main lines and principles is important in an area of significant national importance

[309] A summary of the Commission's recommendation is given in Appendix

[310] The Ministry has placed emphasis on limiting the scope of the report

[311] The main guidelines for the coming years are designed as a perspective outline

[312] The report primarily addresses the main elements of the future structure and activities of the Armed Forces

[313] Emphasis is placed on both describing the recommended structure for the year 2000 and providing guidelines and instructions for the types of measures that must be taken to implement this structure

[314] Detailed plans for material procurement and for new buildings and facilities are not discussed

[315] The Ministry also wishes to present key issues and shed more light on the significant choices we, from the Norwegian side, face regarding the design of future Norwegian defense

[316] Great emphasis is therefore placed on presenting connections between the factors that have the strongest impact on the restructuring process, and the complex development opportunities that the design should take place in relation to

[317] Form and content

[318] The Ministry has chosen to publish the report as an independent document

[319] This means that neither FK90 nor FS91 are commented on in their entirety

[320] The Ministry's assessments of FK90's recommendation will be made in connection with the individual chapters

[321] The report is divided into 11 chapters

[322] A bullet number system has been used primarily to facilitate references and references

[323] Chapter 2 constitutes a summary of the report

[324] Chapter 3 clarifies the security policy basis and Chapter 4 discusses defense policy, economic and other framework conditions for the main guidelines the Government proposes for the design of the future defense structure

[325] Guidelines for the design of the Armed Forces are described in Chapter 5, where the Armed Forces' tasks, target structure and main functions are discussed in more detail

[326] Based on these framework conditions, warstructure and peace organization are described in more detail in the following chapters 6 and

[327] Next, alternative defense concepts are discussed in Chapter 8, and then the strategy and measures for the restructuring process are described in Chapter 9, and the new management concept and its consequences are described in Chapter

[328] The importance and role of the armed forces in Norwegian society is described in the concluding chapter

[329] A summary of the Recommendation from the Defence Commission's report (NOU 1992:12) is available as Appendix

[330] A summary of the consultation statements to FK90 is attached as Appendix 2. The Chief of Defence's principled view of the Armed Forces' needs and development is set out in the Appendix

[331] The status report on the implementation of the main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the period 1989-93 (St meld no. 54 (1987-88)) is discussed in the appendix

[332] The Defence Study 91 is included as an unprinted appendix to the Defence Committee in graded and ungraded versions

[333] GOALS AND PURPOSES OF THE LONG-TERM REPORT

[334] Socio-economic, security and defense policy background

[335] With this Long-Term Report on the Activities and Development of the Armed Forces 1994-98, the Government wishes to clarify and establish both framework conditions and goals for the Armed Forces

[336] The starting point is an assessment of what changes have occurred regarding the foundation and framework conditions for the development of the Armed Forces

[337] These framework conditions exist in the form of international political, military and strategic development, international and national economic development, and military-technological development

[338] The changes within all these areas have been extensive in recent years

[339] They present Norway with a new reality when the Armed Forces are to be assigned tasks and a more defined security policy and societal role

[340] The security policy basis for the design of the Armed Forces and the determination of the war structure is characterized by the fact that Europe has entered a new era

[341] The Cold War has ended

[342] The entire Euro-Atlantic security area is in a transitional phase at the beginning of a new era

[343] The end of the previously divided Europe, and the major changes taking place in its wake, have created new uncertainty and instability

[344] The development is characterized by a multifaceted, complex picture, where unpredictability is growing

[345] At the same time, the new era has created completely new opportunities

[346] New patterns of cooperation and constellations are emerging, helping to change the basis for European and transatlantic security

[347] The need for collective security is growing in the new Europe

[348] To ensure stability, it is necessary to develop mutually binding cooperation

[349] Existing and new international organizations are being developed and created to build on the need to establish a security community across old dividing lines

[350] In the new situation, the importance and role of security policy instruments are changing

[351] This also has an impact on the role and function of military forces in interstate relations

[352] Ensuring European security is increasingly becoming the responsibility of European countries themselves

[353] At the same time, European development is characterized by instability and contradictions in Eastern Europe, where ethnic-national disputes represent a major conflict potential

[354] The war in the former Yugoslavia could threaten to spread to other parts of the Balkans

[355] Conflicts may also increase in the Carpathian regions

[356] The ripple effects could be significant for the security policy order in Europe

[357] Conflict lines and tensions can spread between regions and intensify regional contradictions and disputes

[358] The effects of the end of the former division of Europe, the dissolution of the Soviet Union and the unification of Germany, in parallel with the economic downturn in Europe, have already resulted in new instability in the form of, among other things, increasing social unrest and internal contradictions also in Western Europe

[359] Some signs indicate that contradictions and rivalry between Western countries may also increase

[360] However, this must be seen against the background of the very close mutual ties that Western countries have established

[361] Global factors such as energy and raw materials, environmental issues and population explosion, in addition to ethnic, religious and cultural divisions, also give new aspects to security policy challenges

[362] Based on these factors, changes and key developments, the goals of Norwegian security policy remain largely unchanged, but the instruments for safeguarding Norwegian security must be actively adapted to new international framework conditions, which Norway must increasingly participate in shaping on an equal footing with neighboring countries and allies

[363] Norway's military-strategic situation is characterized by the fact that the Russian force level in the highlands has so far been less affected by the changes in the former Soviet Union than is the case for Central and Eastern Europe

[364] This will change, however, if the reductions announced by the Russian side and largely enshrined in agreements reached are implemented

[365] While Russian forces are withdrawing from the continent, Norway remains a neighbor to one of the world's largest military force concentrations

[366] However, the Russian forces in the north are not connected to an offensive force capacity in Central Europe, as they were during the Soviet era

[367] They are undergoing a transformation aimed at a more defensive structure and a significantly lower level for the land forces

[368] The Russian Northern Fleet is expected to largely maintain its capacity even if the number of vessels is reduced

[369] The challenges in relation to Northern Norway have therefore changed to a lesser extent than the challenges in relation to Southern Norway

[370] As a result of the political and military changes on the continent, there is no longer any direct threat of invasion against Southern Norway

[371] This region is largely shielded by the Allied defense of the Baltic Sea outlets, and the Russian military capacity in the Baltic Sea area has changed significantly

[372] These conditions still make it necessary to prioritize the defense of Northern Norway

[373] By concentrating military activities in the north, Norway will simultaneously meet the needs to maintain the necessary military expertise, including through the ability to practice brigade formations

[374] This expertise is also necessary for Norwegian participation in multinational forces

[375] The fundamental security policy goals that form the basis for the Armed Forces' tasks are

[376] to prevent war and contribute to stability and peaceful development; - to protect Norwegian freedom of action against political and military pressure, and safeguard Norwegian rights and interests; - to defend Norwegian land, sea and air territory against violation and attack

[377] For a more detailed discussion of the Armed Forces' goals and tasks, see chap

[378] and 5.2. The international economy is characterized by stagnation

[379] Economic problems increasingly characterize the economies of several Western countries

[380] The restructuring and social upheavals in the east have so far led to major structural economic problems that have created social unrest

[381] A difficult economic situation in European countries is contributing to political turbulence, growing nationalism and rivalry

[382] The Norwegian economy is going through a difficult period

[383] Aid from abroad has failed to arrive, and restructuring problems in Norwegian business, exacerbated by a weak banking and insurance system, have led to high unemployment and weakened the state's financial situation

[384] This has created a need for economic austerity measures

[385] Both the Norwegian and international economic developments and situations represent a serious challenge, which affects the development of the defense budget

[386] The government will use economic policy in a long-term strategy to increase value creation and employment

[387] This strategy has consequences both for the total expenditure of the state budget - where the Government's goal is that state expenditure should not increase by more than the gross domestic product for mainland Norway - and for the priorities in the budget

[388] Tightening measures must be implemented to preserve long-term fiscal freedom of action

[389] The defense budget must also be weighed against the prioritized goals of economic policy

[390] Maintaining invasion defense capability

[391] To fulfill the tasks and role

[392] As a result of the new framework conditions imposed on the Norwegian Armed Forces, it is necessary to establish a war structure that will govern the peace organization and peace operations

[393] The purpose of the long-term report is therefore to describe and explain both the war structure and peace organization that are necessary for the Armed Forces to be able to carry out its tasks and fulfill its assigned role

[394] The government will therefore aim to achieve the war structure recommended by the majority in FK

[395] The necessity of achieving this structure will have strong implications for the budget development and restructuring process the Armed Forces will undergo

[396] Central in this context is the necessity of maintaining the Armed Forces' capability for invasion defense

[397] In line with the recommendation from the majority of FK90, the Government aims to maintain a time-limited invasion defense limited to one part of the country

[398] This is a consequence of the new international and military-technological framework conditions

[399] After the end of the Cold War, developments in Europe and in international politics in general have been characterized by uncertainty and instability

[400] The internal development in Russia is unclear; an internal power struggle is underway

[401] No one knows the outcome

[402] A relapse into authoritarian rule cannot be ruled out

[403] The disarmament agreements have not yet been implemented

[404] Because they cover certain types of military forces that were more dominant in Central Europe than in Northern Europe, they will also not be able to provide the same security benefits in the North as in Central Europe

[405] In this light, the Government believes it is still necessary to maintain a defense structure that gives the Armed Forces the ability to flexibly solve assigned tasks, including the ability to resist an invasion attempt in a region of the country

[406] In accordance with the current security policy situation, the invasion defense capability is initially linked to Northern Norway

[407] At the same time, emphasis is placed on strategic mobility, so that this antiinvasion capacity can be adapted to changing security policy framework conditions

[408] A certain level of ability to defend the rest of the country against more limited operations against important individual targets and infrastructure must be maintained

[409] Challenges to Norwegian security can also arise at sea in the form of a local conflict that affects vital Norwegian interests

[410] Because air and naval forces are mobile, regional prioritization will have less significance in such contexts

[411] In the new Europe, the threat to Norway's security will not only be a at least in the short term - remote possibility of a direct attack on Norwegian territory

[412] It will also consist of threats to the rules, norms and standards that are necessary to maintain a minimum of order in Europe, and which are codified in the CSCE

[413] Ethnically and religiously based local conflicts can spread, and they can break with the established set of norms

[414] Consequently, Norway, like other NATO countries, will have to contribute to emergency forces that can be quickly present in vulnerable parts of the NATO area, as well as to efforts in peacekeeping and peacemaking operations

[415] Throughout the post-war period, the Norwegian Armed Forces have been designed as a balanced defense in the sense that it contains most of the main components that are included in modern armed forces

[416] A balanced force structure is, among other things, a prerequisite for the Armed Forces to be able to cooperate with and lead allied reinforcements on Norwegian territory more easily and more credibly

[417] The individual main elements of the defense structure have been coordinated in such a way that no gaps can arise in the overall structure that could be exploited by a potential adversary

[418] Through the report, the government emphasizes avoiding that Norway be placed in a position where the country could be challenged in sectors where we lack appropriate means of response

[419] A balanced defense is a prerequisite for maintaining anti-invasion capacity

[420] It is also resource-demanding for Norway, and will be increasingly so, as requirements for technological standards, education, training and management levels increase

[421] The capacity to provide its own forces with the necessary expertise in all main components of a modern defense can give Norway the desired freedom of action in crisis situations and critical periods when allied reinforcements are on the way

[422] Requirements for quantity and quality In order to establish such a defense, clear requirements are placed on the war structure, both quantitatively and qualitatively

[423] This means that peace organizations and activities are also subject to the same requirements

[424] The target for quality is a soberly assessed level in light of the expected technological development of other countries' defense

[425] The proposed war structure thus does not represent high-tech defense, but a necessary and sober adaptation to the new demands of a modern combat environment

[426] Both the qualitative and quantitative requirements are also tailored to the challenges facing Norway in light of international developments

[427] Norway is still dependent on support from allied countries, and that they can send reinforcements to Norway

[428] This also requires personal effort

[429] Future Norwegian defense efforts should at all times be at a level that provides a basis for Norway to be able to request and expect allied reinforcements

[430] However, the conditions and framework for - in addition to the content of - the allied cooperation that forms the basis for the ability and willingness to send reinforcements, are also changing

[431] Norway must actively contribute to ensuring that this change takes place in a way that safeguards Norwegian security interests

[432] The major international changes and the significant uncertainty that characterize developments together form the background for the Government to continue to find it necessary to maintain the Armed Forces also as an antiinvasion defense

[433] In addition to requirements for quality, the Armed Forces' future war structure must be based on requirements for mobility and protection

[434] A gradual improvement in quality must be planned throughout the entire planning period, an improvement that must be continued

[435] Significant parts of the Norwegian Armed Forces' war organisation currently have equipment of such a low standard that the departments would not be able to carry out their tasks in a modern combat environment

[436] Financial framework and operational savings The Government's goal is to realize the defense structure

[437] Due to the difficult economic situation, we will have to spend somewhat longer on realizing the structure than the Commission assumed

[438] Within such a framework, the Armed Forces must be able to handle minor deviations in the annual budgets without losing sight of the long-term structural goals

[439] The Armed Forces must therefore be prepared to demonstrate flexibility with regard to fluctuations in annual defense appropriations

[440] The resource allocation to the Armed Forces in future years' state budgets will be subject to annual budget assessments in the same way

[441] It must be possible to make budget level changes and reprioritizations each year during the long-term reporting period based on overall assessments of the budget situation and the current security challenges

[442] In order to maintain the ability to defend against invasion, the budget framework must be increased to the level required during the planning period, i.e. within three to five years

[443] The majority of the Defense Commission recommended, i.e

[444] Stage III level, compensated for price and wage increases

[445] This means that the total resource allocation for the period 1994-98 will depend on the pace of the increase in the annual budgets, and is expected to be somewhat below that of the Commission majority

[446] This has made it all the more crucial that necessary savings are implemented

[447] These savings must be made through the restructuring and reduction process that the Armed Forces are now facing

[448] The changes are primarily a result of the fact that there has previously been a mismatch between the budget framework and the scope of the business

[449] The defense organization must therefore be reduced in accordance with the existing budget framework and the assigned tasks

[450] Secondly, the restructuring is a result of the new international situation imposing requirements that make it necessary to design the Armed Forces in accordance with new challenges and tasks

[451] Requirements for both quality and quantity regarding the established war structure and peace organization must be met

[452] One cannot be chosen at the expense of the other

[453] For this to be possible, the restructuring and reduction process must be designed in such a way that necessary operational savings can be made

[454] In this way, material acquisitions can be prioritized

[455] Without the described material acquisitions, the planned war structure will not be able to be established

[456] It is therefore critical to the restructuring process that operational cost-saving measures can be identified, designed and implemented to a scale and pace that makes it possible to carry out the development of the war structure and the peace organization in accordance with the set goals

[457] Given that the overall budget framework for the period is expected to be somewhat below the framework recommended by the majority of the Commission, it will be necessary to protect investment funds in this context

[458] This will mean that the level of activity in the Armed Forces' peacekeeping operations must be cut even further compared to the Commission majority's recommendation

[459] This must also be seen in the light of the fact that the Government has chosen to assign new tasks to the Armed Forces, and that there are indications that the proposed war structure will cost more than the cost estimates on which FK90 based its recommendation

[460] The restructuring measures must take place as a function of the consideration of achieving the war structure, and the measures must be designed in accordance with the goal of protecting material investments

[461] This long-term report is therefore primarily a restructuring report, which aims to describe the changes in the framework conditions, assess the consequences these have for the structure that is necessary in the new era and in relation to the goal of maintaining an invasion defense, and finally point out the measures that are required to achieve this structure

[462] More about the assessment basis FK90's

[463] The report and recommendations form the basis for this long-term report

[464] The majority of the commission agreed on a wartime structure that involves a significant reduction of the current structure, especially for the Army

[465] According to the same majority, this constitutes a minimum structure for Norway to be able to maintain a time-limited invasion defense limited to one part of the country

[466] International developments so far do not provide grounds for departing from Norway's current defense concept

[467] The defense concept is based on binding cooperation within NATO

[468] It is the quality of what Norway itself provides that provides real opportunities for reinforcements in times of crisis and war

[469] Norwegian authorities have placed great emphasis on maintaining Norway's reinforcement commitments to the country's most important partners in NATO

[470] The credibility of this argument would be greatly weakened if we, from the Norwegian side, were to downgrade the Armed Forces so that it is no longer sufficient to maintain the ambition of a time-limited invasion defense in a region of the country

[471] For Norway, there is no realistic alternative to American reinforcements

[472] A Norwegian defense that still has the ability to repel an invasion attempt will not least be important in relation to burden sharing between the United States and the country's European allies

[473] Norway's own efforts must be seen, among other things, in light of a reduced American involvement in the defense of Europe

[474] Many NATO countries are reducing their military forces to a greater extent than Norway, but these countries are in a different situation both in terms of security policy and purely in terms of defense

[475] The Norwegian land area is large and the population small

[476] Furthermore, the Norwegian sea areas are among the largest in the world under national authority

[477] The Norwegian Armed Forces are tasked with defending Norwegian territory, while many of our allies have built up forces for deployment in other countries' territories

[478] This opens up the possibility of greater reductions in the new situation

[479] Norway does not allow the stationing of allied forces, and relies on general conscription and a mobilization defense

[480] This places demands on the scope of the Norwegian equipment fleet, demands that are resource-intensive

[481] Economic framework, desired force structure and cost-saving measures Based on the needs for restructuring the Armed Forces, the size and growth of defense budgets are in focus for several reasons

[482] A certain size of defense budgets is required to maintain an operational organization

[483] In addition, significant amounts must be invested in order to have a fully equipped war organization

[484] The defense structure that can be realized in Norway is critically dependent on how much funding can be allocated for investments in new equipment

[485] The funds must either come from operational reductions or from growth in budgets

[486] Since the Government's financial framework for the planning period as a whole is expected to be somewhat below the Commission majority's framework, the necessary funds must come to an even greater extent from operating savings

[487] The budget framework for the planning period assumes a scaling down of the Armed Forces' activities in favor of new investments

[488] This will have consequences for exercise patterns and exercise frequency, among other things

[489] Tight budget constraints will make it even more necessary to increase the differentiation of the training pattern

[490] The level of training during the initial service is sought to be maintained at the current level

[491] For personnel in the lowest priority departments and units, however, training and education beyond initial service will be part of any possible mobilization

[492] Rehearsal exercises will not be held for these

[493] Instead, a training period is assumed in connection with a possible mobilization in which this personnel is made operational

[494] The competence of such departments' staff and management elements is assumed to be maintained at a sufficient level through simulation exercises

[495] For other departments and units, the exercise pattern and frequency will be determined by requirements for Norwegian participation in multinational operations and forces

[496] The future financial framework for the Armed Forces must also take into account the need for and desire for increased participation in peacekeeping activities not only in NATO, but also under the UN and in the CSCE context

[497] In this light, there will be a development in which the Armed Forces will be increasingly characterized by the fact that certain standing departments and units will have to receive a high standard of training, with the competence to participate in joint military operations abroad at very short notice

[498] Parts of the purely national defense, including some of the mobilization defense units and departments, will not have the same continuously high level of competence and training

[499] However, these will be able to achieve this through an intensive training period after mobilization, during the longer warning period that must now be assumed to precede a possible major conflict in Europe

[500] The report addresses these issues for further consideration

[501] A changed threat landscape; the absence of clear threats and the emergence of new challenges, has extended the warning period and made it possible to reduce preparedness

[502] As long as this is the situation, a gradual adaptation of the Armed Forces' peacekeeping organization and activities can be implemented, with the savings potential this provides

[503] The number of brigades in the Army will quickly be reduced to six

[504] until approximately the year

[505] Regardless of the final structural goals and in order to safeguard the potential for reconstruction that has been created through previous investments in materiel and training, the brigades will be maintained as long as they are believed to provide a certain combat capability

[506] The costs of maintaining this combat capability must be continuously weighed against the consequences for the rest of the structure

[507] It is assumed that the equipment for these departments can be stored in such a way that the operating costs associated with them are minimized

[508] The departments will be discontinued as the basis for them ceases to exist

[509] Norway's UN involvement is a high priority area, which will have to burden the defense budget

[510] Taken together, this means that the Armed Forces will face a very large challenge in implementing the defense structure recommended by the majority of the Commission, even with the financial framework that this majority based on

[511] The commission itself assumed that the recommended war structure could only be realized in the period

[512] The Government's long-term goal is to realize the same war structure, even with somewhat lower resource availability in the coming years than the Commission majority assumed

[513] This is done by means of a budgetary escalation throughout the planning period in recognition that the international framework conditions in the near future may allow for some reduction in peacetime activities

[514] The Government will, however, closely monitor international developments and assess the security challenges Norway is currently facing

[515] The Armed Forces will take on new civilian tasks

[520] In accordance with the Government's general employment policy, personnel reductions will be implemented as far as possible without layoffs

[522] This structure will at this point have only to a lesser extent achieved the quality requirements

[523] The commission majority assumed for its recommended war structure

[524] The long-term report places great emphasis on ensuring real flexibility and freedom of action in defense planning

[525] This means that the Armed Forces must be able to handle minor deviations in the annual budgets without losing sight of the long-term structural goals

[526] The government, like the Defence Commission, allows the structure to determine the development of the Armed Forces

[527] The Government's budget proposal will maintain the necessary freedom of action so that the Government and the Storting can decide during the period 1995-98 on what level of ambition, with associated tasks and defence concept, should be the basis for the long-term design of the war structure

[529] During this period, major investment decisions will have to be made to realize the planned structure

[532] Crucial emphasis is placed on the fact that the proposed force structure is assumed to be close to a lower threshold for Norway to be able to maintain a balanced national invasion defense in a region of the country

[533] The long-term report states that a functional Total Defence is a prerequisite for society to be able to quickly adjust from a peacetime to a wartime situation

[534] A main element of the total defense concept is to exempt the Armed Forces from investments in materiel and services that can be obtained from civilian sources, through planned utilization of society's total resources

[535] This civilian support for military defense makes it possible for the Armed Forces to concentrate the use of resources for purely military purposes

[536] This also places demands on interoperability capacity between computer-based decision support systems as they are put into use in important parts of the total defense

[537] Without access to civilian resources, the Armed Forces' material investment needs would have increased significantly, or alternatively, the Armed Forces' structure and tasks would have to be reduced significantly compared to the current situation

[538] The government states in the report that there is no credible alternative for Norway to the total defense concept

[539] This will therefore be continued

[540] THE MILITARY STRUCTURE OF THE DEFENCE

[541] In the report, the government proposes that the Norwegian Armed Forces' war structure be developed in accordance with the Defence Commission's recommendations

[542] This involves a continuation of the anti-invasion capacity in the highest priority parts of the country, combined with the ability to repel violations at a lower level than invasion in the other parts of the country

[543] However, the structure is not tied to specific parts of the country in a way that prevents the Armed Forces from being redeployed, should political developments in the longer term warrant this

[544] Such a reallocation, even of the most local departments and resources, could be implemented more quickly than would be the case for the significant political upheavals that would be required for such a reallocation to become relevant

[545] At the end of the period, the most important structural elements will be

[546] division, 3 brigades and divisional troops (0 in 1992), 3 independent brigades, 12 submarines

[547] coastal artillery batteries 12 missile batteries 5 escort vessels 65 combat aircraft 4 maritime patrol aircraft 6 large transport aircraft 6 air defense missile batteries, medium altitude 10 air defense missile batteries, low altitude 10 air defense gun batteries

[548] In addition, there are various units that will handle peacekeeping tasks, territorial departments, support functions in all branches of defense, etc

[549] Div 6/TLF is currently a separate divisional command that is expected to lead a number of brigades

[550] The actual structure within the proposed division in the year 2000 will, however, be somewhat different

[551] The division concept for the year 2000 will be an integrated division with its own divisional troops, in contrast to the current division, which is only a command element for a number of independent brigades

[552] Compared to the current structure, this implies a strong quantitative reduction, especially of the Army

[553] Such a reduction is nevertheless absolutely necessary if the material investments on which the structure depends to be credible are to be implemented

[554] The degree of modernization will be moderate, and largely based on existing material types and technology

[555] Where material contracts have already been entered into that do not correspond to the needs according to the structure currently being planned, the Ministry will consider renegotiating the contracts if this can result in savings

[556] In line with Norwegian participation in NATO's response forces, which can also be made available for operations under the auspices of and pursuant to a mandate from the UN or the CSCE, personnel and material requirements associated with these forces could be resource-intensive

[557] Participation in the forces will also be crucial for Norway's ability to provide reinforcements in a crisis situation

[558] Norwegian units and departments in such forces will also be valuable as managers of professional expertise in the defense branches, as reduced activity makes it impossible to maintain an equally high standard in all departments

[559] DEFENSE AND COMBAT CAPABILITY

[560] The report defines the terms defense capability and combat capability, which form the basis for assessing the extent to which the Armed Forces can fulfill their tasks and assigned role

[561] A clarification of what the Armed Forces' goals are must form the basis for determining what the Armed Forces will produce and for assessing whether the Armed Forces are prioritizing the use of resources correctly

[562] Once it has been determined what the Armed Forces will produce over a given period, management will need to be geared towards ensuring that production takes place as efficiently as possible

[563] This assumes that the value creation in the entire defense organization can be described, which, among other things, requires a clear distinction between defense and combat capability

[564] The end products are the benefits that society expects to receive from the Armed Forces, and for which the Storting allocates funds

[565] The definition of and distinction between defense capability and combat capability provides an opportunity to assess the connection between security policy developments and the Armed Forces' ability to perform its tasks

[566] The goal of Norwegian security policy is national security

[567] In a defense policy sense, this goal can be seen as a function of defense capability and the likelihood of war or the use of armed force

[568] In isolation, the Norwegian Armed Forces' combat capability will decline during the period, because the material quality improvement cannot compensate for the entire necessary quantitative reduction

[569] When the military development in Norway's immediate vicinity is taken into account, which among other things means that the threat of invasion against southern and central Norway has disappeared, there is still today a basis for characterizing the defense capability as satisfactory

[570] National security must be characterized as satisfactory, as an armed attack on Norway in the foreseeable future cannot be considered probable based on the political interests, needs and force dispositions of potential opponents

[571] However, developments in Russia are constantly changing, and the effects could be significant

[572] THE DEFENCE PEACEKEEPING ORGANIZATION AND ACTIVITIES

[573] The major changes in the war structure mean that the Armed Forces' peacekeeping organization must be adapted to the needs of the new structure

[574] This will involve the largest reorganization in the post-war period

[575] It has not been possible within the time frame of the report to conduct a complete investigation of the reorganization

[576] There will therefore still be aspects of the organization that are under assessment when the report is presented

[577] The peace organization will be designed for two tasks, respectively, production of the war structure and maintenance of operational and other activities in peacetime

[578] The following explains the planning assumptions that will be used

[579] Concrete proposals for reorganization will be submitted to the Storting as they are clarified

[580] Within the Army, the district command level will remain

[581] The district commands will have their tasks within the peace organization strengthened

[582] The number of district commands will be considered further

[583] All defense districts, land defense and reserve departments will be closed down and replaced by a number of territorial regiments that will primarily be responsible for operational planning and management of local defense

[584] Some of the territorial regiments will also be arms-specific competence centers where training within the individual arms is concentrated

[585] Where there are multiple centers of competence within the same territorial regiment's area, these will appear as separate regiments without territorial responsibility

[586] The Home Guard's future peacekeeping organization will be assessed during 1993 in light of the need for closer coordination, especially with the Army

[587] The Naval Districts, which are the Navy's regional organization, will be replaced by a smaller number of bases and stations with reduced tasks

[588] The operational responsibility of the districts is taken over by the defense commands directly, while the Navy's Supply Command centrally takes over the administrative responsibility

[589] Crew training will be rationalized and concentrated in fewer locations

[590] Conscripted personnel in the Coastal Artillery will receive continuous service at the same location

[591] The Air Force will reduce the number of established stations, and concentrate as much of the remaining operations as possible on three main air stations and two air stations

[592] This will apply to both flight operations and the training of air defense crews

[593] The Air Force has no regional organization, but the control and warning system will be rationalized through automation of the radar stations

[594] To reduce operating expenses and free up funds for materiel investment, the defense branches will transition to a base and garrison-oriented exercise pattern

[595] It is assumed that improved training methods, including better infrastructure in the training areas and the use of simulator technology, will be able to compensate for a reduced number of training and sailing days

[596] Under this, education during initial service will be prioritized, and the activity cuts will primarily be linked to the refresher exercises

[597] This means that the departments' dependence on a longer training period after mobilization increases, but this is considered an acceptable risk in the political situation that has arisen

[598] Joint exercises with allied reinforcement units will continue to have priority

[599] The Armed Forces will continue to conduct significant operational activities in peacetime, with emphasis on participation in NATO's multinational forces, UN operations, coast guard services, rescue services, and intelligence and early warning services

[600] The Ministry of Defence will ensure that development and planning within the defence sector takes environmental considerations into account so that existing environmental problems are reduced and new ones are prevented

[601] Environmental considerations must be incorporated into management systems, and the environmental function must be introduced into the organization

[602] ALTERNATIVE DEFENSE CONCEPTS

[603] In light of security policy and economic developments and the increasing cost of military technology, the Government considers it desirable to outline possible alternatives to the existing defense concept

[604] It is emphasized that these are assessments with a long-term perspective, and that the current concept of an invasion defense in the most vulnerable part of the country remains in place for the period covered by the report

[605] The requirements for an invasion defense are of course not absolute and unambiguous, as they will largely depend on the forces deployed in an attack

[606] The goal must be to raise the demands for effort to a level that is not in reasonable proportion to the expected gain and risk of failure

[607] If a national balanced invasion defense as a result of a deliber-ate development, or on the basis of economic necessity, were to be abandoned, there are in principle three alternative main strategies

[608] The defense can be organized as an invasion defense built on a risky assumption of large allied reinforcements

[609] The armed forces can be organized as a core defense force sized to fulfill peacekeeping tasks, combined with a cadre function for rebuilding a larger organization over a longer period

[610] The ambition of being able to fight off an invasion is abandoned in favor of a lower level of ambition and the structure is adapted to this

[611] The conditional invasion defense can consequently be structured in two ways, depending on whether the risk is placed in the assumption of reinforcements or in the assumption of a long time to regain strength

[612] For a defense with a lower level of ambition, several solutions can be considered, depending on what this level of ambition should be

[613] STRATEGY FOR THE CHANGE PROCESS

[614] General guidelines for developing the structure

[615] The Armed Forces are facing the largest restructuring process in the post-war period

[616] This is not limited to a simple reorganization, but also requires restructuring of basic procedures, abandoning traditional goals and considerations, and reprioritizing activities according to other criteria

[617] The overarching principle for the restructuring process is to ensure the greatest possible freedom of action by preserving as much of the Armed Forces' ability to adapt to changing political and economic framework conditions as possible

[618] This is made difficult, however, by the fact that the Armed Forces are believed to be close to a threshold situation in relation to the existing defense concept, which is linked to the ambition of invasion defense

[619] Failure in the availability of resources or in other assumptions regarding operational savings, cost developments, etc. may thus mean that the assumptions on which the structural objective is based cannot be met

[620] This could result in many of the investments and organizational measures that have already been implemented losing much of their justification

[621] Such freedom of action is nevertheless best achieved by protecting material investments and training a sufficient core of commanders and specialists

[622] In turn, this creates the basis for developing the organization's breadth in the direction that development makes necessary or appropriate

[623] Capital investments in the period should therefore be kept at approximately 30 billion 1992 NOK, and are expected to increase from the current approximately 24 percent to approximately 32 percent of the budget after the planning period

[624] This is a very high proportion by international standards, but only reflects that the Norwegian defense concept makes this necessary due to the very low proportion of standing forces

[625] However, capital investments should only be made in sectors that will last in the long term

[626] Both our own studies and analyses conducted abroad indicate that the most time-consuming part of any force reconstruction is the acquisition and phasing in of new equipment, especially if entire categories of technically and operationally advanced equipment have been phased out (fighter aircraft, submarines, tanks, etc

[627] Advanced military equipment has a very long procurement time

[628] Depending on complexity, it will take from 2 to 10 years to acquire such equipment

[629] If the international situation indicates that many countries will demand the same defense equipment, acquiring the necessary equipment may prove very difficult or impossible

[630] It will also take from 2 to 10 years to regain the technical and operational expertise required to use the equipment effectively

[631] The development of competent professional environments takes a very long time

[632] For some of the most complex organizations where technology and expertise must work together in an optimal way, recovery could take even longer

[633] This is considerably longer than the time required to train new crews in their functions, or to train mobilization departments to a credible standard

[634] In the development of the war structure, material procurement must therefore be protected, and any failure in resource access must be borne as far as possible by the operating budget

[635] Training the necessary number of specialists and commanders at all levels to create a certain cadre must then be ensured at the expense of training and refresher training of larger forces in Norwegian formations

[636] Strength recovery in the somewhat longer term (6-12 months) thus takes priority over the ability to mobilize in the very short term

[637] This is also in accordance with the security policy situation, which indicates that the probability of a major war is low

[638] In any case, the emergence of such a threat will require a long preparation period

[639] It is emphasized in this context that this is about force recovery within the framework of the existing defense concept, in contrast to the alternative core or cadre defense described in chapter

[640] This cadre defense requires a reconstruction of the Armed Forces over several years

[641] In the former case, it primarily concerns training an existing organization, in the latter, major organizational changes, training of new crews, etc

[642] The need to reduce operating costs dictates that equipment that will not be renewed in the long term is phased out as quickly as possible

[643] Utilization of older equipment may mean a lower investment share in a given period, but older equipment will also be more expensive to operate, including through increasing maintenance costs

[644] Maintenance of older equipment will also often result in different generations of weapons being used simultaneously within the same defense sector

[645] This can be costly, for example in the context of education and training

[646] At the same time, the Armed Forces will at all times have equipment that is far from technically worn out, even if it is operationally obsolete

[647] Such equipment can often be retained without major additional costs and used by departments with less demanding assignments

[648] It will therefore be essential to have an overall, coordinated and well-thought-out rotation and phasing-out plan for the equipment, especially the expensive main equipment items

[649] Reducing the Armed Forces' operating expenses is an absolute prerequisite for sufficient investment funds to be available to realize the structure

[650] The peace organization must therefore be reduced regardless of structural goals, because reduced operating expenses primarily require reduced use of personnel

[651] The restructuring should, to the greatest extent possible, take place by removing entire units and businesses from the structure, so that the number of garrisons and service locations can be significantly reduced

[652] This provides both the greatest savings and the best functionality in the remaining departments

[653] The organization shall, to the greatest extent possible, be developed to meet the need for the production of crews and units as dictated by the war structure

[654] In some contexts, however, the type and scope of permanent activities are determined by considerations of peacekeeping tasks, or by considerations of maintaining expertise

[655] This is particularly relevant where a specific activity is a prerequisite for national ability to assert sovereignty and manage crises, or for national control of allied operations on Norwegian territory in times of crisis and war

[656] Norway has joined NATO's new strategy and force structure, and Norwegian participation in NATO's multinational response forces is therefore a priority task

[657] Norwegian units earmarked for participation in the emergency response forces must, as a result, be developed and maintained in such a way that they satisfy the operational requirements set by the alliance

[658] Especially about personnel structure and personnel reductions

[659] Personnel reductions are the most important single measure for reducing operating expenses

[660] The goal is to reduce the Armed Forces' personnel consumption by the equivalent of 6,400 man-years over a ten-year period, of which 3,200 in the period

[661] At the same time, the activity must be structured in a way that triggers variable additions beyond the fixed salary costs to the lowest possible extent

[662] It is a prerequisite that the personnel reductions are carried out without layoffs as far as possible

[663] Natural and random attrition in combination with a reduction in the intake of military schools and the controlled recruitment of civilians will form the basis for the personnel reductions

[664] From an ideal perspective, it would be important to have an appropriate age and grade structure

[665] However, in a transitional phase, this will not be possible due to the consequences for budget funds for necessary investments

[666] A new equilibrium can therefore only be regained in the somewhat longer term

[667] The development of the Armed Forces' future personnel structure will be a difficult and complex process where different instruments must be used

[668] The revised command structure (RBO) will be reassessed

[669] As part of this, the Government is considering, among other things, submitting a proposal to abolish the right and obligation to obtain employment after graduation

[670] The goal is to find solutions that satisfy the Armed Forces' need for access to professional officers, maintain a high-quality military academy education and, in this context, secure the rights of the officer within the framework of the Civil Service Act

[671] A separate proposal regarding changes to the RBO will be submitted to the Storting

[672] Changes in initial service Initially, the need for conscripted personnel for military defense is governed by the size and scope of the war structure

[673] The best savings results could therefore be achieved by only calling up the number of conscripts for initial service that the war structure requires

[674] However, like FK90, the Government rejects such a solution, even though tight financial constraints dictate strict adaptation to existing needs

[675] As a matter of principle, all available conscript personnel should still be deployed after the session

[676] The government has nevertheless wanted to take into account the fact that there is a significant dropout rate during the first time service

[677] By emphasizing only calling up personnel for initial service who satisfy the requirements for the individual service function, as set out in the Armed Forces' requirements catalogue, the Armed Forces will avoid calling up personnel who, based on experience, are discharged at an early stage in their service

[678] Continuous service, where the individual conscript's service takes place in one and the same place throughout their initial service, has been considered, but is made difficult by several factors, including operational requirements and practical possibilities

[679] The regional priorities will continue to govern the disposition of the Armed Forces' forces in peacetime

[680] It is a prerequisite that the Army be able to train in brigade formations in the northern part of the country

[681] A significant military presence in Northern Norway therefore still requires the transfer of personnel from Southern Norway

[682] On this basis, continuous service will be implemented to the extent that it is practically possible and provides financial savings

[683] First-time service is one of the most cost-driving factors in the operating budget

[684] The differentiation of service time that has been adopted from 1 January 1994, and the distribution of personnel that is planned in this connection, is nevertheless insufficient to achieve the necessary savings

[685] The number of crews whose service hours are reduced must therefore be increased beyond this

[686] In the longer term, 12 months of service will only be maintained for those units that will be part of NATO's emergency response forces, for certain types of specialists and for other categories that must have 12 months of service for national emergency reasons

[687] Such a practice will also contribute to increasing the preparation time before the main part of the Armed Forces can be operational

[688] However, this must be seen in the context of the overall prioritization of materiel procurement and officer and specialist training, which is a direct consequence of which functions are most time-consuming in a force recovery process

[689] The first-aid service must be made more efficient and intensified

[690] Necessary educational goals should be achieved in a shorter time for several categories of personnel by facilitating the conditions for this and by removing some existing restrictions

[691] This will mean fewer leaves and longer days of service, which in isolation may conflict with the requirement for reductions in the commander's variable allowance

[692] The demands for programmed working hours will increase

[693] Other areas A sharp reduction in the Norwegian Armed Forces' war structure provides opportunities for significant operational savings

[694] The armed forces' command and control apparatus shall be simplified and reduced

[695] The national command apparatus will be adapted to NATO's new command structure and the new management concept with an emphasis on management by objectives and results

[696] The reduction in this command apparatus should be at least 25 percent

[697] To the extent appropriate, uniform management lines will be established for all aspects of the Armed Forces' activities, including force production, management and operational activities

[698] The two defense commands will retain responsibility for operational planning and operations, including major field service exercises with allied participation, while the Chief of Defense will manage a larger part of force production and management directly through the Inspectors General and the Supply Commands

[699] The costs of exercises and operational activities must be reduced considerably

[700] This makes it necessary to introduce a base and garrison-oriented exercise pattern, and a stronger differentiation of the exercise level

[701] However, there must be a balance between the level of activity and the length of service, so that a limited exercise activity is not distributed over a period of time that is so long that the intensity is perceived as too low

[702] This is a fundamental limitation of the conscription system

[703] The Home Guard currently has the highest training frequency of the mobilization defense departments

[704] This has been necessary so far, partly due to the uneven basic education and service background of the HV crews

[705] With a large proportion of crews trained directly for Home Guard tasks through 6 months of service in the Army, this problem will decrease

[706] At the same time, resource scarcity is forcing a reduction in HV's activity, which is in line with that of the defense branches

[707] The Home Guard's practice of annual exercises will therefore be assessed during the period

[708] Existing buildings should be utilized to the maximum extent possible by relocating operations and departments to where there is available capacity

[709] The reorganization of the Armed Forces will not be possible without a certain amount of new construction activity

[710] Construction projects will be prioritized in relation to their savings potential

[711] The costs of operating and maintaining buildings and facilities must be reduced by at least 25 percent

[712] until the year

[713] Despite the reduction in the war structure, the Armed Forces' material stockpile will not be reduced correspondingly during the period

[714] Expenditures for equipment maintenance and operation will nevertheless be reduced by approximately 25 percent by the year

[715] Primarily, this occurs through changes in exercise patterns and activity levels and through a transition to condition-based rather than periodic maintenance

[716] The Navy's transition to a base-oriented training pattern and condition-based maintenance has already contributed to reducing ongoing operating expenses

[717] The army's transition to container storage in a few locations will, compared to today's decentralized storage, mean significant savings, in addition to improved security, reduced costs for supervision, etc

[718] In addition, contingency plans will be reduced in line with reductions in the structure, and stockpiling independent of contingency will be managed according to rational economic principles

[719] At the same time, efforts will be made to reduce the costs of implementing material investments through better management of material projects, including by investing in a new project management system

[720] Consideration will be given to giving the Armed Forces the opportunity to generate revenue by competing in the civilian market with services on a commercial basis, e.g. with workshop capacity, etc

[721] This can help maintain an appropriately large support system for the Armed Forces' primary activities

[722] The prerequisite is that income-generating activities must be carried out in accordance with normal competitive requirements and conditions

[723] REORGANIZATION OF GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT OF RESOURCE USE

[724] New management concept for the Armed Forces

[725] The Government places great importance on ensuring that all government activities achieve better utilization of allocated resources and appropriations

[726] The Armed Forces are working on several measures as part of the follow-up to the Government's efficiency improvement program

[727] Chapter 10 explains the restructuring process that is underway and the management concept that the Armed Forces are based on
