[2533] The development of this program is taking place, among other things, in collaboration with allied countries, and one of the goals is to be able to counter threats of the type illustrated during the Gulf War, when a regional superpower with weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile technology could threaten other countries in its region

[2534] A growing number of countries are acquiring ballistic missile technology, and GPALS will be able to fulfill a necessary function for crisis management and the implementation of multinational peacekeeping and peacekeeping operations

[2535] The United States and Russia are discussing cooperation on such systems, and the Russians have expressed strong interest

[2536] From the Norwegian side, emphasis has been placed on avoiding the use of nuclear weapons and the deployment of weapons in space

[2537] Similarly, a modern air defense and area air protection will have a major impact on a country's ability to resist limited attacks or terrorist attacks

[2538] As a result of changes in the international situation, there has been a clear trend in recent years towards a reduced emphasis on nuclear weapons within the Euro-Atlantic security area

[2539] Defense arrangements in Europe will be characterized by nuclear weapons to a much lesser extent than before

[2540] Development here is characterized by nuclear disarmament and elimination

[2541] In other parts of the world, however, nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction may become increasingly important as a result of the spread of modern weapons technology to an increasing number of countries

[2542] The dissolution of the Soviet Union could also affect the likelihood of the spread of fissile material and knowledge about advanced weapons production

[2543] As strategic deterrents, the remaining nuclear weapons will retain their importance for the foreseeable future

[2544] In line with this shift, conventional weapons are becoming more important

[2545] This trend is reinforced by the major improvements in performance of advanced conventional weapons

[2546] A new international situation is creating other forms of use of weapons, and the performance of modern conventional weapons gives them a flexibility and impact that must be seen in close connection with the new conflict patterns that are emerging

[2547] The possibilities for the use of military force in a peacekeeping and peacemaking context must also be seen in close connection with the performance of such weapons

[2548] However, from a future perspective, the question may be raised whether the development of highly effective conventional means of warfare will also make conventional war a very difficult means of promoting one's own interests

[2549] The willingness to accept the great damage, loss and suffering that accompany a major war seems to be decreasing, although this depends on the country/region in question and the circumstances associated with the use of military force

[2550] At the same time, the possibilities for limited conflicts are increasing, often linked to ethnic conflicts, where modern weapons are unlikely to be used to the same extent

[2551] As long as the Norwegian defense is organized according to the goal of maintaining the ability to provide a credible invasion defense, limited to one part of the country at a time, the Defense Forces will have to be built up as regular units, trained for combat between regular units

[2552] Armed conflicts where groups with randomly assembled weapons and greater or lesser degrees of military training operate, and where regular combat is not conducted, as is the case in the Balkans, will represent different framework conditions for armed conflict, where the impact of modern weapons technology will be difficult to assess in advance

[2553] In such cases, it will be difficult to assess the extent to which the warring parties have access to modern equipment, and to what extent they can operate and utilize such equipment

[2554] The defense is built around future threats and challenges that are primarily based on combat in the form of broad-based operations with regular forces

[2555] These are operations of the same type as the Falklands and Gulf Wars, not a tangled conflict situation as characterized by the ongoing conflicts in the former Yugoslavia

[2556] If the likelihood of multinational forces being deployed in the latter category of conflicts increases, this will also have consequences for the significance of weapons technology developments in conflict and for the requirements placed on personnel in such forces

[2557] If increasing deployment of multinational forces is to appear politically and militarily possible and desirable, however, it is necessary that this type of force, with potential combat, police and peacekeeping tasks, has a technological level that makes them qualitatively superior to the groups of regular forces, militia and guerrillas they are to control in an area of deployment

[2558] Modern weapons with high precision can help reduce unintended damage to civilian targets

[2559] However, if the war escalates to also include such targets, the damage could be all the more extensive

[2560] In recent years, therefore, greater emphasis has been placed, particularly in the United States, on developing technology that can be used in so-called "non-lethal" weapons

[2561] These can be weapons that temporarily reduce humans' ability to wage war, or that selectively neutralize systems and functions that society or the military apparatus depend on for continued defensive combat

[2562] Technological level in the Norwegian Armed Forces

[2563] As the consequences of not possessing or mastering weapons and equipment with the necessary technological level could be significant, sufficiently high requirements must be set for the quality of equipment and personnel in the Norwegian defense

[2564] With limited national resources, sovereignty must be enforced over a large geographical area

[2565] The size of the area to be defended places certain minimum requirements on the scope of the defense structure

[2566] Keeping the entire defense force equipped with fully updated, modern equipment will be very costly

[2567] The balance between quality and quantity will therefore be a key issue in Norwegian defense planning in the years ahead

[2568] As long as the use of military force cannot be ruled out, the characteristics of the military forces that may be deployed against Norway will primarily determine what level of quality the Norwegian Armed Forces must strive to maintain, as a minimum

[2569] Such levels of that constitutes the lowest quality have been thoroughly assessed through the analyses that form the basis for FK90's recommendation

[2570] The consequences of not being able to reach these levels are also highlighted for all the main components of the Armed Forces

[2571] Receiving and cooperating with allied reinforcements also places demands on the technological level of the Armed Forces

[2572] Among other things, Norwegian forces must also be made capable of fighting in the dark

[2573] If Norway is unable to further develop the performance level of critical defense components in a way that balances the quality of the potential adversary's forces, there will be a great risk that a potential war will be lost in the very first opening phase

[2574] The possibilities for continued defensive struggle, even with support from allies, will thereby be greatly weakened

[2575] The consequences are most noticeable when it comes to air defense

[2576] Aircraft with inferior performance in terms of detection, weapons range, electronic protection and maneuverability will quickly be defeated by an opponent who must also be expected to be numerically superior

[2577] If the quality differences are significant, the air war could be lost and the main premises for continued defensive combat could change drastically in a negative direction within a short period of time

[2578] Area defense and effective air defense take on increased importance in this context and should also be developed further for Norway

[2579] The level of performance of the land forces in several fields is also critical to Norway's ability to stop and eventually defeat a modern invasion force

[2580] Decisive performance factors are the ability to concentrate artillery fire, anti-tank, protection and mobility, and not least combat command and logistics

[2581] If Norwegian land forces are too weak in one or more of these fields, there is a great risk that the forces will suffer heavy losses, be outmaneuvered and unable to carry out their primary military tasks

[2582] For the Navy, important quality requirements are related to the survivability and weapons effectiveness of the naval invasion defense, and to mine warfare and defense against submarines in connection with the protection of maritime transport

[2583] The consequences would be particularly critical if maritime transport security were to fail

[2584] Major losses and delays in the transport of reinforcements and supplies to Northern Norway will greatly complicate the defense of this part of the country, both in the opening phase and in the somewhat longer term

[2585] In naval warfare, modern submarines also represent a very flexible and significant force for a smaller country

[2586] The ability for integrated combat management is also crucial for the overall defense effort

[2587] The surveillance and warning systems at both operational and tactical levels must have the necessary detection capability against future combat targets and acceptable survivability

[2588] The communications systems must also have the necessary resilience against both physical and electronic countermeasures

[2589] Using modern computer technology, critical information for decision-making and combat management must be made available at the right time and in an appropriate manner

[2590] The requirement for quality applies not only to materials, but also to personnel

[2591] The training standard must be maintained through solid basic education and effective exercises at all levels

[2592] System simulators and integrated combat simulation must be used to the greatest extent possible as a supplement to field exercises and training using the equipment itself

[2593] This is necessary both to increase training efficiency and reduce exercise costs

[2594] It is also important that advanced equipment is designed to be as easy to operate and use as possible

[2595] However, some use of enlisted personnel may be necessary to get full benefit from the most demanding types of equipment

[2596] The general level of technological knowledge and expertise in Norway is high

[2597] Also within certain parts of the industry, the level of technological expertise is high in areas that are important to the Armed Forces

[2598] This should be utilized to develop, produce and support weapons and support systems in areas where Norwegian operational conditions impose special requirements, or when it can provide solutions that utilize the technology in a particularly cost-effective way for Norway

[2599] An overarching moral consideration that must be taken into account is that future Norwegian soldiers should know and have confidence that they are equipped and trained so that they have acceptable opportunities both to solve their tasks in a war and, not least, to survive

[2600] In the longer term, this is a crucial prerequisite for maintaining the will to defend and the fighting morale that will be necessary in war to defend our country

[2601] Norwegian research and materials development

[2602] Norway will always have to acquire a large part of its defense equipment from abroad

[2603] Norwegian industry has neither the capacity nor the necessary expertise to meet the needs in all fields

[2604] Norwegian needs are often so limited in quantity that deliveries only to Norwegian defense can hardly provide a basis for development and production at an acceptable price

[2605] This means that Norwegian research and materials development must be seen in an international context

[2606] The Government is of the opinion that Norway must continue to seek to maintain national defense technology expertise and an ability to produce certain categories of technologically high-quality military equipment

[2607] This will provide basic technological insight and a basis of experience to be able to understand and assess the consequences for Norwegian defense and security of technological development in general

[2608] Such insight is important for assessing Norway's situation from a strategic perspective and for shaping the Armed Forces in the long term

[2609] It is also a prerequisite for being able to act as a well-informed and strong buyer when purchasing equipment abroad

[2610] It is also a prerequisite for being able to make sensible choices and for being able to ensure the operation and maintenance of technologically advanced equipment

[2611] In relation to the Norwegian Armed Forces' special needs and the economic framework conditions that are expected to exist, national development and production may in some cases appear to be the best solution

[2612] Other countries' materiel is developed to meet needs that are often significantly different from those of Norway, and the level of ambition can often be significantly higher than what seems appropriate based on the financial framework for Norway's defense

[2613] A separate Norwegian development may therefore be justified by the fact that products that meet Norwegian operational needs are not available on the international market, or that it provides a product with a more appropriate ratio between performance and price

[2614] A review of the total costs for a number of our own material development projects shows that in most cases this has been less expensive than purchases abroad, especially if adaptation to Norwegian conditions would have been necessary

[2615] Development of a naval missile for use in coastal waters and a radio system to cover a broad spectrum of functions are good examples

[2616] In some particularly sensitive areas, consideration of one's own and other countries' needs for secrecy and protection of sensitive technology will make foreign procurement impossible or inappropriate

[2617] In addition to meeting the Armed Forces' needs for cost-effective procurement, our defense investments should, to the greatest extent possible, promote Norwegian industrial and technological development

[2618] Although the Armed Forces' domestic procurement will be very limited in scope compared to overall Norwegian industrial production, the consequences could be significant in some local communities and for specific parts of Norwegian industry

[2619] Own development and production of high-tech equipment for the Armed Forces contributes to raising the general level of expertise and to further developing the technologically advanced parts of the country's industry

[2620] Military missions in connection with multinational projects contribute to Norway's ability for international industrial cooperation also in the civilian sector

[2621] This is increasingly becoming an important consideration

[2622] For a more detailed assessment of the societal and business policy consequences for the Norwegian defence industry that restructuring and reductions in the activities and organisation of the Armed Forces may result in, see sections 11.3.5 and 11.3.6, especially section

[2623] Guidelines for the design of the Armed Forces

[2624] FOR DEFENSE ACTIVITIES

[2625] Overall goal for the Armed Forces

[2626] The overall goal of the Armed Forces is to secure Norwegian sovereignty, help give Norwegian authorities the necessary freedom of action, prevent war in our region and contribute to peaceful development in the world

[2627] Without a continued credible defense capability, Norway could contribute to creating insecurity and uncertainty, which in given future situations could encourage undesirable actions from other countries aimed at Norwegian security interests

[2628] Norway's defense should be able to contribute to stability and predictability in our part of the world

[2629] The disappearance of the threat from the east in its traditional form indicates that in the design of future Norwegian defense, greater emphasis should be placed on more general defense and security policy issues

[2630] A broad commitment to peace, détente and disarmament also includes other instruments

[2631] Future international stability and peace will depend on several factors, including how countries can collectively solve problems related to the environment, population growth, poverty, and ethnic, cultural, and religious contradictions

[2632] Although the international situation in many areas has developed in a favorable direction, there is still a continuing need to be able to ensure Norway's integrity and sovereignty by using military means, if necessary

[2633] Norway's security can only be maintained through international cooperation and in the context of alliances

[2634] It is important that the design of the future peace and war structure for the Armed Forces provides the necessary flexibility to enable tasks that are currently difficult or impossible to predict to be solved, among other things, with the help of the Armed Forces

[2635] Security and defense policy considerations are based to a significant extent on professional military assessments

[2636] This applies to ongoing defense planning and the field of arms control and disarmament

[2637] Requirements for participation in, among other things, the verification process may prove to be resource-intensive, as new verification and inspection schemes are implemented as a result of new confidence- and security-building agreements

[2638] It is necessary for the Armed Forces to maintain expertise in this field

[2639] To achieve the overall goal for the Armed Forces, the design of the Armed Forces' organization and activities must be linked to four main goals, each with underlying sub-goals

[2640] Main objective 1 and underlying sub-objectives

[2641] As the first main goal, the current security and defense policy must be based on dialogue, cooperation and the ability for collective defense

[2642] In other words, the Armed Forces must be able to contribute to linking Norwegian security interests to the corresponding interests of other countries, and this work must be based on dialogue and cooperation, including militarily

[2643] As a sub-goal to achieving this main goal, firstly, the security policy situation, including the military challenges, must be continuously assessed

[2644] Secondly, a defense policy must be pursued and resources must be used to secure the country's situation

[2645] Thirdly, cooperation must be established with allies who draw up lines for mutual defense assistance

[2646] The fourth sub-goal in this context is an effective emergency preparedness system and crisis management apparatus, and the fifth consists of participation in the work on agreed disarmament and arms control

[2647] Main objective 2 and underlying

[2648] As a second main goal, Norwegian sovereignty must be asserted by military means

[2649] As a first sub-goal to achieving this main goal, any military threat, violation of Norwegian sovereignty and occupation of Norwegian territory must be met with sufficient military forces

[2650] Secondly, the national forces must be credible in terms of mobilization capacity

[2651] A third sub-goal will be that allied forces can be used effectively, and a fourth that military surveillance should take place in accordance with the security policy and military situation

[2652] Fifth, the main goal is to be achieved by providing the best possible insight into and understanding of Norwegian defense and security policy and Norwegian defense among the population and the general public

[2653] The sixth and final sub-goal in this context is ensuring an effective total defense in which military defense is coordinated with civil preparedness

[2654] Main objective and underlying

[2655] Sub-goal International security and defense obligations must be able to be complied with and fulfilled militarily

[2656] The first sub-goal is that Norwegian interests in achieving this must be safeguarded within NATO, the UN and other multinational cooperation

[2657] Secondly, suitable personnel and equipment must be able to be deployed in international missions and operations for the UN and other international forums or organizations

[2658] Thirdly, concluded disarmament and arms control agreements must be implemented and complied with

[2659] Main objective 4 and underlying sub-objectives

[2660] The Armed Forces must be able to provide support for priority tasks in civil society

[2661] To achieve this last main goal, the Armed Forces' resources must first be made available for national exercise of authority and resource jurisdiction, secondly, the Armed Forces' resources must be deployed in public rescue services and disaster relief, and as a third sub-goal, the Armed Forces must be able to provide support for other tasks in society where this is compatible with the Armed Forces' other goals

[2662] Emphasis must be placed on removing and limiting environmental pollution resulting from military activities, and combating such destruction that would reduce the quality of life in our society and increase the risks of international conflicts

[2663] The Coast Guard Service will continue to be an integral part of the Armed Forces' peacetime activities

[2664] Resource jurisdiction in the form of a separate coast guard is not in itself a purely military matter, but the Armed Forces' expertise and resources mean that this falls naturally within the Armed Forces' areas of responsibility

[2665] The Armed Forces already have a well-developed rescue capacity that will be continued

[2666] In a number of fields, the Government considers it both desirable and natural for the Armed Forces to provide support to civil society where this is in harmony with the Armed Forces' primary obligations

[2667] Such activities will give the Armed Forces a greater contact surface with the rest of society, and make the organization visible in a positive way

[2668] From a socio-economic perspective, such utilization of the Armed Forces' large organization contributes to better utilization of the country's overall resources

[2669] To achieve the aforementioned goals, the Armed Forces, within the framework of the Total Defence and a binding Western defence cooperation, shall be able to carry out the following functions

[2670] Invasion defense In order to establish a real war situation as soon as possible and to provide time for our own and allied force buildup, the Armed Forces must be able to immediately provide military resistance in areas where Norway is attacked

[2671] However, the ability to defend against invasion will be limited to one part of the country at a time

[2672] The goal of the battle is to stop the attack as quickly as possible

[2673] If this is not successful, the battle should be fought in such a way that Norwegian forces alone or together with allies can bring the situation under control so that lost territory can be regained

[2674] Necessary reinforcements and their securing are essential elements of an effective invasion defense that must be able to function as intended over time

[2675] An effective defense will still have to consist of a combination of the land military presence in peacetime, homeland security, locally mobilizable army divisions, rapidly deployable units, and naval and air forces

[2676] The task of conducting an effective invasion defense will, to a greater extent than other tasks, have a guiding effect on the future defense structure

[2677] It is of course not possible to precisely quantify the requirements for an invasion defense, as it will depend to a certain extent on the scope and composition of the forces deployed against our defense forces

[2678] This is not about absolute requirements, so that one can say that one has or does not have an invasion defense

[2679] The defender can raise the threshold for the effort required to be put into an invasion attempt to an unacceptable level

[2680] What is unacceptable to the attacker, however, is also not possible to estimate in general, as it will depend on the overall situation and the forces that can be made available for the operation

[2681] However, there are also lower thresholds that are determined by the extent and nature of the defended area, and the requirements for the type of forces that are assembled to be able to repel an invasion attempt

[2682] The extensive analyses that have been carried out are based on sober and not worst-case assumptions

[2683] Intelligence, surveillance, warning and security services Intelligence activities contribute to the basis for shaping foreign, security and defense policy in both the short and long term

[2684] The intelligence service and a well-developed surveillance capacity are important prerequisites for correct incident and crisis management, and should be able to provide strategic warning of a possible attack on the country

[2685] Intelligence also contributes to the necessary basis for long-term planning of the Armed Forces

[2686] A well-developed Norwegian intelligence service is a contribution to NATO's collective defense and also gives Norway the necessary expertise to be able to cooperate effectively with the country's allies

[2687] An appropriate security service is a necessary part of adequate preparedness and total defense

[2688] Military presence and assertion of sovereignty Military presence forms the basis for assertion of sovereignty, effective handling of incidents and contributes to information about other states' military activities in areas where Norway has interests to safeguard

[2689] This requires that, in peacetime, the Norwegian side has operationally ready units in all branches of defense of a scale that enables sufficient presence in and surveillance of the Norwegian area of interest

[2690] This also applies to the exercise of authority in areas under Norwegian jurisdiction in the form of control and supervision of activities on the continental shelf and in the economic zones

[2691] Crisis management and rejection of violations Norway must have the ability to quickly reject deliberate violations

[2692] Crisis management is often a question of military presence and contact between the parties' units; it is also a question of communication between political authorities and military staffs

[2693] In the event of any attempts to influence Norwegian governing bodies to make decisions that are perceived to be contrary to the country's interests, it is necessary to emphasize that Norway will defend its territory and sovereignty

[2694] To achieve this, the Armed Forces must, in peacetime, have units with the ability to isolate a conflict by quickly concentrating an appropriate military capacity in the areas where violations may occur

[2695] Preparedness and national reinforcements

[2696] Northern Norway will also be the most militarily exposed part of the country for the foreseeable future

[2697] The military presence should be of such a size that a potential adversary must carry out a force buildup before offensive operations can be launched with any degree of probability of reaching crucial areas

[2698] This can give Norwegian authorities the time needed to consult Norway's allies through NATO and bilaterally, and make decisions on raising the alert level, mobilizing and transferring forces to meet a more comprehensive threat

[2699] In a crisis situation, the need for forces for the defense of Northern Norway could exceed the military presence in peacetime and the locally mobilizable combat forces

[2700] There could also be a large need for resupply from Southern Norway to Northern Norway, for both civilian and military use

[2701] A sustained defense in Northern Norway depends on supplies and reinforcements being able to be supplied from and through Central Norway

[2702] The ability to secure supply lines, especially across the sea - between Northern Norway and Southern Norway - will therefore be of crucial importance for the defense struggle

[2703] Future defense planning should take into account that the forces that are initially intended to be stationed in Northern Norway will still need to be able to be transferred to Southern Norway

[2704] There is also a need for a military presence in peacetime in Southern Norway

[2705] Although it is likely possible to plan for a longer notice period than previously, it is still important that mobilization departments have a training standard that allows them to complete missions very quickly after deployment, if necessary

[2706] The defense must therefore have the ability to secure important infrastructure in all parts of the country and, if necessary, be able to reduce the risk of sabotage of installations in the North Sea

[2707] Cooperation with Allied reinforcements

[2708] A Norwegian defense force must be able to stop a first invasion attempt on its own

[2709] Maintaining a balanced defense with invasion defense capabilities in a region of the country will ensure this

[2710] However, such a defense alone will not be able to maintain control for long under sustained pressure

[2711] Norway will therefore not be able to establish a defense that can single-handedly stop a comprehensive military attack from a great power over a long period of time

[2712] Against this background, allied reinforcements constitute a significant strengthening of defense capabilities, but also place clear demands on Norwegian military competence, training level and infrastructure

[2713] To operate effectively, allied air forces require a comprehensive and modern infrastructure with well-developed and well-defended airfields capable of withstanding the effects of enemy air attacks, and a modern command and control system

[2714] The reception and deployment of allied combat forces, especially armies, is a comprehensive operation and requires regular training activities in order to function according to the requirements

[2715] Allied naval forces make an important contribution to the defense of Norway

[2716] In order to coordinate the allied effort effectively, a well-developed and well-adapted command system is required

[2717] In connection with the changes in NATO's command structure, the Ministry will conduct a thorough assessment of how the Norwegian command structure should be adapted to a new reality and new needs

[2718] A reorganization of the command and control apparatus into a leaner and more adapted structure will, in addition to operational savings, also provide better utilization of limited resources and will have a major impact on Norway's ability to cooperate with the country's allies

[2719] Assistance in the exercise of authority in areas under Norwegian jurisdiction Norway's economic zone encompasses large areas of sea

[2720] In addition, Norway has special jurisdictional responsibility for the fish protection zone at Svalbard and the fishing zone at Jan Mayen

[2721] Oil and gas extraction is an important industry and there is reasonable reason to expect growing international interest in the northern sea areas, which suggests that Norway should possess significant monitoring and control capacity

[2722] Professional military advice in connection with the formulation of Norwegian defense and security policy

[2723] Security and defense policy considerations are based to a significant extent on professional military assessments

[2724] This applies to both ongoing defense planning and disarmament, arms control and verification/inspection

[2725] The Armed Forces must therefore have the expertise and capacity to provide the political authorities with ongoing advice and information on such issues

[2726] Participation in NATO's joint response forces The general détente and disarmament in Europe has led to a reduction in force levels

[2727] Some of the remaining combat forces in NATO countries will be organized into immediate response forces and rapid response forces

[2728] Norway will be one of the possible deployment areas

[2729] These forces will make a valuable contribution to the Alliance's collective defense, and can be utilized flexibly both as a tool for crisis management and in the defense of member countries

[2730] Norway will participate in the new emergency response forces in all branches of defense

[2731] This task could be of great importance for Norway's contribution to stability and security in Europe

[2732] Support for UN and possibly CSCE peacekeeping operations

[2733] Norway will still participate in UN peacekeeping operations

[2734] New tasks and possible deployment areas require that Norway, similar to our participation in NATO's emergency response forces, can provide units with a high material and educational standard

[2735] For Norway, it is important to contribute to ensuring that the UN can fulfill the function for which the organization is intended

[2736] The UN is increasingly involved in peacekeeping and peacemaking operations, including in Europe

[2737] If appropriate, Norwegian forces should also be able to participate in peacemaking and peacekeeping operations under the auspices of the CSCE

[2738] Protection of the environment and combating environmental disasters

[2739] In its operations, the Armed Forces shall emphasize contributing to sustainable development by avoiding pollution and unnecessary environmental impacts

[2740] The main goal is to prevent environmental damage, but the Armed Forces must also have the ability to quickly and effectively repair any damage it may cause

[2741] An important task for community security is to map, monitor and remove pollution and threats to the environment as a result of military activities

[2742] The Armed Forces must contribute to this work to the extent that it has suitable resources

[2743] Nuclear pollution in the northern seas is a particular threat to Norway

[2744] The Armed Forces must also maintain forces that can be deployed to combat acute environmental disasters in Norway and the international community under the auspices of the UN or the CSCE

[2745] As part of society's general environmental preparedness, the Armed Forces will be able to make a contribution

[2746] In this context, oil spill preparedness appears to be a relevant area where the Ministry believes that the Armed Forces should be able to take on greater tasks

[2747] Ensure implementation and compliance with entered into disarmament and verification agreements and arrangements

[2748] Requirements for participation in the verification and inspection schemes that are the result of agreements entered into may prove resource-intensive and require expanded professional expertise

[2749] The Armed Forces must establish sufficient and suitable capacity to ensure effective compliance with both the existing verification and inspection schemes, and the new schemes that may eventually be introduced

[2750] The Armed Forces' expertise in this context will be of great importance to Norway's ability to cooperate and collaborate with other countries and as a basis for further developing trust and common security

[2751] Participation in international military cooperation The Norwegian Armed Forces' international contact surface will be greatly expanded as a result of NATO's new strategy and force structure, the emergence of closer European defense cooperation and cooperation with the former Warsaw Pact countries

[2752] The Armed Forces must therefore actively participate in integrated military cooperation in NATO, military cooperation in WEU and military cooperation under the auspices of NACC in order to safeguard overall Norwegian security interests

[2753] Territorial defense As part of the efforts to maintain a military presence in all parts of the country, the Home Guard continues to be an important part of the Norwegian defense concept

[2754] The Home Guard makes the defense organization visible and helps to connect the Defense Forces more closely to the rest of society

[2755] The Army and the Home Guard will together have the task of ensuring adequate territorial defense, including against acts of sabotage and terrorism, against commando or terrorist attacks, raids, etc

[2756] Cooperation with civil society In a number of fields, it is both desirable and natural for the Armed Forces to provide support to civil society

[2757] Such activities give the Armed Forces a greater contact surface with the rest of society, make the organization visible in a favorable way, and contribute to better utilization of the country's overall resources

[2758] The Armed Forces already have a well-developed rescue capacity and this should be continued

[2759] FOR THE DESIGN OF

[2760] THE DEFENSE STRUCTURE The following guidelines will guide the development of the future Norwegian defense structure

[2761] Requirements for the war structure

[2762] When determining the future war structure, necessary consideration must be given to the demands of a modern combat environment

[2763] In this context, the Armed Forces' future war structure must be based on requirements for quality, mobility and protection

[2764] Technological development sets clear conditions for the qualitative level that regular military forces must meet in order to be able to carry out their assigned tasks

[2765] Experience from recent wars also has a certain validity for the requirements that must be placed on the war structure, see section

[2766] The design of the Norwegian Armed Forces' war structure should therefore be based on a focus on quality

[2767] An upgrade of the Armed Forces' equipment is necessary for the Armed Forces to fulfill its assigned function in relation to other countries' military capacity and military-technological level

[2768] It must be emphasized that the quality target is a soberly assessed minimum level in light of the expected technological development of other countries' defense

[2769] A gradual improvement in quality must be planned throughout the entire planning period, an improvement that must not least be continued

[2770] Significant parts of the Norwegian Armed Forces' war organization currently have equipment of such a low standard that the departments would not be able to carry out their tasks in a modern combat environment

[2771] This applies especially to some of the Army's brigades, but the other two branches of defense also contain some technologically obsolete equipment

[2772] The invasion defense capability will be linked to Northern Norway

[2773] In order to maintain a certain level of ability to defend the rest of the country against more limited operations against important individual targets and infrastructure, it is necessary to significantly reduce the quality requirements for the land forces in these areas

[2774] When it comes to air and naval forces in these areas, this will mainly be limited to infrastructure and support systems that cannot be moved in a crisis situation and which are crucial for building up an invasion defense in these parts of the country, partly by redeploying national weapons and partly by allied reinforcements

[2775] A balanced Norwegian defense

[2776] Throughout the post-war period, the Norwegian Armed Forces have been designed as a balanced defense in the sense that it contains most of the main components that are included in modern armed forces

[2777] The main components of the armed forces must be built up and developed so that they are in mutual balance

[2778] It has been considered important that Norway has defense systems with the technology, firepower, range and mobility that are necessary in relation to the weapons systems that a potential attacker could deploy

[2779] The principle of balanced defense is resource-demanding for a small country

[2780] Reductions in Western forces and unpredictability regarding further developments in Eastern Europe emphasize the need to maintain a balanced defense

[2781] A balanced force structure is, among other things, a prerequisite for the Norwegian Armed Forces to be able to cooperate with and lead allied reinforcements on Norwegian territory more easily and more credibly

[2782] Consequently, necessary expertise in the most important areas of a modern defence operation and organization has been sought to be maintained

[2783] Such expertise is necessary, among other things, to enable the Armed Forces to be quickly built up if the political authorities find that international developments make this necessary

[2784] The individual main elements of the defense structure have been coordinated in such a way that no gaps can arise in the overall structure that could be exploited by a potential adversary

[2785] However, the consequence when it comes to certain expensive weapons systems has been that the number of such systems today is relatively low

[2786] There are four main reasons for continuing a balanced defense

[2787] the necessity of being able to bear the brunt of the defense effort in the initial phase of a war, so that a potential adversary cannot exploit missing capacities in our own defense; - cooperation with and management of allied reinforcements; - maintenance and development of established expertise; - consideration of important peacetime tasks such as asserting sovereignty, surveillance and warning

[2788] Although Norway must be able to expect allied assistance if the need arises, it is both politically and militarily necessary that we be prepared to bear the main burden ourselves in an imagined initial defense conflict

[2789] A balanced defense represents greater effectiveness in that its combat capability appears greater than the sum of the combat value of each of the individual force components in itself

[2790] If entire sectors of Norway's defense structure are removed, gaps will arise in the total defense capability that a potential adversary could exploit

[2791] This could give the opponent decisive advantages even with a relatively limited effort

[2792] It is important to maintain and develop expertise across the majority of the professional military spectrum

[2793] If Norway were to lose any of the main components, the country's authorities would, after a relatively short time, no longer have a full overview of developments in this area, neither among Norway's allies nor among potential adversaries

[2794] The consequence could be that Norwegian authorities lose an important part of the decision-making basis both for assessing Norway's defense capability and for the further design of the country's defense

[2795] A balanced defense gives the professional military weight and has the organization necessary for the country's allies to consider it appropriate that command and control over allied units is exercised by Norwegian military authorities

[2796] This means that a balanced defense contributes significantly to ensuring the greatest possible Norwegian influence over the overall allied effort in the event of a crisis or war

[2797] When it comes to peacekeeping tasks, it is particularly the need for effective assertion of sovereignty and the ability to handle crises that dictate the necessity of balance in defense

[2798] This means that Norway must have military units that can handle situations at sea, in the air and on land with appropriate means

[2799] This way, we avoid being in a position where the country could be challenged in sectors where Norway lacks appropriate means of response

[2800] However, considerations of sovereignty assertion, surveillance and warning do not in themselves require a balanced defense, but maintaining such a defense will make it easier to solve these tasks together with the tasks assigned to the Armed Forces in general

[2801] A balanced defense is resource-demanding for Norway, and will be increasingly so as requirements for technological standards, education, training and management levels increase

[2802] Specialization and division of labor within NATO can, in certain sectors, provide greater defense capability with lower resource consumption

[2803] The advantages of such a division of tasks must nevertheless be weighed against the consequences that the reinforcements that are supposed to cover any gaps in the defense structure may arrive too late or not be adapted to needs

[2804] The capacity to provide its own forces with the necessary expertise in all main components of a modern defense can give Norway the desired freedom of action in crisis situations and critical periods when allied reinforcements are on the way

[2805] The changes in Western patterns of cooperation, unpredictability on the eastern side, and the possibility of a relapse into authoritarian forms of government in the east do not provide grounds for deviating from the principle of balanced defense in the current planning period

[2806] With increased integration and deepening of binding cooperation arrangements in Europe and the Atlantic area, an expanded division of labor may become necessary in the longer term to create security together in the most effective way possible

[2807] A broader assessment of how Norwegian security interests are best safeguarded indicates that Norway must have a balanced defense in the coming period

[2808] However, this places demands on both force structure, weapons systems, and level of education and training

[2809] The need for flexibility and freedom of action in defense planning

[2810] Due to the fundamental uncertainty that exists in the longer term, it is important to ensure flexibility and freedom of action in defense planning

[2811] The Ministry therefore places crucial importance on maintaining as many options as possible throughout the entire period

[2812] Planning under uncertainty and ongoing adaptations of the Armed Forces' activities and development to variable framework conditions will have to become a much stronger part of the Armed Forces' coordination and decision-making process

[2813] The defense must therefore be reduced in such a way that freedom of action and efficiency are maximized, both in terms of force recovery and possible alternative defense concepts as a result of a lower level of ambition in the future

[2814] Uncertain international developments and uncertain economic forecasts may make a lower level of ambition than an anti-invasion defense desirable or necessary

[2815] As a consequence of this strategy, decisions on heavy investment projects that have consequences for the force structure should be made as late as possible

[2816] However, the lack of decisions on reductions in the peacekeeping organization will reduce flexibility in relation to the realization of the Armed Forces' war structure

[2817] Decisions of direct importance for necessary reductions in the peace organization should therefore be made as early as possible

[2818] The need for mobility and the ability to transfer forces

[2819] In accordance with the above, the Norwegian Defence Force should be prepared to a greater extent than before to meet unforeseen challenges

[2820] Since a relatively large proportion of the combat forces should be concentrated in Northern Norway, it is necessary that these resources can be transferred and used in Southern Norway to the greatest extent possible if the security policy situation over time should warrant such a reallocation

[2821] The instability in Europe could, if it were to lead to significant changes or setbacks, make Southern Norway more vulnerable, even though the current situation does not make this likely

[2822] Naval and air forces are mobile and can be transferred to vulnerable parts of the country at short notice, should developments require it

[2823] Transferring army units and land military capabilities will require longer time and more extensive preparations

[2824] This logistics system particularly applies to the land military forces in Northern Norway

[2825] Should political, military and economic developments result in Norway becoming more dependent on allied reinforcements, this could affect flexibility

[2826] The Norwegian authorities' freedom of action in relation to the use of military forces, for example for crisis management purposes, could again be affected by this

[2827] Faced with unpredictability regarding military and political developments in Europe and in Norway's immediate vicinity, and the need to adapt Norwegian security and defense policy to changing international framework conditions, it is strongly desirable to build the greatest possible flexibility and mobility into the new defense structure

[2828] The need to enable the Armed Forces to solve tasks that cannot be predicted today requires a defense structure that is relatively more mobile and flexible than today's

[2829] It is therefore of great importance that the forces that are initially assumed to be deployed in Northern Norway are not unnecessarily structured so that they become too dependent on fixed installations or a specific topography in order to be able to carry out their missions

[2830] The military resources that are pre-positioned in Northern Norway should, to the greatest extent possible, be able to be transferred and used in Southern Norway if the security policy situation over time should warrant such a reallocation

[2831] Ability to recover strength

[2832] Given that the warning period has become longer as a result of international developments, the Ministry considers it, in accordance with the restructuring of NATO's strategy and force structure, to be more justifiable than previously to rely on force recovery

[2833] The ability to recover strength must be given crucial importance

[2834] This means that the force categories and weapons systems that take the longest to build up and make operational should be shielded from reductions

[2835] As long as the key components of the defense structure are maintained, this will contribute most significantly to the ability to recover forces

[2836] Should the international situation change so that Norwegian authorities deem it necessary to expand the Armed Forces, both the key components and the necessary and sufficient cadre positions must be maintained in such a way that the recovery of forces can be carried out quickly and in a targeted manner

[2837] The necessary training of personnel and equipment should be able to be carried out within 6-12 months

[2838] Such an ability to regain strength by increasing competence over a shorter period of time makes it prudent to reduce the level of exercise

[2839] This must be continuously assessed in relation to international developments

[2840] As a consequence of this, material investments and the competence to operate main weapon systems should be prioritized

[2841] It is emphasized in this context that this is about force recovery within the framework of the existing defense concept, in contrast to the alternative core or cadre defense described in chapter

[2842] This cadre defense requires a reconstruction of the Armed Forces over several years

[2843] In the former case, it primarily concerns training an existing organization, in the latter, major organizational changes, training of new crews, etc

[2844] Requirements for the peace organization The long-term goal must be a peace organization that is adapted and large enough at all times to be able to satisfy the needs of the war structure

[2845] The peacekeeping organization must be designed so that it can fulfill the assigned peacetime tasks, including asserting sovereignty, monitoring and warning

[2846] Peacekeeping operations must be adapted to these tasks, in addition to the needs that the achievement of the war structure imposes for the balance between peacekeeping operations and peacetime operations on the one hand and the necessary investments for establishing the war structure on the other

[2847] Reductions in the Armed Forces' peacekeeping organization must preferably take place through closures of entire units

[2848] Only then will the full effect of personnel reductions be achieved through reductions in construction and other operations

[2849] The goal is to create larger units through closures and mergers that provide a better basis for competence development and more rational operating units

[2850] Joint solutions should be sought to the greatest extent possible, and the principle of largest user should guide which branch of defense should organize the joint activities

[2851] Allied cooperation abroad and at home - participation in multinational forces

[2852] The design of the Armed Forces' organization and activities shall be based on the considerations that must be taken in order for the Armed Forces to be able to cooperate effectively and appropriately with allied forces, and thereby contribute to linking the defense of Norway to collective Western defense cooperation

[2853] For a more detailed assessment of allied cooperation, see sections 4.4.3 and

[2854] Crucial emphasis must be placed on Norway's ability to participate in NATO's multinational forces and Norway's ability to receive and support allied reinforcements

[2855] A significant portion of the standing Norwegian forces must be earmarked for participation in NATO's multinational response forces, which will also be able to operate under a mandate from and under the auspices of the UN and the CSCE

[2856] In particular, the proportion of ocean-going vessels in the Navy and combat aircraft in the Air Force may be high for the units to be decommissioned

[2857] In addition to the fact that significant Norwegian forces will be deployed in this way, stricter requirements will be placed on the personnel, their equipment, training and competence levels, partly because the units must be able to operate together with allied units in the emergency forces

[2858] Against this background, a more long-term trend is emerging regarding the development of the Armed Forces

[2859] On the one hand, territorial defense forces will continue in the same pattern as before

[2860] On the other hand, increasing emphasis will be placed on units and departments that will be able to participate in multinational forces, where somewhat different requirements and needs will be the basis

[2861] The Armed Forces' command and control apparatus

[2862] With a significant reduction in the Norwegian Armed Forces' war structure, especially for the Army, the Norwegian Armed Forces' command and control apparatus must be simplified and reduced and built up in accordance with the requirements of the new management concept

[2863] Norway's own command and control apparatus must also be adapted to NATO's command structure

[2864] The reduction in scope must be at least 25 percent, the number of levels must be as few as possible, and the management concept's requirement for uniform management lines for operational activities, force production and management must be given significant weight in the process

[2865] In order to have a functional, rational and effective future command and control apparatus, these issues must be seen in a defense context and not treated by defense branch

[2866] Support apparatus and assignments on a commercial basis

[2867] A larger support apparatus must be maintained than optimal utilization of the defense framework requires by freeing up support and common functions to allow them to take on assignments on a commercial basis and thereby finance a larger operation

[2868] Occupational defense and/or military defense

[2869] The conscription scheme helps to anchor the Armed Forces in society

[2870] The Armed Forces should reflect the society the organization serves

[2871] A close connection between the Armed Forces and the society of which the organization is an integral part should be continued

[2872] The conscription system contributes significantly to this

[2873] Only a conscription defense system makes it possible for Norway, through mobilization, to put on a war footing a defense force that is large enough to defend our vast country, including providing invasion defense in a region of the country

[2874] The conscription scheme also makes it possible to draw on the overall competence in society, thereby avoiding that competence in the Armed Forces becomes dependent on the economic cycle in connection with the Armed Forces' ability to compete for the best workforce

[2875] The conscription scheme is an important democratic measure that helps to anchor the Armed Forces in society

[2876] The conscription system therefore provides, in a broader perspective, the best defense arrangement for a country like Norway, where the Armed Forces' most important task is to defend its own territory

[2877] The challenge in the coming period is how a defense based on general conscription will be able to fulfill the functions and tasks

[2878] The defense is assigned and at the same time fulfills the requirements for quality development travels

[2879] The consideration that the future Norwegian defense should be able to operate credibly also in a modern combat environment makes it necessary, among other things, to place increased demands on the individual conscript

[2880] This can only be achieved by making the service more efficient in relation to the goals and tasks the Armed Forces must solve

[2881] However, the conscription system has its weaknesses, particularly with regard to education and training standards for conscripted officers and crews

[2882] Sufficient resources must therefore be allocated to reduce this weakness as far as possible

[2883] A conscription defense does not mean that the Norwegian defense is without an element of professional personnel

[2884] The professional element of officers, civilians and enlisted personnel constitutes an important proportion of great importance for the Armed Forces' peace related activities and ensures a necessary element of professional military knowledge and insight

[2885] This meets several needs, including those related to education and transition to higher readiness and full war effort

[2886] When designing the future defense structure, considerable emphasis will be placed on maintaining a sufficient proportion of conscripts

[2887] The professional component in our defense is greatest for the maintenance and operation of the most advanced weapons systems in the Navy and Air Force

[2888] Technological developments place increasing demands on education and training levels for both commanders and crews

[2889] A transition to professional defense would therefore have its advantages in terms of combat capability

[2890] A defense based on personnel employed for many years would mean that the forces would acquire long-term education and training

[2891] In this way, professional personnel could become well qualified to utilize high-quality and advanced materials and equipment in an efficient and professional manner

[2892] In a professional defense, the educational apparatus would be smaller and resources could flow to a greater extent to the combatant elements

[2893] But a professional defense would require large expenditures and would, within realistic financial limits, limit the scope of the Armed Forces to the extent that the country's basic defense needs could not be satisfactorily met

[2894] The country's size and special topography require that our defense must have a certain scope that can only be achieved through a mobilization defense based on general conscription

[2895] A professional defense will therefore still not be a realistic alternative to a Norwegian conscription defense

[2896] The recommended war structure also does not provide a basis for reassessing women's position in relation to the principle of universal military service

[2897] Women's access to service in the armed forces will therefore continue in accordance with current regulations

[2898] Future conscription and service pattern

[2899] Military conscription for personnel entering their first term of service is discussed in detail

[2900] As a result of the necessity to adapt the Armed Forces to new framework conditions, service time and service pattern have been changed for those subject to conscription

[2901] The restructuring, together with organizational adjustments, also contributes to reducing operating expenses

[2902] Basically, the need for conscripted personnel for military defense is governed by the size and scope of the war structure

[2903] The best savings results could therefore be achieved by only calling up the number of conscripts for initial service that the war structure requires

[2904] However, like the Defence Commission, the Government rejects such a solution, even though tight financial constraints dictate strict adaptation to existing needs

[2905] As a matter of principle, all available conscript personnel should still be deployed after the discharge

[2906] The Ministry has nevertheless wanted to take into account the fact that there is a significant dropout rate during the first-time service

[2907] A modern combat environment also demands more from the individual soldier

[2908] There is therefore a need to set strict and consistent requirements for physical and mental fitness

[2909] By emphasizing only calling up personnel for initial service who satisfy the requirements for the individual service function as set out in the Armed Forces' requirements catalogue, the Armed Forces will avoid calling up personnel who, based on experience, are discharged at an early stage of their service

[2910] The current service arrangement usually involves initial training and subsequent service being carried out in multiple locations

[2911] The Ministry has considered whether it would be more cost-effective to conduct the entire initial service at the same service location; so-called continuous service

[2912] Although several factors spoke in favor of such a scheme, the conclusion was that the scheme could not be fully realized

[2913] To a certain extent, such adaptation will be sought

[2914] A general change to such a service pattern would have major organizational consequences for the Armed Forces, including for the location of the peacekeeping organization

[2915] The factors that were found to speak in favor of such an arrangement included the fact that an integrated exercise pattern could be followed from the first to the last day with the benefits this would have for the individual conscript and the department

[2916] The scheme could also provide administrative and financial gains

[2917] Carrying out the entire initial service at the same place of service, preferably near the soldier's home, would, in addition to more integrated service training, also reduce welfare requirements

[2918] However, continuous service must be seen in the context of a number of other factors, including operational requirements and practical possibilities that make such an arrangement difficult

[2919] The regional prioritization will continue to govern the disposition of the Armed Forces' forces in peacetime

[2920] It is a prerequisite that the Army be able to train in brigade formations in the northern part of the country

[2921] A significant military presence in Northern Norway therefore still requires the transfer of personnel from Southern Norway

[2922] Other factors, including building conditions, also make it difficult to carry out continuous service for several conscripts

[2923] However, continuous service will be implemented to the extent practically possible

[2924] Throughout the post-war period, Norway has been based on a total defense concept

[2925] A credible Total Defence requires, as today, good planning and careful interaction between the responsible agencies and organisations

[2926] The individual level must be responsible for what takes place at the lower level, and the Armed Forces should actively participate in the work within the civilian part of the Total Defence

[2927] A functional Total Defence is a prerequisite for society to be able to quickly adjust from a peacetime to a wartime situation

[2928] A main element of the total defense concept is to exempt the Armed Forces from investments in materiel and services that can be obtained from civilian sources, through planned utilization of society's total resources

[2929] The Requisition Act of 1951 gives the Armed Forces extensive powers to requisition materiel and services from civilian society

[2930] This civilian support for military defense makes it possible for the Armed Forces to concentrate the use of resources for purely military purposes

[2931] The significance and scope of this requisition access can be illustrated in terms of materiel by the fact that over 30,000 vehicles, 600 vessels, nearly 100 helicopters, a similar number of small aircraft and, in addition, Norwegian scheduled aircraft have been pre-requisitioned and can be made available to the Armed Forces as needed

[2932] The same applies to, for example, workshop capacity

[2933] In addition, plans have been drawn up for the production of equipment for the Armed Forces in a crisis situation

[2934] Without access to these resources, the Armed Forces' material investment needs would have increased significantly, or alternatively, the Armed Forces' structure and tasks would have to be reduced significantly compared to the current situation

[2935] The Armed Forces depend on requisitions being carried out as planned in order for the necessary defense preparations and mobilization to proceed as planned

[2936] Structural changes in the business sector and in society at large, especially the changing settlement pattern, the centralization of retail trade and the closure of a number of businesses, have, however, reduced the Armed Forces' ability to rely on requisitioning civilian services and resources in a crisis situation

[2937] There will still be significant resources that can be utilized for military purposes

[2938] The civilian resources that the military defense utilizes primarily include provisions, oil and fuel, vehicles, land, sea and air transport capacity, ports and base facilities, establishments, hospitals, building and construction capacity, various consumer goods, medicines, telecommunications services, press and information services, and police and fire services

[2939] Improved communications and increased turnover rates have reduced inventories in retail and at the same time led to more centralized warehousing and longer transport lines

[2940] There is also specialization taking place across national borders, which is increasing Norway's dependence on imports, while at the same time, businesses and other activities that have traditionally strengthened total defense are being closed down

[2941] Likewise, changes in settlement patterns and thus natural changes and reductions in business activity have reduced the possibility of requisitions from civil society in several parts of the country

[2942] The basis for deliveries and services from civil society has therefore weakened in recent years, with the consequence that the Armed Forces themselves will have to build up stocks of warcritical material and supplies in peacetime to a much greater extent than before

[2943] This will require investments for which very limited funds have been allocated so far

[2944] However, there will be a clear objective that such stockpiling will be limited to what is absolutely necessary

[2945] At the same time, the Armed Forces must, to an even greater extent than before, consider its investments in a total defense context and, as far as possible, avoid investments in materiel that, if necessary, could be requisitioned from civilian society

[2946] This will in turn place new demands on the Armed Forces' exercises of both materiel and personnel, while an expanded use of civilian materiel for military purposes will lead to an increased need for adaptations of the materiel

[2947] The overall tasks of the Norwegian Defence Force also include special protective measures for the country's population, where, among others, the Civil Defence Force is assigned special tasks and functions

[2948] In the broadest sense, Total Defence therefore encompasses all essential societal functions, centrally as well as regionally and locally

[2949] Maintaining the will to defend and support for total defense in a time without clear fronts and threats requires greater understanding in civil society of necessary military dispositions and measures

[2950] Such understanding can best be achieved through greater transparency and better access to relevant information about the actual military situation in Norway's immediate vicinity and the main features of Norwegian defense planning

[2951] For Norway, there are no credible alternatives to the total defense concept

[2952] This concept will therefore be continued, and assumes that the country's combined resources will continue to contribute to the defense struggle

[2953] The military part of the Total Defence Force should be able to utilize a number of civilian resources to operate effectively and to save on procurement that the Defence Force would otherwise have to make

[2954] The Armed Forces will also continue to collaborate with other groups that work on issues of importance to the Armed Forces' activities

[2955] Cooperation with voluntary organizations, including within the framework of the Total Defense, will continue to be of great importance

[2956] The armed forces' war structure

[2957] The design of the war structure aims to ensure that the Armed Forces will be able to maintain the military functions that are stated in Chapter 1 throughout the period

[2958] The function that primarily becomes governing is the continuation of an invasion defense in the Troms/Ofoten area, as a consequence of the northern areas' proximity to a politically unstable major power

[2959] The main weapons in an antiinvasion structure will, however, also be those that are important for meeting challenges at a lower intensity level than invasion, and which thus ensure the Armed Forces the greatest possible flexibility in relation to a spectrum of challenges

[2960] The major political changes that have occurred in Europe since the previous long-term report was presented must nevertheless have certain consequences for the structure

[2961] It is therefore necessary to adjust the Norwegian Armed Forces' war structure in accordance with developments in the security policy area, especially with regard to changes in NATO's strategy and force structure

[2962] As the probability of a major European war decreases greatly, the tasks of the Armed Forces become less one-sidedly linked to the protection of Norwegian territory in such a conflict

[2963] Instead, the Armed Forces must increasingly be prepared for tasks related to safeguarding Norwegian security interests in general, through participation in multinational reaction and emergency forces for crisis management and peacemaking or peacekeeping operations

[2964] In traditional and purely national defense, operational and preparedness requirements will be subordinated to considerations of rational force production, based, among other things, on assumptions of longer reaction times than previously

[2965] However, in the case of units earmarked for NATO's response forces, the requirement for deployment readiness dictates that considerations of operational standards are prioritized over the function the units also have as force-producing elements, should a conflict arise between these considerations

[2966] When the principle of continuing an invasion defense is established, this will result in strict requirements for the quality of the war structure, primarily for material standards, but also for training standards

[2967] This standard is set by the international level in the area, and Norway can to a small extent rely on compensating for lower quality by exploiting other advantages, see chap

[2968] The military structure will therefore be modernized with a material quality that is considered marginally sufficient in relation to the demands that the combat environment will make

[2969] However, it must be strongly emphasized that the proposed modernization does not represent a transition to a high-tech defense

[2970] All the material proposed for introduction into the structure is thus based on technology that is already in use today

[2971] Several of the most important weapons systems will have to be based on the modernization of weapons and platforms designed in the 1960s

[2972] For example, the army will adopt an updated version of the Leopard tank at the same time as the same version is being phased out by our allies

[2973] However, even a sober modernization profile will require such large investments that the war structure must be reduced in scope

[2974] A completely similar development can also be observed in other European countries, not least in Sweden and Finland, which, like Norway, have defense systems dictated by small populations spread over large areas of land

[2975] This implies a reduction in the production apparatus, i.e. the peace organization, which in itself contributes to a better war structure by allowing funds to be transferred from operations to investment

[2976] However, the reductions affect the defense branches to varying degrees, for several reasons

[2977] The Air Force's fighter aircraft sector with necessary support systems will be maintained at the current level, even when the remaining F-16s are to be modernized and supplemented with a new fighter aircraft after the turn of the century

[2978] Such prioritization is related to the crucial importance that the battle for air supremacy over a main area of operations will have, especially in the opening phase of a conflict

[2979] This is not least important in view of our ability to secure the possibilities for the supply of allied reinforcements, which will be crucial for the ability to resist over time

[2980] A national combat air force is also a basic prerequisite for asserting sovereignty in one's own airspace in peace or during crises

[2981] It would obviously represent a completely unacceptable surrender of political sovereignty and freedom of action to have to depend on allied aircraft and allied operational leadership in order to be able to give graduated signals about Norwegian political intentions in such a situation - to the extent that this is at all practically possible

[2982] The Navy will have its invasion defense capability reduced in favor of maintaining its escort capacity, i.e. the ability to secure the lines of communication between Southern and Northern Norway and carry out the Navy's peacekeeping tasks

[2983] This priority follows from a reduced threat of sea invasion, combined with an undiminished need for escort capacity along the coast and the escort vessels' peacekeeping duties in the high seas in connection with the assertion of sovereignty, etc

[2984] In addition, there is the consideration of the Navy's significant participation in the alliance's multinational forces on the maritime side, which also requires this type of vessel

[2985] The army must therefore bear the greatest burden of the quantitative reductions, partly because it has already long been considerably larger than the available investment funds would indicate, and has therefore built up a significant material backlog

[2986] However, the land forces' dependence on other defense elements, especially their own air defense aircraft, means that a larger army would not necessarily provide a higher combat capability

[2987] The Home Guard's wartime structure will be maintained at its current level for the time being, pending a closer assessment of the future operational need for HV units

[2988] Although the Home Guard's primary task is to ensure mobilization and the transition from peace to war, the strong reduction of the Army in particular will not automatically imply a corresponding reduction of the HV

[2989] The importance of a nationwide, territorial element to protect critical installations and businesses against state-sponsored terrorism, sabotage and other low-intensity threats is increasing, and this calls for a nationwide and effective HV

[2990] The overall quantitative reduction in the Norwegian Armed Forces' war structure could have been captured as a more evenly distributed reduction across the country

[2991] However, with the current security policy and strategic developments, the Government has found it right and necessary to maintain a strong priority for Northern Norway in terms of initial allocation of resources

[2992] However, if political developments or other circumstances should indicate a different priority, the units can be redeployed within a period of time varying from a few days to 1-2 months

[2993] Political upheavals of the size required if the strategic picture is to change radically will in any case require considerably longer than this

[2994] The necessary freedom of action to reallocate defense resources, should developments require it, will therefore still be present
