[3001] Joint leadership and chain of command

[3002] The leadership of the Armed Forces consists of joint command levels (FO, FKN, FKS) and the regional command levels of the defense branches

[3003] It is a national requirement that allied units in Norway must be led by Norwegian officers in the allied chain of command

[3004] When building the chain of command, allied requirements, both in terms of size and organization and competence, will therefore govern structuring and resource requirements

[3005] Our national command and control apparatus will therefore be adapted to this, and our personnel will be given the opportunity to develop the necessary expertise

[3006] NATO's new command structure entails the establishment of a new allied command in Norway, Principal Subordinate Command North (PSC NORTH), located in Jåtta near Stavanger

[3007] The commander-in-chief of this command will be a Norwegian officer

[3008] PSC NORTH will carry out NATO's tasks within the command area in peace, crisis and war

[3009] As an integrated part of this command, FKS will carry out national tasks in southern Norway in peace

[3010] FKN will remain as a separate national command for Northern Norway, and upon transfer of command will be subordinate to PSC NORTH as Joint Task Force North Norway (JTFNOR

[3011] The current headquarters Allied Forces Northern Europe (AFNORTH

[3012] at Kolsås will be replaced by a new Major Subordinate Command (MSC) in High Wycombe west of London with the designation Allied Forces Northwest Europe (AFNORTHWEST), which will become the parent body of PSC NORTH upon transfer of command

[3013] As part of the rationalization of the Armed Forces' top leadership and the introduction of a unified management concept, the division of responsibilities between the Armed Forces High Command and the two defense commands will be revised

[3014] The resource allocation will be pooled and channeled through the four Inspectors General of the Norwegian Defence Force, who have executive responsibility for all peacetime force production

[3015] However, significant factors such as the need and possibilities for exercising command and control in the command area, distances, and topography within and between the regions mean that the aim is to retain two regional defense commands, one of which will also be the multinational PSC (Principal Subordinate Command) in NATO's chain of command

[3016] The defense commands thus become planning and management elements for major exercises and operations in peace and war, while all responsibility for force production and management is concentrated in the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces

[3017] Credible command chains require the maintenance of an adequate peacetime organization and wartime structure, adequate exercise and training activities, protected wartime headquarters, and necessary communications and information systems

[3018] Modern computer-based decision support systems are increasingly being used by allied forces that can reinforce Norway in crisis situations

[3019] The multinational NATO forces will also make extensive use of such systems

[3020] Particularly critical to our ability to lead such departments when deployed in Norway is the ability to interact with the departments' management apparatus through interoperable computer-based information systems

[3021] If this is not achieved, the consequence will be that Norway will not be able to lead allied units on Norwegian soil

[3022] A timely command, control and information system (CCI) will therefore be built and integrated into NATO's systems in accordance with the new command structure in the alliance

[3023] The Armed Forces will participate in and influence the allied forums that formulate strategies, guidelines and standards in the field

[3024] The Norwegian Defence Digital Network (FDN) will meet the needs for telephone, messaging and data services for all national and NATO users in Norway

[3025] A system for operational IT support for FKNO, FKS and prioritized parts of the Air Force's operational units will be in operation (NORCCIS I

[3026] This will be further expanded to cover land and sea operational functions (NORCCIS II

[3027] These systems will be integrated with NATO's systems in accordance with the new command structure in the alliance

[3028] Military operations require increasingly strong integration of troop types and defense branches

[3029] The Armed Forces will therefore place increasing emphasis on our war headquarters' ability to coordinate the management of units and weapons, including through increased emphasis on the joint operations component at the staff schools and a stronger focus on computer-assisted staff service exercises in the operational headquarters

[3238] The army will have essentially established its organization when the new division is introduced around the turn of the century

[3239] However, most of the major material investments needed to give the organization its anticipated impact will remain, and must be made in the following 10-12 years

[3240] In the Navy, replacement for the OSLO-class frigates will have to begin immediately

[3241] New escort vessels will eventually become the Navy's most extensive materiel project, and this investment will further the ability to protect supply lines

[3242] These vessels, in addition to the submarines, will be the only ocean-going units capable of effective crisis and incident management in the Norwegian area of interest

[3243] Finally, they will be responsible for asserting sovereignty, participating in multinational maritime forces and leading limited allied joint operations in Norwegian waters

[3244] The modernized KOBBEN class submarines must be phased out during the same period, and possibly replaced with 4 new submarines

[3245] In the Air Force, the F-5 aircraft will have to be phased out

[3246] Instead, a new fighter aircraft must be acquired in the air-to-air role, to supplement the modernized F-16 aircraft

[3247] This will be necessary to maintain a combat aircraft fleet that ensures the ability to continue control over a limited part of Norwegian airspace, especially with regard to the critical opening phase of a conflict

[3248] Equipment and supplies

[3249] The Armed Forces have for far too long sought to maintain a larger structure than has been adequately resourced

[3250] This applies especially to the Army

[3251] This has had the consequence that before the Army has had time to replenish all the material categories for 13 brigades, other material categories have fallen out

[3252] The army therefore never managed to fulfill its structural goals with the resources that were made available

[3253] There is therefore currently a significant imbalance in the structure of the Armed Forces, especially in the Army

[3254] This imbalance will have a binding effect on the renewal of the Armed Forces in the years to come

[3255] Development of materials

[3256] The imbalance within certain parts of the Armed Forces' material structure will, with the ongoing material projects and measured against the smaller structure for which investments will be made in the future, continue to increase in the coming years

[3257] This applies especially to the Army

[3258] This will have an impact on some ongoing contracts

[3259] The Ministry will therefore consider renegotiating certain contracts if it becomes clear that this equipment will not be included in a future structure, or where the Armed Forces already have enough equipment compared to the new structure

[3260] In the future allocation of resources, it is the future costs in relation to the utility that must be the decisive decision criterion

[3261] As an alternative to possibly terminating contracts, it may be appropriate to resell equipment that becomes redundant under a new structure

[3262] Development of the supply organization Competence and capacity in the supply organization must be adapted to the needs of the war structure

[3263] Participation in NATO's multinational forces will mean that the supply organization must also be adapted to meet the necessary supply responsibilities

[3264] While logistics is otherwise a national responsibility within the alliance, supplies for the IRF/RRF will also be a NATO matter in a coordination context

[3265] This means, among other things, that materiel and supplies earmarked for the Norwegian contingents earmarked for the reaction forces can be made available to the alliance

[3266] Accordingly, great emphasis will be placed on meeting the needs that exist for allied forces to be able to operate in support of and in cooperation with our national units

[3267] A balanced relationship between material structure, supply system and organization is planned

[3268] The Chief of Defence's Logistics Directive, which specifies the goals and status of stockpiles, is based on NATO and national goals for supply arrangements

[3269] The ongoing reduction in capacity within the national and international defense industry means that it will take longer to deliver critical materials and ammunition if one wishes to rebuild the structure or increase stockpiles

[3270] Specialization in business and centralization and increased rotation in retail have made our entire society more vulnerable to disruptions in supply lines

[3271] It will be identified which areas within total defense have the greatest significance in the context of preparedness

[3272] These factors will have an impact on which supply arrangements will be determined in the Chief of Defence's Logistics Directive

[3273] The level of ambition for supply arrangements will have a major impact on the combat endurance

[3274] The defense will have, and on the resource access that different levels of ambition will require

[3275] As a starting point, inventories of critical materiel components and ammunition in accordance with the changed war structure will not be increased beyond the current level of ambition, as the security policy risk associated with this is considered acceptable

[3276] Cost/benefit assessments based on the goal of optimal resource utilization in peace support such an assessment

[3277] Within the Army, there will be an emphasis on a more centralized storage concept based on container storage at the district command level

[3278] This will primarily reduce resource use in peacetime, but could be used to increase mobility and security in times of crisis or war, given sufficient reaction time

[3279] In the Navy, the reorganization planned for the Navy's regional organization will result in a more centralized supply service

[3280] The ability to secure the supply lines between Northern Norway and Southern Norway, especially the maritime lines, will be of crucial importance for a credible defense concept both for resupplying military forces and civilian society

[3281] This means that efforts will be made to exploit the opportunities offered by advance storage to improve the ability to receive allied aid and protect supply lines

[3282] Stationary defense facilities include forts, air stations, naval bases, advance stores, war headquarters, communications facilities, warning facilities, and fortified positions

[3283] Significant investments have been made in such facilities, and many of them are of high construction quality

[3284] Where possible, investments have been made through NATO's jointly funded infrastructure program

[3285] This applies especially to facilities in the Navy and Air Force

[3286] In a future structure, air bases, ports and supply facilities will continue to be of crucial importance if allied combat forces are to be deployed in Norway

[3287] There will also still be a need for the bulk of the other stationary facilities

[3288] Developments in weapons technology have meant that stationary facilities have become more vulnerable to precision-guided weapons

[3289] This must be countered either with greater mobility or better fortification protection

[3290] However, a number of tasks and functions can only be performed in stationary facilities, and the economic framework conditions will also limit the possibilities for choosing the most ideal fortification solutions

[3291] Based on the military challenges and future resource constraints, strict prioritization of financial resources for this purpose will have to take place

[3292] This indicates that the greatest possible flexibility and mobility must be built into the future war structure

[3293] At the same time, there will be clear financial limitations on which goals can be achieved

[3294] It is therefore planned to make the best use of existing good defense facilities, and to upgrade and supplement them to the extent that this is economically possible

[3295] Defense facilities that there is no room for in the new war structure will be closed down so as not to drain resources

[3296] This will essentially be a number of ex-German coastal artillery installations, some communications and radar installations and some older developed positions

[3297] Some unprotected radar stations will continue to be used for surveillance, due to their great importance in peacetime and crisis

[3298] Command and control points and communications installations are likely high-priority targets for an attacker

[3299] Existing war headquarters will therefore be improved as best as possible, and priority will be given to the protection of essential communications and data installations

[3300] Civilian communications resources shall be utilized in a contingency context to increase the network's capacity and flexibility

[3301] The final concept for the development of the coastal artillery's surface weapons is under assessment and will possibly be applied to the ex-German forts that are expected to be upgraded/renewed at the end of the period

[3302] All KA forts built after the war are expected to be retained and utilized in the future structure

[3303] Depending on NATO's objectives and financial possibilities, the warning chain and air stations will be renewed or upgraded

[3304] COMBATABILITY

[3305] Reference is made to section 4.1.1 for a more detailed definition of the terms combat capability and defense capability

[3306] All branches of defense will eventually have the qualitative part of their combat capability improved through the modernization that is being carried out

[3307] To varying degrees, however, this comes at the expense of quantity, and thus of the Armed Forces' ability to combat an invasion even in strategically less vulnerable areas

[3308] It must also be emphasized that the qualitative improvement requires large material investments, which will not be complete

[3309] before towards the year

[3310] As the quantitative reduction will largely be completed by the year 2000, this means that the Armed Forces' overall combat capability will initially decrease, before recovering somewhat

[3311] However, the individual department that remains in the structure will have its combat capability continuously increased, first by supplying usable equipment from departments that are being closed down, and then in the form of new equipment

[3312] The army will, once the new war structure has been established and the anticipated investments have been implemented, maintain a material standard at an almost international level

[3313] The infantry's combat capability is increased through significant motorization of tracked vehicles with over-snow capacity, and thus higher mobility

[3314] The infantry divisions' armor protection will also be strengthened

[3315] Quantitatively, however, the Infantry will see a very strong reduction as the number of battalions will be more than halved

[3316] The cavalry will gain a more unified tank force as Leopard tanks replace all older models currently in service

[3317] The army will then have 170 tanks, which is Norway's quota under the CFE agreement, but only about half of these will be upgraded to modern standards

[3318] The cavalry will also introduce new assault armored vehicles for the accompanying infantry in the armored battalions, to replace older equipment

[3319] The artillery will gradually phase out older shells from the US arms assistance program

[3320] Within a main operational area, the aim is to improve the overall combat capability of army divisions through a new concept for divisional operations

[3321] This means that brigades operating together in a division have their support and supply departments centralized under the division's command

[3322] This enables both rationalization and a greater ability for the division to make operational decisions by pooling resources in a prioritized direction

[3323] Further improvements would primarily be desirable through updating all Leopard tanks, strengthening air defense coverage at medium and higher altitudes, and improving armor protection through the introduction of a helicopter- or artillery-based anti-tank weapon

[3324] The army's anti-invasion capability in the prioritized area of operations will thus be strengthened

[3325] However, the improvement comes at the expense of similar capabilities in other parts of the country, where the operational brigades either disappear completely or are greatly reduced in number

[3326] Together with a sharp reduction in the number of local field battalions, this leads to a sharp decrease in the Army's territorial coverage

[3327] Another limitation on the combat capability of our army units will lie in the mobilization units' training standards, which will not increase significantly compared to current levels

[3328] This is because increasing the training frequency to an international level for reserve forces would require such large outputs that this in itself would have a devastating effect on the structure

[3329] Under the prevailing political circumstances, however, it is considered prudent to give high priority to the departments' material standards, as training of the departments will be able to be carried out during the longer escalation period that is now expected to precede a possible major conflict

[3330] However, it is a clear prerequisite for the deployment of mobilization army units that they have undergone intensive training in advance before being deployed into combat

[3331] This limitation in combat capability places strong constraints on the political choice of mobilization time

[3332] An assessment of how the Army's overall combat capability is developing therefore requires that the qualitative improvement be weighed against the quantitative reduction

[3333] This is not directly comparable, especially because the quantitative reduction occurs before the significant qualitative improvement

[3334] Even when the major material investments are completed, however, the land military coverage of Norwegian territory will be so greatly reduced that the Army in the proposed structure will have its combat capability weakened compared to the current level

[3335] The Home Guard's continued presence throughout the country will, due to

[3336] HV's weaker material set-up could not compensate for this

[3337] In the Navy, the reduction in the number of coastal artillery forts and missile torpedo boats will lead to a decline in combat capability in the anti-invasion sector

[3338] Remaining coastal artillery installations will be modernized and supplemented with mobile missile batteries to some extent be able to capture coverage of the inlets that will be without stationary coastal artillery

[3339] This must also be seen in the context of the greater vulnerability of stationary installations as a result of precision-guided weapons

[3340] Overall, however, the Navy's ability to establish an anti-invasion defense outside the highest priority region of the country is eroding

[3341] In this context, the maintenance of a submarine force with 10 vessels is considered critical to ensuring a certain residual combat capability in this sector, including through the submarines' ability to attack reinforcement and supply transports over time

[3342] Submarines also have a significant deterrent effect through their ability to create uncertainty and thereby make it difficult for an attacker to assess their own chances of success

[3343] The ability to protect one's own supply lines will, however, be improved as a result of new mine sweepers and deep mine hunting systems

[3344] These vessels also contribute indirectly to anti-invasion capability by enabling the naval transfer of allied reinforcements to Northern Norway

[3345] Combat capability lower down the threat spectrum is also maintained at the current level by continuing the ability to assert sovereignty in the high seas

[3346] Such capacity must be considered particularly important in relation to the growing economic interests now associated with the Barents region

[3347] The escort vessels also ensure the ability to participate in multinational maritime forces, and thus safeguard important Norwegian security interests

[3348] An assessment of how the Navy's overall combat capability is developing will have to be based on the assumption that a continuation and slight improvement of the escort sector occurs at the expense of a somewhat strong weakening of the anti-invasion sector

[3349] Overall, the reductions in the Coastal Artillery and the MTB fleet will be so great that the Navy's combat capability will be reduced, although the reduction is not as great as for the Army

[3350] In the Air Force, an attempt will be made to maintain the fighter sector at its current level through an update program for the F-16 aircraft

[3351] Together with the necessary improvements in support systems, such as air defense, control and warning systems, runway repair capacity, etc., this will provide a marginally sufficient combat capability in one main area of operations during the initial phase of a conflict

[3352] However, it is not possible to give as many air stations as desired a sufficient ability to survive and conduct fighter operations—thereby ensuring that air control is not lost because operational aircraft are confined to a few stations

[3353] A stronger development of several air stations would therefore provide greater security for both greater resilience in one area of operations and greater ability to meet a threat in several areas

[3354] The fighter jets are also a significant contribution to asserting sovereignty in Norwegian airspace, and thus to the possibility of avoiding doubts being raised about our will and ability to safeguard our own interests

[3355] Continuation of the maritime patrol aircraft sector maintains the ability to monitor the sea areas around Norway

[3356] This capacity must be seen in the context of the Navy's escort vessels, and maintains an ability for jurisdiction and sovereignty assertion significantly beyond the capacity of the Coast Guard

[3357] Overall, the Air Force's capacities in the various sectors will be maintained to a significant extent

[3358] However, there will be reductions in both the number of fighter aircraft and operational air stations, and this will weaken combat capability to some extent, until the planned acquisition of new fighter aircraft can begin after the turn of the century

[3359] The difficulties in assessing an aggregate combat capability for the individual branch of defense are further amplified by an assessment of how the Armed Forces' overall combat capability will develop over the period

[3360] The Norwegian Armed Forces as a whole will have its materiel quality increased so that the departments will still be able to carry out missions in a modern combat environment, but the quality improvement is still moderate in relation to the demands of the combat environment

[3361] In combination with the fact that the level of ambition must be lowered significantly in strategically less exposed parts of the country due to quantitative reductions, it therefore seems correct to characterize the Armed Forces' overall combat capability as decreasing as a new structure is realized

[3362] This reduction will be strongest in the period after the organizational reductions are completed and before the major material investment programs are completed

[3363] In addition to the supply of allied reinforcements, defensive capability also depends on the assumptions made about the opponent and scenario

[3364] The Armed Forces strive to maintain defense capabilities despite weakened combat capability by concentrating the remaining combat capability in the most vulnerable area

[3365] The combat capability of the Allied reinforcements that can be supplied to Norway will increase when NATO's new force structure is implemented

[3366] The deployment of, for example, IRF and parts of RRF in Norway will thus represent a somewhat stronger effort than the current reinforcement agreements imply

[3367] However, the uncertainty is related to the likelihood of receiving reinforcements when the system with dedicated departments is abolished

[3368] If the alliance's assumption about the regional nature of a possible new conflict holds true, this uncertainty must still be said to be acceptable

[3369] The conclusion is therefore that the combat capability of allied forces will be at least at the same level as today, taking into account their multiple deployment options

[3370] The combat capability of the forces that could be deployed against Northern Norway in a conflict is currently very difficult to assess

[3371] On the one hand, the Leningrad Military District, primarily the southern parts of the district, has become a current storage and transit area for some of the forces being withdrawn from Eastern Europe and the western military districts, as a consequence of the dissolution of the Soviet Union and the implementation of the CFE Treaty

[3372] This has led to a general improvement in the material quality of the forces in the military district

[3373] The support units and equipment transferred to the southern parts of the Leningrad Military District as a result of withdrawal from the Baltic states and other former Soviet republics are stated by the Russian side to be temporary dispositions

[3374] Equipment that is being stored will reportedly be destroyed as the ability for such destruction is expanded

[3375] When the number of main weapons is removed in accordance with the CFE Treaty, the ability to also carry out attacks against key areas in Northern Norway will be reduced, as a long preparation and reconstruction period would be required

[3376] The reduction of Russia's overall military forces will reduce the ability to transfer forces from other areas to the LEMD without weakening the ability to defend or reinforce more troubled and vulnerable areas along Russia's long borders

[3377] At the same time, the extensive reorganization and reduction that is generally taking place within the Russian forces is also taking place within the Leningrad Military District

[3378] This has led to a marked reduction in the scope of exercises and operational activities within the forces in the district

[3379] The number of divisions in LEMD is halved

[3380] The majority of the remaining divisions are understaffed

[3381] But the divisions are being strengthened with new equipment (tanks and self-propelled artillery

[3382] They will receive lighter equipment and will be part of a more defensive corps/brigade structure

[3383] However, the transfer of fighter-bombers to the Northern Fleet and a helicopter regiment to the army in the north increases offensive capacity

[3384] The net effect is probably that the capacity that can be deployed towards the northern Norwegian area under given circumstances is less than previously

[3385] The dissolution of the Warsaw Pact and Russian withdrawal from Eastern Europe have simultaneously led to the elimination of the invasion threat against Southern Norway, unless a major European war is first fought in which Russia regains control over all of Eastern Europe

[3386] Norway's overall defense capability is therefore developing as a consequence of four main development trends

[3387] the combat capability of the national defense is weakened, - the combat capability of allied reinforcements is maintained or strengthened, - Russian capacity to intervene militarily in Northern Norway is materially improved, but other factors make it very uncertain, - there is no longer any threat of invasion against Southern Norway

[3388] Overall, this provides a basis for characterizing our defense capability as satisfactory in the current situation, primarily because a significant part of the country no longer faces any real threat of invasion

[3389] National security

[3390] When assessing national security, the potential attacker's intentions to use military force must also be taken into account

[3391] Even though one's own defense capabilities to some extent influence other states' assessments of the appropriateness of military means, there is still reason to believe that Russian assessments in this area are determined by the country's fundamental strategic interests and needs

[3392] Political, economic, and social disintegration creates an overriding need for outside help, making it unlikely that Russia would see its interests served by a major war in Europe - especially as long as the type of assistance the country needs cannot be conquered by military force

[3393] However, the possibility of local conflicts in which military means are used, including in the highlands, cannot be ruled out in the longer term

[3394] The overall risk that Russia would see the use of military force against Norway or our allies in Western Europe as appropriate or necessary must be said to be greatly reduced

[3395] The Norwegian Armed Forces' peacekeeping organization and activities

[3396] In this report, it has been chosen to focus on the main lines of the Norwegian Armed Forces' future peacekeeping organization

[3397] The specific and detailed organizational changes will be submitted to the Storting in separate propositions

[3398] The Armed Forces' peacetime organization and activities are determined primarily by the size and composition of the war structure

[3399] The Norwegian defense is a mobilization defense where the war structure will govern the use of resources

[3400] The organization of the Armed Forces' activities in peacetime must therefore be adapted so that the organization safeguards what is necessary to produce and maintain the war structure, and to be able to carry out mobilization and force recovery

[3401] In addition, the Armed Forces' peacekeeping organization must be able to perform functions such as asserting sovereignty, supporting civil society, etc

[3402] Chapter 6 describes the Norwegian Armed Forces' wartime structure

[3403] until the year

[3404] These plans assume a relatively strong reduction in the current war structure

[3405] The peace organization must be adapted to the war structure we are to achieve within the same time frame, and the adaptation of the peace organization must be carried out in such a way that it happens in step with the transformation of the war structure

[3406] The report previously pointed to a number of security policy and economic factors that entail a high degree of uncertainty regarding future developments

[3407] During the implementation of the reorganization of the Armed Forces, this must be taken into account, so that the future organization is as flexible as possible

[3408] This means that some organizational choices must be made at a somewhat later date, but without this hindering the restructuring process

[3409] The Ministry will return to this on an ongoing basis in future organizational proposals

[3410] Security policy developments have reduced the requirements for standing readiness

[3411] This development, together with the changed financial framework that is the result of the Storting's budget decisions from 1990 onwards, has led to a significantly increased need for change within the Armed Forces compared to St meld no

[3412] This has been expressed in the organizational propositions no. 53 (1990-91), no. 43 (1991-92), no. 99 (1991-92) and St. prp. no. 98 (1991-92) on military conscription and changes in service time and service pattern for personnel for initial service

[3413] These propositions and associated recommendations form the basis for further work on changing and adapting the Armed Forces' peacekeeping organization to the proposed war structure

[3414] The principles of the new management concept for the Armed Forces are described in more detail in chapter

[3415] These are the basis for further development of the Armed Forces Peacekeeping Organization

[3416] The principles suggest a simplification of the current command system, goal and results management, greater coordination of similar activities across traditional dividing lines between and within the defense branches and the Home Guard, and greater centralization of the Armed Forces' activities within the individual regions and districts

[3417] This will of course lead to ripple effects of a district political nature, as pointed out in chapter

[3418] CHIEF OF DEFENCE

[3419] MANAGEMENT AND JOINT INSTITUTIONS

[3420] The Ministry of Defence shall have an overarching, constitutionally governing and controlling role, while the Chief of Defence shall be responsible for the executive management and control of the Armed Forces' overall activities and use of resources

[3421] The work that has been initiated to improve the ministry's own organization in order to be able to manage in line with the principles in the management concept will continue

[3422] The Ministry will then become a more integrated working secretariat for the Minister, and will strengthen its ability to investigate new policy areas and long-term strategies within its areas of responsibility

[3423] During the period, the Ministry will strive for internal rationalization with the aim of reducing operating expenses and getting more out of the available resources

[3424] The Supreme Command of the Armed Forces and the defense commands The implementation of the new management concept for the Armed Forces and the changes in NATO's command structure that are explained in Chapter 3 will have consequences for the current command structure

[3425] The new management concept indicates that an organizational structure must be established to a greater extent than before that enables better cross-prioritization and resource allocation

[3426] The Ministry has initiated studies assessing the internal organization of the Norwegian Armed Forces High Command and the defense commands and their mutual relationships, as well as their relationship with NATO

[3427] This assessment assumes that overall savings within senior management of at least 25 percent will be achieved

[3428] It is also a prerequisite that the joint staff in the High Command be strengthened with the aim of achieving better cross-prioritization and coordination in the Armed Forces

[3429] The Ministry aims to clarify these issues so that they can be presented to the Storting during the

[3456] ARMY AND HOME GUARD

[3457] The Norwegian Defence Forces' peacekeeping organisation has education, force production and mobilisation of the war structure as its primary tasks

[3458] This includes school and training departments, and preparatory departments and staff levels to plan and facilitate rehearsal exercises, preparedness and any transition to war

[3459] Furthermore, an extensive fleet of equipment will be maintained and modernized

[3460] This requires an efficient workshop and supply organization

[3461] The army's peacekeeping organization must now be rationalized and dimensioned according to the needs of the war structure

[3462] The peace organization must be concentrated to a greater extent than today in the main areas of inner Troms and in the Eastern region

[3463] It will be necessary to close down and merge departments and educational units in all branches of the Army, leaving fewer service locations, and also reduce activities within most of the remaining garrisons and educational units

[3464] Within the land defense, the district commands (DK) will continue to constitute the main elements of the regional organization both in peace and war

[3465] This is where operational, force-producing and administrative responsibilities come together

[3466] The tasks and responsibilities of the district commands will largely remain as they are today

[3467] Their tasks in the peace organization will be strengthened by giving them greater responsibility for mobilization preparations and the management of mobilization materials

[3468] The number of district commands, their location and size will be considered in line with the downsizing of the war structure, but will initially be proposed to be reduced from five to four by merging DK Vestlandet and DK Sørlandet

[3469] The current defense districts/land defense and reserve departments will be proposed to be closed down and replaced by a lower number of territorial regiments

[3470] The regiments will handle operational planning and leadership in war at the local level, undertake total defense planning in collaboration with the counties' emergency response agencies, and be the local administrative authority

[3471] Some of the territorial regiments will also be centers of expertise for a branch of the armed forces and have administrative responsibility for the refresher training centers

[3472] Where there are multiple arms-specific competence centers within the same territorial regiment's area, these will appear as separate regiments without territorial responsibility

[3473] All current departments will be closed down and the tasks will be transferred to other levels as follows

[3474] The competence centers take over the roll call for the conscript command

[3475] The Conscription Agency takes over the roll call of private personnel

[3476] The district commands take over the management of the mobilization materials

[3477] The competence centers and education departments in Northern Norway take over educational responsibility for the refresher courses

[3478] Training of personnel during initial service will mainly take place at the individual arm's competence centers, the reduced "brigade school

[3479] Brigade in Northern Norway), through the IRF battalion and at branches in Finnmark

[3480] Training of personnel for the Home Guard with 6 months of service will, for the time being, take place at the garrisons and service locations that are already used for this purpose, and at garrisons that are fully or partially released due to reduced production for the field army

[3481] The number of garrisons that will conduct this education will need to be assessed in relation to future educational needs and the desire for the most cost-effective education possible

[3482] Standing departments

[3483] The requirement for standing readiness has been greatly reduced as a consequence of recent security policy developments

[3484] The brigade in Northern Norway will therefore be adapted to future production needs for the field army rather than emergency preparedness conditions

[3485] This will involve a reduction of the brigade, which will consist of a varying number of larger and smaller training units

[3486] Any tasks in a preparedness context must be adapted to the department’s size and level of education

[3487] Norway's contribution to NATO's multinational forces (the IRF battalion) will be a standing infantry battalion that will be capable of meeting the requirements set within the alliance

[3488] His Majesty the King's Guard will carry out missions for the Royal House as today

[3489] The Border Guard in Sør-Varanger is expected to remain in place with a strength level similar to today

[3490] Competence centers, schools and training departments

[3491] In the future structure, all branches of the Army are expected to have their own competence center established in connection with the weapon instructors and weapon schools

[3492] This is almost complete today

[3493] The competence centers will be responsible for the weapon's tactical and technical development, basic officer training, recruit training, conducting rehearsal exercises and rolling up the weapon's conscript commanders

[3494] Crew training and basic officer training currently take place at 28 education departments with centers of gravity in District Command Eastern Norway and District Command Northern Norway

[3495] In the effort to reduce the number of education departments, the Ministry will emphasize these professional principles: - mainly one department in Northern Norway and one in Southern Norway for each branch of the military, with the exception of the Infantry, which will have a greater need, - the shortest possible distance between departments from the different branches of the military, with the aim of improving opportunities for cooperation and reducing education costs, - maintaining opportunities for training in brigade and higher formations, - facilitating a possible consistent service pattern

[3496] the educational departments must be provided with good shooting and training ranges and other establishments

[3497] When it comes to the training of officers and civilian personnel, the Ministry refers to a separate report to the Storting on training in the Armed Forces

[3498] However, it can be mentioned that the number of command schools in the Infantry will be considered for reduction

[3499] Other officer schools are expected to be maintained, but the size of each school will be adapted to educational needs

[3500] It will be proposed to merge the army's war schools at Linderud and Gimlemoen

[3501] The Army Staff College and the Army Administration College will have reduced operations

[3502] The army's educational activities must be adapted to the requirements of the future war structure

[3503] In addition to an assessment of training and education during initial service, at command and war schools and other schools, the refresher exercises must be specifically assessed

[3504] It will be more necessary than before to prioritize between the rehearsal departments with regard to the frequency, length, content, implementation and location of the exercises

[3505] The Army Supply Command will have the same responsibility as today with regard to the acquisition and operation of materiel for the Army

[3665] EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXERCISES

[3666] The Norwegian Armed Forces are one of the country's largest educational institutions, including the training of conscripts

[3667] The main principle is that educational levels and educational systems should support the needs of the Norwegian Armed Forces' warfighting structure in the future

[3668] It will also be planned that the education will enable targeted use of personnel within the peace organization

[3669] The scope of educational activities will be adjusted to adapt to the future structure of the Armed Forces

[3670] In addition, the lack of other degrees of freedom means that activity, and thus also training and exercises, will have to bear a significant portion of the operating savings, especially before the effects of organizational changes and changes in the personnel structure become noticeable

[3671] This is a direct consequence of the decision to shield material investments, as the most important contribution to the war structure

[3672] In the following, the term "training" is used to refer to the daily training of individuals and smaller units in a garrison, on a vessel, fort, station or other unit

[3673] Exercise" is used to refer to training that takes place during several days of continuous activity in the field, waters and airspace by larger units or forces

[3674] For the sake of simplicity, however, "rehearsal exercise" is used as a common term for the activity in the rehearsal departments that normally includes both initial training and a final field exercise

[3675] Training of commanders

[3676] Officer training is provided at officer schools, war schools, and staff and administration schools

[3677] The quality of officer training will be maintained at the current level, but the scope will be adjusted to meet future reduced needs

[3678] Basic officer training will continue to take place at the defense branches' officer training schools

[3679] These are intended to provide students with basic knowledge, attitudes and skills so that they are able to function in the mobilization defense as a squad commander after sufficient practical service at a department

[3680] Modern equipment often places different and higher demands on education and skill levels than what one year officer schools make possible

[3681] To utilize resources in the best possible way, training must be conducted in accordance with current needs

[3682] The military schools are to continue the foundation that the command has already received and, in addition, develop the students further into professionally well-qualified officers and leaders

[3683] Emphasis will be placed on retraining commanders for other tasks, as a result of the major changes the Armed Forces will have to undergo to adapt the organization to reduced resource allocation

[3684] Staff schools and management schools will continue to have a central place within upper secondary education

[3685] Great emphasis will be placed on improving the competence of the commanding corps when it comes to financial and budget management

[3686] Greater emphasis will also be placed on educating leaders who can function within the framework of increasing international cooperation

[3687] Particular emphasis will be placed on enabling our officers to serve in allied and international staffs

[3688] A number of officers will continue to be sent to courses abroad so that they can keep up with international developments and so that they can contribute to innovative thinking within their own organization

[3689] Relevant management training for the Armed Forces' leaders will be important in achieving the best possible leadership and resource management

[3690] Education of civilians

[3691] In cases where new recruitment is necessary, the Armed Forces will continue to employ civilians with relevant education and expertise from civilian educational institutions to the greatest extent possible

[3692] It will be the best use of resources in terms of the Armed Forces' needs

[3693] There will also be an emphasis on retraining civilians to meet needs resulting from reorganizations

[3694] Internationalization, changing requirements for competence and adaptability will pose future challenges

[3695] To overcome this, the Armed Forces will continue to focus on high-quality and targeted further education, and retraining where deemed appropriate to achieve the best possible utilization of personnel resources

[3696] Training and practice during initial service

[3697] In order to best enable our military departments to solve their wartime tasks, in addition to being equipped with the necessary high-quality equipment, there is a need for the forces to practice under as realistic conditions as possible and to the necessary extent

[3698] In a defense based on conscription and mobilization, the standing departments and units are also under training the a large part of the time

[3699] This applies in particular to the Army, where the proportion of conscripts is the largest and where the departments at any given time contain several contingents with different periods of service behind them

[3700] This will be even more pronounced with a future reduction in the initial service for certain categories

[3701] Training of the individual soldier and unit must therefore have first priority when planning all service

[3702] The Navy has streamlined its training activities by establishing a more base-oriented sailing pattern for the Navy

[3703] This development will continue

[3704] The Coastal Artillery will carry out its educational activities at training forts and competence centers

[3705] Bodø, Ørland and Rygge main air stations will become the Air Force's main bases for training during initial service

[3706] Repetition exercises and HV exercises

[3707] Future conflicts will place high demands on the departments' operational standards

[3708] Even with the current frequency of rehearsal exercises, it is not realistic to assume that mobilization units will be able to meet these requirements without an intensive training period before being deployed into combat

[3709] This thus becomes a guiding factor for choosing the time of mobilization

[3710] For the Army's prioritized units in the brigade and division structure, the current exercise frequency (3-4 years) will be maintained

[3711] However, the scope and content of the exercises will be changed with the aim of increasing the benefits for the individual soldier and smaller unit

[3712] Personnel in territorial departments and units will have their training levels reduced

[3713] These departments must be given the necessary additional training as part of the mobilization itself

[3714] The Navy's pattern for rehearsal exercises will maintain its current frequency

[3715] However, total resource use is to be reduced by 20 percent

[3716] This should be achieved, among other things, by

[3717] through shorter and more intensive exercises with selective participation (cadre exercises

[3718] Rehearsal exercises should be coordinated with other activities to ensure good utilization of personnel and material resources, and to improve the benefits of the exercises

[3719] The effectiveness of the air defense departments and mobilization additions to the K&V stations is expected to increase during the period with the training at NOAH/NASAMS and the implementation of mobilization exercises at the air stations, with support from the K&V stations

[3720] The scope of these exercises is under review

[3721] A balanced distribution of activity reductions across the entire Armed Forces indicates that the Home Guard's practice of annual exercises will be assessed during the period

[3722] High training standards are an essential part of the concept of quality

[3723] However, building up the departments' training level is both the least time-consuming part of a strength recovery process, and the part of the process that is under the strongest degree of national control

[3724] If resource shortages make it necessary to relax quality requirements, this therefore indicates that material procurement is prioritized over training, especially in the refresher departments

[3725] Necessary repetition must instead be considered an integral part of the mobilization itself

[3726] This has corresponding consequences for how quickly the departments will be ready for deployment

[3727] The part of the quality determined by the training standard will therefore not be present at all times, but will only be achieved after a preparation period that is reasonably consistent with the notice period that can be expected based on security policy conditions

[3728] Primarily, this will only apply to lower priority mobilization departments of all branches of defense

[3729] However, it cannot be ruled out that the resource situation will force a more extensive reduction in repetition activity for shorter periods

[3730] The detrimental effects of this on the staff and management elements that are trained in connection with larger exercises for rehearsal departments will be compensated for through increased use of computer-supported staff service exercises, etc

[3731] The weighing of considerations must be carried out continuously, also in light of the security policy situation and the assumptions made in NATO regarding expected warning times and readiness requirements

[3732] Joint exercises with allies Allied support must be arranged and practiced in peacetime

[3733] This will also require efforts from Norwegian resources, including personnel resources

[3734] There will therefore also be a need in the future to train both national and allied forces at approximately the same level as today under different climatic conditions

[3735] Exercises with allied reinforcement forces are a prerequisite for the successful deployment of such units under Norwegian conditions, and will continue to be given high priority

[3736] The ability to lead national and allied forces is also a crucial condition for continued Norwegian command of allied reinforcements in crisis and war

[3737] training of command and staff levels

[3738] The Armed Forces will have to emphasize a more garrison- and base-oriented training pattern for both initial service and refresher exercises, primarily to achieve the necessary savings on the operating budget

[3739] However, this also opens up the possibilities for more targeted and realistic training of the individual soldier and lower unit, especially in the Army, where large field service exercises are mainly conducted for the benefit of staffs and higher-level command levels

[3740] Field service exercises provide excellent practice in dealing with field conditions, but rarely provide the opportunity to practice lower-level combat skills under realistic conditions

[3741] This is the main reason why there is currently a certain imbalance between the departments' field resilience, which is in some cases very good, and their combat technical level, which in some contexts is insufficient

[3742] Great emphasis will therefore be placed on developing shooting and training ranges with the necessary infrastructure, to ensure that more garrison-oriented training creates opportunities for a greater degree of realism and efficiency in the training of leaders and departments at lower levels

[3743] The disadvantages of the base- and garrison-oriented exercise pattern for staffs and higher level command levels will be compensated for through increased focus on computer-based staff service exercises and war games

[3744] In the long term, these have significant training and financial gain potential, in that it will be possible to practice the staff apparatus both more frequently and more realistically in a number of areas than real exercises allow, without the simultaneous need to have large departments physically present in terrain, waters and airspace

[3745] The computer-based management simulators thus make it possible to confront commanders and staffs with real decision-making problems in real time, without the training, safety, environmental and other limitations that always accompany large exercises

[3746] In addition, technical simulator systems will become increasingly important for training individual soldiers and crews on weapons systems and platforms that are complicated and expensive to use, with the aim of reducing the use of expensive input factors such as fuel and ammunition

[3747] A deprioritization of preparedness considerations in favor of force production also indicates that commanders' meetings and cadre exercises for mobilization exercises will no longer be used to review and update operational plans, but to train the individual in his or her service position and function

[3748] DEFENCE OPERATIONAL ACTIVITIES

[3749] Participation in NATO's Multinational Response Forces As part of NATO's new force structure, the Alliance will create larger multinational response forces

[3750] These forces will play an increasingly important role in NATO's strategy, which is based on the assumption that any new conflict in Europe will be regional in nature

[3751] In this context, it is important that Norway, which itself is a nation dependent on reinforcements, contributes suitable land, sea and air combat forces

[3752] Besides the fact that through participation in the multinational forces we demonstrate our willingness to take joint responsibility, this will contribute in a decisive way to making it easier for the same forces to be deployed in our part of the alliance's area of responsibility in the event of crisis and war

[3753] For the Army, an infantry battalion is planned, with special readiness and training

[3754] The additional costs of establishing such a department will have consequences for other activities in the Army, but will also add significant experience and expertise

[3755] For the Navy, permanent participation with a frigate and a mine clearance vessel is being considered

[3756] This will roughly be a continuation of the involvement Norway has had so far in the Standing Atlantic Force (STANAVFORLANT) and in the Channel Command Mine Clearance Force (STANAVFORCHAN

[3757] In addition, consideration is being given to making another frigate and a mine clearance vessel available as a contribution to a regional emergency response force for the Northern Region

[3758] With reduced military service time, this may require a greater proportion of enlisted crew in several of the work positions on board

[3759] The Air Force has many years of experience participating in multinational operations through deployment and exercises

[3760] The Air Force will continue to have personnel assigned to the NATO Airborne Warning and Control Force (NAEW

[3761] In addition, an F-16 squadron will be earmarked for NATO's multinational response forces, possibly as a collaboration with the Danish Defense Forces

[3762] Participation in UN operations

[3763] Norwegian participation in UN peacekeeping operations is a political priority area

[3764] Resources will therefore be allocated for increased engagement in this area

[3765] Norway is an important contributor to UN peacekeeping operations

[3766] Norway's support for the UN's peacekeeping commitment must be seen in the context of our support and expectations for the organization's activities in general, and with the good experiences we have gained with this type of international military presence in conflict areas

[3767] Norway's military involvement in the UN has gradually gained significant scope

[3768] In November 1992, slightly over 1,000 Norwegian officers and crews participated in peacekeeping operations in the Middle East, the Persian Gulf, Asia, Africa and the former Yugoslavia

[3769] The framework for the Norwegian emergency response force is therefore proposed to be increased, from 1,300 commanders and crews

[3770] It is also proposed that the strength itself be adjusted in line with the new requirements for participation

[3771] The harbor command is proposed to be abolished, and the force should be added to an engineer company and a transport company

[3772] The UN's military involvement has experienced a significant upsurge since the end of the post-war period

[3773] The UN has become an important conflict resolution mechanism in the international community

[3774] The UN is involved in more peacemaking and peacekeeping operations than before

[3775] Approximately 50,000 soldiers operate in the service of the UN

[3776] The number of countries providing military forces has increased from about

[3777] For the first time, a peacekeeping operation under UN auspices has been launched in Europe; UNPROFOR in the former Yugoslavia

[3778] To a greater extent than before, UN operations now also include civilian tasks

[3779] Many of the ongoing operations have missions related to election monitoring, disarmament of guerrilla groups, human rights monitoring and civilian police tasks

[3780] Composite forces/operations" involve a larger civilian component and in many cases also a civilian leader of the operation

[3781] Peacekeeping operations that also involve coercion are no longer excluded, either in international conflicts or in civil war-like situations

[3782] It can therefore be expected that the tasks that UN forces must be prepared to perform in the future will be more varied than before, i.e. that they will cover a larger part of the spectrum that ranges from observation through peacekeeping to peacemaking operations

[3783] Participation will be based on volunteerism when it comes to Norwegian commanders and crews

[3784] The government emphasizes that UN personnel receive the best possible education

[3785] In this regard, the current system should be improved

[3786] It will be considered whether a national training and competence center should be established for this purpose

[3787] The government has also taken an initiative with the UN to establish an international training institute for senior key personnel in Norway

[3788] This could possibly be seen as an expansion of a purely national center

[3987] This could not be done with the limited time the Commission had at its disposal
