[3989] FK90 recommended a defense structure that, according to itself, constitutes a lower limit for maintaining the current defense concept

[3990] It is therefore important that we can have a defense policy debate about what alternatives exist in relation to this concept

[3991] When inviting a defense policy debate on alternative defense concepts, it must be emphasized that this does not imply any form of position on whether such concepts are considered relevant or desirable

[3992] Our current defense concept, with the ambition of anti-invasion capacity in the most vulnerable parts of the country, remains in place

[3993] However, developments in the coming years may make it more relevant to consider alternative defense concepts, with lower levels of ambition than invasion defense

[3994] As a basis for such a defense policy debate, it will therefore be outlined why and how alternative defense concepts might become relevant

[3995] Certain developments of a political, economic and technological nature will therefore be assessed in relation to the long-term effects these may have on alternative ways of viewing the function, tasks and role of the Armed Forces in the future

[3996] The assessments will necessarily have to be based on outlines of possible development courses, primarily purely security policy ones

[3997] It is not only the sketches that are of greatest interest in this context, but also the fact that there are several factors that may make assessment of alternative defense concepts relevant

[3998] However, the sketches are intended to illustrate the types of challenges Norway may face when it comes to the long-term design of the Armed Forces and the determination of the Armed Forces' future role and function

[3999] DEVELOPMENTAL TRENDS THAT AFFECT THE CHOICE OF DEFENSE CONCEPT

[4000] Political developments

[4001] The discussion in Chapter 3 of the security policy situation in Europe emphasizes uncertainty about developments in the coming years as the most dominant feature of the picture

[4002] This uncertainty and unpredictability open up a wide spectrum of possible outcomes, some of which provide reason to assess the Norwegian defense concept in light of key international developments

[4003] The United States, like Europe, is in disarray after the end of the post-war period

[4004] A new American administration represents a generational shift, and will have to consider the nature of the United States' future role in Europe

[4005] If developments lead to the United States maintaining its involvement in European security issues, NATO will likely remain in the form it is currently envisioned

[4006] However, this implies changes in both strategy and force structure, with a greater focus on multinational, integrated reaction forces, perhaps especially intended for local and limited conflicts

[4007] A possible Norwegian concept would therefore be to focus on a stronger degree of integration in the alliance's joint defense, beyond the commitments that Norway has already undertaken

[4008] If, in the longer term, the United States were to choose to withdraw from Europe with the bulk of its forces, and also reduce its political involvement, this would probably lead to an increase in the importance of the WEU

[4009] NATO would then have less importance in the interconnection of European and trans-Atlantic security perspectives and interests

[4010] In such a situation, the limited national capacities of European countries will further highlight the development of a multinational joint defense

[4011] International specialization and task division then become necessary to maintain capabilities that only the United States would be able to have on a national basis

[4012] However, this would be a type of alliance where the members in given situations would likely only have limited opportunities for engagement in Norway and its surrounding areas

[4013] Norwegian opportunities to create a reinforcement commitment similar to the one Norway currently enjoys in NATO would in any case require clear Norwegian integration into such a joint defense

[4014] If Russia succeeds in the course that the country's political leadership is trying to follow, Russia will in the long term be able to grow into the larger European political and economic community, regardless of the formal form of cooperation

[4015] In that case, the use of military force in the NorwegianRussian conflict context will probably appear as remote as it is in relation to other Western European countries

[4016] Not because Norway will be a militarily credible adversary, but because the use of force against another member of the community will have political costs that exceed the value of influencing Norwegian politics in any context

[4017] Such a development could lead to Norwegian authorities finding it justifiable to have a defense with a lower level of ambition than antiinvasion

[4018] If the EC process were to continue along the lines outlined in the Maastricht Treaty, Norway would have to deal with expanded European defense and security cooperation

[4019] Then the crucial point would be how closely Norway is linked to such cooperation

[4020] If the connection were close, Norway would have significant political and military backing in relation to any pressure and challenges from an authoritarian Russia

[4021] Financial framework

[4022] The way structure the message proposes in the longer term is based on FK90's stance

[4023] In the Commission's assessment, such a structure can be realized with a financial framework at the level of the 1992 budget, compensated for wage and price increases

[4024] To achieve this, however, the Commission has made very optimistic assumptions about operational reductions, including a personnel reduction of 6,400 people over a ten-year period

[4025] Furthermore, it was assumed that a new coast guard vessel, new rescue helicopters and any new tasks for the Armed Forces would be financed outside the framework

[4026] These are assumptions that have changed, and which therefore contribute to tightening the requirements regarding the implementation of the Commission's structure in the longer term

[4027] The goal of implementing this structure therefore places further pressure on the need for operational savings

[4028] A development that implies a lower total material investment than approximately 30 billion 1992-kroner over the period 1994-98 should lead to a reassessment of anti-invasion capability as a goal for Norwegian defense in the longer term

[4029] Otherwise, it will require significant budget increases in later periods to make up for what has been lost

[4030] Technological development

[4031] There are also aspects of military technological development that affect Norway and other small countries in a special way

[4032] Modern military equipment is being renewed today by giving each new generation of equipment higher performance than the equipment it replaces, primarily by introducing new technology

[4033] On the performance side, this contributes to making approximate technological parity critically important for the outcome of military operations, i.e. technological inferiority can no longer be compensated to the same extent by tactical adaptation or the like, cf

[4034] On the cost side, however, it leads to a price increase also in fixed kroner from one generation of equipment to the next, making it increasingly difficult to modernize military units on a one-by-one basis

[4035] Currently, this so called technological increase in price amounts to 2-4 percent per year for the most important material categories, i.e. the replacement value of a complete defense structure doubles approximately every 20 years

[4036] It is likely that reduced international tensions and tougher competition in the market will reduce this growth somewhat, but unless there are completely unexpected and revolutionary technological breakthroughs, it will still continue to push costs upwards

[4037] This decimating effect of technological cost increases is of course relatively the same in all countries, but the problems first become critical in small countries that have the least to reduce in the first place

[4038] Unless a prolonged period of economic recession slows down development because even the major countries will not be able to keep up, Norway will therefore be faced with fundamental defense policy decisions within the foreseeable future

[4039] It will occur when it is no longer economically feasible to maintain a defense that is both qualitatively credible and quantitatively sufficient under any realistic threat or challenge

[4040] ALTERNATIVES TO

[4041] If a national balanced invasion defense as a result of a deliberate development, or on the basis of economic necessity, were to be abandoned, there are in principle three alternative main strategies

[4042] The defense can be organized as an invasion defense built on a risky assumption of large allied reinforcements

[4043] The armed forces can be organized as a core defense force designed to fulfill peacekeeping tasks, combined with a cadre function for rebuilding a larger organization over a longer period

[4044] The ambition of being able to fight off an invasion is abandoned in favor of a lower level of ambition and the structure is adapted to this

[4045] The conditional invasion defense can consequently be structured in several ways, depending on which dimension one chooses to place the risk in

[4046] For a defense with a lower level of ambition, several solutions can be considered, depending on what this level of ambition should be

[4047] Reinforcement-based anti-invasion capability

[4048] If the anti-invasion capacity is linked to a dependence on allied reinforcements, this can in practice be done in three ways

[4049] Option 1 would be to create a nationally unbalanced structure in which one or a few sectors are completely closed down, e.g. the fighter aircraft sector or the Navy's anti-invasion elements (coastal artillery, missile torpedo boats

[4050] Instead, it is assumed that the corresponding capacities will be provided by Norway's allies, either directly as reinforcements - e.g. fighter squadrons - or through corresponding operations in Norwegian areas - e.g. aircraft carrier groups in the Norwegian Sea

[4051] Alternative 2 would be to maintain a national defense that is balanced in the sense that it continues all major components in a certain minimum number, and then assume that a broad spectrum of reinforcements can be supplied in time, aircraft, land forces, etc

[4052] Alternative 3 would be to tailor all of the Norwegian Armed Forces' significant elements for participation in the alliance's new multinational response forces, i.e. full integration that leaves only the pure territorial defense (HV, equivalent) outside the alliance structure

[4053] Alternative 1, a nationally unbalanced structure, has as its greatest advantage that the savings potential is very high when entire businesses can be closed down with their associated personnel categories, education schemes, etc

[4054] A controlled closure of the fighter sector by 2010 will thus make it possible to maintain approximately the FK-90 structure for the Army and Navy themselves with a 2 percent annual reduction in the budget until 2000 and zero growth thereafter

[4055] It is then assumed that three large bases will be maintained in northern Norway with a view to Allied fighter reinforcements

[4056] Similarly, a solution where no new investments are made in the naval invasion defense within the same total framework would allow the Army division with four brigades in Troms to be maintained along with four large air bases and 60 combat aircraft

[4057] This provides a marginal antiinvasion capacity in Troms, assuming 1-2 Allied squadrons of air defense fighters in addition to the basic assumption that an early sea invasion is unlikely due to Allied naval control in the Norwegian Sea

[4058] A third option would be to prioritize the Navy and Air Force at the expense of the Army, but since this would mean maintaining a naval invasion defense without a corresponding capability on land, such an alternative would not make sense

[4059] However, the disadvantages of a nationally unbalanced structure are many, such as negative consequences for peacekeeping and crisis management, and high vulnerability to hostile strategy adaptation to this imbalance in the opening phase of a conflict

[4060] A unilateral waiver of operational responsibility with a declaration that Norway's allies are expected to cover this sector will also have a very unfortunate political effect within the alliance

[4061] Such solutions are therefore only nationally acceptable as part of any future agreements on a comprehensive division of labor and specialization within NATO or other international security cooperation

[4062] Option 2, a balanced but insufficient defense, has a lower savings potential because all sectors are maintained

[4063] Thus, in a typical such structure, the Army would be able to have three independent brigades, the Navy could maintain the submarine force, but would have to refrain from new investments in coastal artillery and missile torpedo boats, while the Air Force could retain 60 combat aircraft and four large bases in Northern Norway

[4064] If the anti-invasion capability is to be maintained, this will thus require a minimum of two Allied brigades in addition to two Norwegian brigades deployed in Troms, a favorable naval situation in the Norwegian Sea and 1-2 Allied fighter squadrons transferred and ready before a conflict breaks out

[4065] The disadvantages are thus not as great with regard to peacekeeping missions, etc., but the reinforcement requirement will be all the more critical, because a broad spectrum of all types of forces is required here

[4066] Option 3, a defense structure fully integrated into NATO's new response forces, would be in line with the assumption on which the alliance's new strategy and force structure are based, namely that a future conflict in Europe is likely to be regional and limited

[4067] Reference is made below to section 3.3.5 for a more detailed description of the force structure

[4068] In this regard, Norway has already decided to contribute to the IRF (Immediate Response Force

[4069] Full integration would have to consist of participating with larger forces from all branches of defense in the manner that Norway, in agreement with the alliance, finds appropriate, preferably in multinational units linked to the RRF (rapid response forces

[4070] It can thus be expected that the availability and ability of the response forces to be deployed in Norway will increase

[4071] However, the high demands on preparedness, training level and material standards that this requires, indicate that such departments must mainly be permanent and based on voluntary conscripts or enlisted personnel

[4072] This in itself will have a limiting effect on the scope, and in reality entails a division of the Armed Forces into a highly qualified standing part and a territorial defence based on short initial service for the bulk of the conscript population

[4073] Anti-invasion capability based on force reconstruction over time

[4074] All branches of defense have so far been dependent on mobilization in the transition from peace to preparedness and war, albeit to varying degrees

[4075] With the structures that can be realized on a low budget, however, this need will have to be seen as twofold; a relatively short-term mobilization need and a somewhat longer-term strength recovery need

[4076] Ideally, the organization of the Armed Forces should allow for two forms of expansion

[4077] mobilization of a certain war structure at relatively short notice with a view to crisis management, reinforced border surveillance, defense against strategic coup, reinforcementdependent invasion defense or other tasks for which the individual structure may be dimensioned

[4078] This will, as now, mainly be a problem concerning the Army, because the other two branches of defense are to a completely different extent based on standing forces with a high proportion of professional personnel; - expansion of the entire Defense to a significantly higher level in the longer term if security policy developments make this desirable and the necessary financial resources are made available

[4079] This will primarily be a question of combining the tasks of the individual branches of defense in peacetime and during mobilization with a structure that can function as a cadre in a reconstruction of the Armed Forces that takes place over years

[4080] However, it may be difficult to maintain a satisfactory ability to handle both peacekeeping tasks and two different forms of expansion in one and the same structure without making compromises that are both costly and have a strong negative impact on the ability to solve each of the tasks

[4081] It may therefore be appropriate to consider a core defense adapted to a combination of peacekeeping tasks and the long-term recovery function, which probably indicates that such a specialized organization makes the more short-term mobilization function impossible to maintain for both financial and organizational reasons

[4082] This solution involves a standing defense force that is large enough and professional enough to both carry out peacekeeping tasks and to function as an instructor and command cadre at all levels in a long-term reconstruction of the Armed Forces

[4083] In practice, such a scheme would probably have to mean that the Army, Navy and Air Force in their entirety consisted of voluntary conscripts or enlisted personnel

[4084] The Home Guard had to be retained as a conscription-based force with a short initial service (3-4 months) and 4-5 years on the rolls to ensure the territorial security function

[4085] The fundamental weakness of such a structure would be its inability to mobilize a large war structure on relatively short notice

[4086] The doubts associated with the possibilities for large-scale material acquisitions at a time when international tensions may be rising are partly compensated by assuming a period of several years for the recovery of forces, but this will still be an uncertain figure

[4087] It must also be emphasized that this type of expansion requires very large annual budget increases if a force buildup of any significance is to be carried out even over 4-5 years

[4088] The strength of the structure lies in the ability to professionally perform tasks both at home and abroad in peacetime, combined with the ability to function as a cadre by providing an expanding defense with professional expertise at all levels - including the lower management level which is currently based on reserve commanders

[4089] The final balance will therefore consist of determining whether security policy developments indicate that the ability to maintain these functions becomes more important than the ability to mobilize for a major conflict at a few weeks' notice

[4090] Defense with a lower level of ambition

[4091] A defense with a lower level of ambition than antiinvasion will have to aim to establish a threshold that makes it necessary for an opponent to invade if it wishes to impose its political will on Norway

[4092] Should an opponent nevertheless invade, Norwegian military resistance, as a result of such a lower level of ambition, could quickly collapse, without the Norwegian side being able to ensure the reception of any allied reinforcements that would otherwise have given Norway the necessary anti-invasion capability

[4093] When this nevertheless appears to be a meaningful capacity, it is because military power can well be used as a political instrument at a lower level of intensity than invasion

[4094] A possible lower level of ambition could be a consequence of Norway consciously making a choice, considering the probability of invasion to be so small that it does not build up capacity to meet this possibility

[4095] With such a level of ambition, it will be important that modern military technology in the form of precision-guided weapons, among other things, enables the selective destruction of vital civilian and military targets without having to bear the political, military and economic burden of resorting to invasion or massive aerial bombing

[4096] This opens up the possibility of political blackmail using military means, which it will be important to be able to oppose in the future

[4097] The same will apply to the ability to protect against state-sponsored terrorism and other smaller military attacks and operations, which can also be assumed to be of increasing relevance and importance

[4098] Such an ambition will require a nationally balanced and quality-oriented defense with the ability to combat air attacks on civilian and military targets, prevent raids, sabotage and other efforts by special forces, and combat minelaying or other attacks against shipping along the coast

[4099] In addition, there is the ability to assert sovereignty and other peace functions under conditions that vary from peace to politically aggravated situations, i.e. patrolling and presence in Norwegian airspace and territorial waters, and the ability to have a reinforced presence in our border areas in the event of widespread unrest in our politically unstable neighboring country, Russia

[4100] The structure is also expected to provide the capacity to participate in international response and emergency forces, UN service, etc

[4101] Initially, such a structure may seem quite similar to a nationally balanced structure with anti-invasion capability based on allied reinforcements

[4102] However, abandoning the anti-invasion role would imply a different cross-prioritization between the branches of defense, on the basis that the air threat dominates when there is no anti-invasion capability, and the Defense Forces are thus not built up to be able to meet an invasion

[4103] This indicates a prioritization of the fighter air force, initially at the expense of the pure anti-invasion element of the Navy, but also to some extent at the expense of the Army

[4104] If a decision in principle were to be made to reduce the Armed Forces' level of ambition, this would therefore entail a structure consisting of a limited number (3-4) of independent brigades (but no divisions), and submarines, antisubmarine vessels, mine-clearing vessels and advanced combat aircraft with capacity for both air defense and attack on surface targets

[4105] A further emphasis on the capital-intensive Air Force at the expense of the Army and the personnel-intensive parts of the Navy (Coastal Artillery) combined with an absolute assumption of large operational savings, which would be necessary in this case, would indicate that the position of conscription would then have to be reassessed

[4106] A possible alternative to this type of structure would be a personnel-intensive and low-tech territorial defense that compensates for its qualitative inferiority by waging war over large areas, targeting the most vulnerable parts of the opponent's organization

[4107] This would in practice entail a purely guerrilla defense

[4108] Such a defense meets the desire for continued full utilization of the conscription population

[4109] At the same time, it enables the maintenance of the Armed Forces' peacekeeping operations at the current level, with positive consequences for employment and regional policy

[4110] However, a guerrilla strategy assumes that the country must first be occupied, and that one then uses limited actions directed against the occupying power's departments and activities to make the situation untenable for the attacker in the long term, thereby forcing him to withdraw

[4111] Throughout this phase, the guerrillas must live in secluded bases with no other supplies than those that can be obtained from the civilian population, dropped from planes, brought in from unoccupied territory or from friendly neighboring countries, etc

[4112] The classic guerrilla strategy also assumes that liberated zones are gradually established in occupied territory, and that the defensive struggle then takes on a more conventional form

[4113] Guerrilla campaigns thus take on the character of long-term moral and physical tests of strength, characterized by the occupier's reprisals against the civilian population and indiscriminate destruction of life and property over years

[4114] This is a form of defensive warfare that has proven effective in predominantly agricultural societies in parts of the Third World, provided that the guerrilla movement has initially been able to operate from bases in a friendly country and provided that the strategy's condition of gradual transition to conventional operations has been met

[4115] In a modern society like Norway, where special climatic conditions also play a role, however, the prerequisites for successful guerrilla warfare are not present as anything more than a supplement in occupied areas to conventional operations elsewhere

[4116] Such a strategy thus represents a defense that is not only unreliable in relation to the threat it assumes, but is also unilaterally directed towards a less likely challenge

[4117] The strategy also assumes that if conflict were to occur, the risk of unacceptable losses in human life and material assets would be great

[4118] The defense may develop in this direction if the organization is not reduced so that the expected operational savings are achieved, and where necessary material investments cannot be made as a result

[4119] Norwegian units will then gradually lose the ability to fight a modernly equipped attacker, and will instead have to make a tactical adjustment that in practice involves a transition to guerrilla defense

[4120] Guerrilla defense thus appears as the defense one indirectly chooses by not consciously making another choice

[4121] CONCLUSION As a consequence of these assessments, the Ministry will examine three alternatives in more detail with regard to the type of possible long-term development outlined

[4122] a national balanced core defence built up in relation to a combination of peacekeeping tasks and force reconstruction over a longer period; - a significant/important contribution to the Alliance's reaction forces with the aim of maintaining an alliance-based anti-invasion capability, combined with a national territorial defence; - a national balanced defence optimised for a non-invasion threat

[4123] As can be seen, there are clear organizational similarities between core defense and a defense based on strong integration in the alliance's multinational response forces

[4124] The further investigation will therefore also aim to clarify the possibilities for a combination of these alternatives

[4125] Strategy for the change process

[4126] General guidelines and principles The following describes how the restructuring of the Armed Forces' activities will be implemented in order to achieve the described war structure and peace organization

[4127] In this chapter, the Ministry will first specify the main guidelines and principles that will form the basis for the restructuring, then describe the measures that must be implemented to realize a war structure and peace organization in the individual branches of defense and how considerations of freedom of action can be safeguarded in the longer term

[4128] Finally, material development and construction, facilities and properties are discussed

[4129] The Armed Forces' restructuring needs at the beginning

[4130] to a new long-term notification period is not only affected by the changed framework conditions that this notification sets out

[4131] The Armed Forces also have a backlog from the previous period, where they were unable to make sufficient progress with the operational savings that were reported to the Storting

[4132] assumed to be implemented

[4133] This means that the budget framework will have greater consequences than the reduction in isolation would suggest

[4134] In this situation, it is therefore absolutely crucial that the transition takes place according to a comprehensive and overarching strategy, where ideal sectoral goals must give way

[4135] The difficulty is compounded by the fact that the downsizing must occur very quickly in relation to the degrees of freedom, especially on the personnel side

[4136] To ensure that certain sectors do not have to bear a disproportionately large part of the burden of the restructuring process, thereby bringing the organization completely out of balance, the effects must be distributed to other areas as well

[4137] Ideal goals and considerations must then be sacrificed, otherwise the development of the Armed Forces could easily become the result of pure arbitrariness

[4138] This could in turn create difficulties for the Armed Forces' ability to regain strength as quickly as possible, for example in a crisis situation

[4139] The financial framework for the long-term report is for the period as a whole somewhat below the total framework

[4140] The government will nevertheless maintain the structural goals of FK90, and thus a framework for material investments of 30 billion 1992 crowns in the LTM period

[4141] This is because both our own and other countries' studies clearly identify the acquisition and phasing in of modern equipment as the most time-critical part of a force-building process

[4142] If the proposed investments and new tasks (coast guard ships, rescue helicopters, increased UN involvement) are to be realized within the framework set by the Government, other parts of the budget must be reduced accordingly

[4143] This need is further reinforced by the fact that the cost calculations on which FK90 was based may prove to be somewhat optimistic

[4144] Primarily, this means reductions in those parts of the operating budget where there are degrees of freedom in the shorter term, i.e. by reducing the level of activity

[4145] A lower level of activity can be distributed in several ways, and it is therefore important to find a way to prioritize the activity that is consistent with the choices and priorities that are made in other areas

[4146] A conscription system is fundamentally very vulnerable to reduced intensity in training, compared to a system based on a larger proportion of professional soldiers

[4147] This is because new age groups of crew members must be trained to a certain skill level from scratch during a limited period of service

[4148] Furthermore, the constant repetition of this training process is very costly, compared to maintaining skills at a certain level after they have been first achieved

[4149] Since general conscription should continue to be a fundamental principle in our defense, it would therefore be contrary to the entire basic premise of conscription to allow activity reductions to affect initial service to a greater extent than is already planned through the proposed reductions in service time

[4150] This means in practice that the largest reductions will have to be made by the departments that have completed their basic training, i.e. the repeat departments

[4151] This is consistent with security policy developments, which require significantly increased warning time before a potential major conflict can break out

[4152] The necessary training of the mobilization departments must therefore become a part of the mobilization itself to a greater extent than is now the case, which must then extend over a longer period before the departments are ready for deployment

[4153] A well-developed plan for how the departments can be trained after they have been set up must therefore become an integrated part of the departments' mobilization plans

[4154] In addition to the fact that such prioritization limits political freedom of action with regard to

[4155] The choice of mobilization time can also have negative consequences for general confidence in the mobilization defense

[4156] It will therefore be an important task to create understanding that prioritizing investments in modern equipment, solid initial service, and training of command and specialist cadres represents the best possible adaptation of the Armed Forces to the economic framework

[4157] It is emphasized that when a relatively high proportion of materiel investment is planned according to international goals, this is only a natural consequence of the Norwegian defense concept, with a small standing defense and a large war structure based on mobilization

[4158] To the extent that it nevertheless becomes necessary to reduce activity related to the initial service, this must also be done in accordance with overall considerations

[4159] In practice, this means that departments that, due to their peacetime role, must have a high level of readiness are prioritized over departments that are purely engaged in force production for the mobilization defense

[4160] This primarily applies to the departments that are earmarked for deployment in NATO's emergency response forces, where the alliance's operational requirements for such forces must be met at all times

[4161] The following guidelines are the basis for the restructuring work

[4162] The basis for the restructuring must be that the Armed Forces be able to solve its primary tasks in a way that satisfies the demands of a modern combat environment

[4163] Necessary considerations must therefore be taken to ensure that the military requirements for the organization and activities of the Armed Forces can be met

[4164] An overarching consideration during the restructuring is to safeguard future freedom of action and flexibility in defense planning

[4165] The defense should therefore be developed in a way that best satisfies this requirement, especially with regard to the recovery of strength and possible alternative defense concepts

[4166] The most important prerequisite for meeting the requirement for operational reductions is to reduce the Armed Forces' personnel consumption

[4167] In this context, the Ministry will seek to utilize the natural and accidental departure of personnel as far as possible

[4168] Dismissal will only be used where it is not possible to redeploy civilian employees who have become redundant as a result of organizational changes

[4169] The Ministry is committed to finding personnel policy measures that can reduce such outcomes to the greatest extent possible, such as retraining to be able to take on new tasks in the Armed Forces or in civilian activities

[4170] However, the Ministry will not use measures such as one-off payments or similar, and will seek measures that ensure that as few people as possible are referred to temporary unemployment benefits

[4171] As part of reducing wage costs, the Ministry, in collaboration with employee organizations, will look at the possibilities for changes to the variable supplements

[4172] In this context, the practice pattern that triggers such additions will also be considered

[4173] The structure of the Norwegian Armed Forces will in the future contain departments and units from all branches of defence earmarked for efforts in NATO's

[4174] Immediate Reaction Force (IRF

[4175] The deployment readiness of these forces, as well as their general importance for both the Alliance's and others' assessment of our defense, dictates that IRF units should have priority over purely national units when allocating resources

[4176] This applies to both the allocation of personnel and materiel, and the necessary training resources to meet the requirements stipulated in the Allied Command Europe Forces Standard and Maritime Forces Standards

[4177] All service at IRF units will be based on a volunteer basis, but both financial and other conditions for service in and outside Norway will be determined and must be accepted by the individual when applying to an IRF unit

[4178] The ability to recover forces over a somewhat longer period of time should be given priority over the ability to immediately mobilize the largest possible war structure

[4179] This means that the areas and sectors that take the longest to rebuild should be shielded from reductions

[4180] In particular, the acquisition of materiel and training of command cadres and specialist categories should be prioritized over crew training for less training-intensive categories and lower-priority departments

[4181] It is emphasized, however, that this concerns force recovery within the framework of the existing defense concept, in contrast to the alternative core or cadre defense described in Chapter 8, which presupposes a reconstruction of the Armed Forces over several years

[4182] In the former case, it primarily concerns training an existing organization, in the latter, major organizational changes, training of new crews, etc. New tasks may be assigned to the Armed Forces where there are significant socio-economic benefits to using the Armed Forces' material and expertise, and where the primary tasks are not significantly affected

[4183] However, tasks that require expertise, material and training that do not already exist in the Armed Forces mean that separate departments must be organized for the purpose

[4184] Both considerations of the Armed Forces' primary tasks and of proper socio-economic management then dictate that both the resources and tasks be allocated to the ministry to which they naturally belong, even where it may be appropriate to use the Armed Forces as an executive body

[4185] This applies especially to areas where the Armed Forces are required to perform tasks that are primarily of a civilian nature

[4186] Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1994-98, for example concerning the transfer of conscripts to other forms of community service

[4187] This principle is reinforced by the fact that a conscription and mobilization defense is in a special position because it is in a continuous state of training, partly at an elementary level

[4188] In this context, a future benefit from streamlining the service has already been realized in the form of a more differentiated service period

[4189] New, civilian-oriented tasks should therefore not govern the organization of the Armed Forces

[4190] A larger support system than that required by optimal utilization of the framework must be maintained, where temporary staffing and net budgeting make it possible for the institutions in question to undertake assignments on a commercial basis, and thereby finance a larger operation

[4191] The restructuring of the Armed Forces should, to the greatest extent possible, take place by removing entire units or departments from the structure, so that the number of garrisons and service locations is significantly reduced

[4192] The remaining departments and units must remain fully operational, capable of contributing to the Armed Forces being able to carry out their assigned tasks

[4193] This consideration is of great importance for both operational efficiency and financial savings opportunities

[4194] This will also include joint solutions across the defence branches to the greatest extent possible

[4195] As a general rule, it is the production tasks of the war structure that determine the size and composition of the peace organization

[4196] However, it may also be considerations of peacekeeping tasks and the need for functional training and education units that in some cases make it necessary to maintain a larger peacekeeping organization than production needs would dictate

[4197] As long as brigades are included in the Army's structure, there will therefore have to be a virtually standing brigade in peacetime, for the sake of developing and maintaining necessary expertise, testing tactical and operational doctrine, etc

[4198] Due consideration must be given to the existing infrastructure in the Armed Forces

[4199] New construction projects should be assessed based on their savings potential

[4200] To the extent that it is possible to bring together multiple activities and units within the same area, this should be strived for

[4201] This is especially true where the branches of defense conduct uniform training independently of each other, such as MP service, medical training, training on common types of equipment, etc

[4202] This includes maximizing the capacity of the camps and garrisons that are to be centers of expertise before new establishments or expansions are made elsewhere

[4203] The possibilities for a joint location of the activities of the Home Guard and the defense branches shall be pursued, in order to achieve the greatest possible rationalization of the Norwegian Defence Forces' peacekeeping activities

[4204] The Armed Forces must also in the future have the ability to be present in all parts of the country

[4205] However, the overall goal of the restructuring of operations and organization should be to make it possible to quickly concentrate the necessary military capacity in Northern Norway

[4206] However, considerations of operational savings and the maintenance development of necessary military expertise will make it expedient to further investigate the distribution of military activities in the respective regions of the country

[4207] In order for the structural changes to be implemented, the Armed Forces must initially be given great freedom of action in the use of instruments in the restructuring process

[4208] It is only when crucial social considerations dictate that this basic rule will be deviated from

[4209] The transformation also requires centralized management of the process in the defense branches, to ensure that the transformation measures are coordinated to the necessary extent

[4210] The Joint Staff of the Armed Forces High Command must therefore be given a more central role in relation to the defense branch staffs

[4211] FREEDOM OF ACTION IN THE LONG TERM

[4212] The great uncertainty about both future political and economic developments and about cost developments in the military area means that Norway may, in the foreseeable future, be forced to undertake a fundamental reassessment of the entire Armed Forces' level of ambition, concept and structure, cf

[4213] This requires that the restructuring takes place in a way that preserves the greatest possible degree of freedom of action in relation to such later assessments

[4214] To support such an assumption, the Armed Forces must significantly increase its ability to plan under uncertainty

[4215] The technical possibilities for this in the form of simulation tools, etc. are already present today, but the Armed Forces' staff capacity to conduct ongoing studies and analyses across the defense branch level must be improved

[4216] Regardless of the decision-making time and choice, however, it would be a correct strategy to dismantle the peace-organization because any conceivable future defense would require fewer personnel and increased material investments, which presupposes reduced operating costs

[4217] Nor will the reductions in the war structure that can be implemented within the planning period be able to significantly weaken freedom of action, as cost developments make a continuous renewal of our entire current defense structure unattainable in the future

[4218] By the middle of the planning period, however, both materiel programs and organizational changes will have progressed to the point where they are in the process of being adapted to a very specific structural goal, based on the security policy, technological and economic assessments that form the basis of the report

[4219] At this point, a decision should ideally be made as to whether to continue to steer towards a balanced national invasion defense in a region of the country, or whether the Armed Forces should be oriented towards a different concept

[4220] Any later decision will therefore have consequences for freedom of action and costs

[4221] This will have the greatest consequences if the structure adopted involves the closure of one or more main sectors

[4222] We may then risk that it will be desirable to close down a sector in which significant resources have recently been invested

[4223] The problem is exacerbated by the fact that the Armed Forces are very close to a threshold value for the current defense concept

[4224] This situation clearly limits the freedom of action that exists with regard to the further development of the Armed Forces

[4225] The inability to implement the investments proposed in the report will therefore lead to the collapse of the concept on which the structural objective is based, with the consequence that other investments and structural measures that have already been implemented lose their justification

[4226] For the Army, this primarily concerns the implementation of the new division concept, which is based on the continuation of an invasion defense in the highest priority areas of the country, and which involves a fundamentally different organizational form and brigade structure, in addition to materiel projects in the artillery and air defense sectors

[4227] For the Navy, it will also be a matter of do-or-die for large parts of the anti-invasion sector, especially in the Coastal Artillery, which has no multipurpose potential in relation to challenges other than a major invasion

[4228] During the same period, a decision must also be made regarding the acquisition of a new fighter aircraft after the year 2000, and investment in new escort vessels for the Navy

[4229] A decision to align the Armed Forces with a different defense concept can be made at the earliest in connection with the submission of the next long-term report for the Armed Forces

[4230] The basis for decision-making must therefore be prepared during the period

[4231] However, the reduction of both the peace organization and the war structure that is necessary in any case, combined with the prevailing political and economic uncertainty, makes it desirable to postpone the decision as long as possible

[4232] This could mean, among other things, that international political developments will enter a clearer track and thus improve the basis for decision-making

[4233] The Ministry will therefore carefully assess those investment projects and organizational changes that are sensitive in relation to the choice of defense concept

[4234] As part of this work, it may be appropriate to postpone decisions until the next long-term report

[4235] However, if the necessary material investments to realize the FK-90 structure cannot be achieved, and we wait with the decision beyond 1995-98, any further postponement will result in reduced freedom of action, and the final structure will be weakened as a result

[4236] If we wait too long, our departments will eventually completely lose the ability to fight a modernly equipped adversary

[4237] Instead, they will have to make the type of adaptation of tactics and operational patterns described in Chapter 8, which involves a gradual transition to a pure guerrilla strategy

[4238] Guerrilla defense thus appears to be what is indirectly chosen by not making another decision in time, see section 8.3.3. If the proposed structure cannot be realized initially and it is then decided at a later date to make up for lost time, this is uncomplicated in relation to the structural development in the meantime

[4239] However, it will have an increasing cost effect and require very large budget increases if the losses are to be made up over a limited number of years

[4240] To illustrate this, it can be mentioned that it would require a budget growth of just over 8 percent per year for four years to compensate for the volume loss by a reduction of 2 percent per year over five years plus one year of zero growth

[4241] If the reduction is increased to 3 percent per year for five years followed by one year of zero growth, budgets must be increased by 12 percent per year over a four-year period

[4242] DEVELOPMENT OF THE MILITARY STRUCTURE

[4243] Chapter 6 discusses the Norwegian Armed Forces' wartime structure

[4244] In the following, the Ministry will explain in more detail which specific organizational changes and operational measures must be implemented to achieve this wartime structure

[4245] The discussion will be limited to general organizational measures and key operational factors

[4246] The development of the war structure will be the most decisive and determining factor for the downsizing and restructuring process that must take place within the Armed Forces' overall peacekeeping apparatus

[4247] This war structure will affect both the size and scope of the command and control apparatus, and the number and size of the other elements required to maintain the war structure

[4248] The overarching principle for the development of the Armed Forces is to ensure a war structure that satisfies the minimum qualitative requirements that a future combat environment entails

[4249] The quality of the armed forces is therefore determined by operational requirements, while the economy primarily affects size

[4250] The share of the budget for capital investments is expected to increase significantly during the period

[4251] It must be assumed that a lower materiel investment share than just over 30 percent in the future will mean an insufficient renewal of the war structure's materiel, and the creation of an investment backlog

[4252] This will, within a few years, result in a structure with an imbalance between quality and quantity

[4253] The war structure as described in Chapter 6 indicates which sectors can be retained and which may have to be closed under different assumptions about the future economy

[4254] Future material investments should therefore only be made in sectors that will exist in the long term

[4255] Both our own studies and analyses conducted in other countries indicate that the most time-consuming part of any force reconstruction is the acquisition and phasing in of new equipment, especially if entire categories of technically and operationally advanced equipment have been phased out (fighter aircraft, submarines, tanks, etc

[4256] Advanced military equipment has a very long acquisition time, and depending on the degree of complexity, it could take from 2-10 years to acquire such equipment

[4257] If the international situation indicates that many countries will demand the same defense equipment, it may prove very difficult or impossible to obtain, and prices will likely rise with demand

[4258] It could also take just as long to regain the technical and operational expertise required to use the equipment effectively

[4259] This is considerably longer than it takes to train new crews in their functions, or to train mobilization departments to a credible standard

[4260] In the development of the war structure, material procurement must therefore be protected, and any failure in resource access must, as far as possible, be borne by the operating budget

[4261] Training the necessary number of specialists and commanders at all levels to create a certain cadre must then be ensured at the expense of training and refresher training of larger forces in purely national defense

[4262] Strength recovery in the somewhat longer term (6-12 months) thus takes priority over the ability to mobilize in the very short term

[4263] This is also in accordance with the security policy situation, which indicates that a major war scenario is unlikely, and will require a long preparation time in other countries as well

[4264] As a consequence of security policy developments in Europe, increasing emphasis is now being placed on the ability to act jointly politically and militarily, both in NATO and in the CSCE and UN contexts

[4463] Overall objectives and priorities

[4464] The Armed Forces' materiel management will face major and demanding challenges in the restructuring process the Armed Forces is entering

[4465] In the coming years, the Norwegian Armed Forces' equipment fleet will be adapted to a new structure, while the equipment's contribution to combat capability will be optimized within the framework set by this new structure

[4466] The report assumes that the relative share of materiel investments in the defense budget will be increased in the years ahead to achieve the recommended structure

[4467] In order to get more effect from the investment volume, the Ministry of Defence has initiated work to further develop methods and management instruments that enable the Defence to handle and manage its investment projects in a better and more rational way than before

[4468] A higher materiel investment share will also have consequences for how future operational reductions in the Armed Forces will be implemented

[4469] An increase in the volume of equipment investment depends on the equipment sector being shielded to a certain extent from operational reductions

[4470] The introduction of new, possibly updated, material raises personnel requirements both in terms of numbers and, not least, competence

[4472] Nevertheless, there will be a strong focus on cost-effectiveness in the Armed Forces' management of the resources made available for material purposes, whether these are used for investment or for operation and maintenance

[4473] The efficiency and rationalization process that has been initiated within a number of areas of material management will be continued and intensified

[4474] Investments that result in reduced operating expenses will be prioritized

[4476] To ensure optimal utilization of available resources, higher efficiency and reliability, and reduced life cycle costs, the Armed Forces will adopt new working methods and technology in the implementation of its procurements

[4501] Close cooperation between the Armed Forces and Norwegian defense-related industry and business will often be a prerequisite for obtaining materiel with qualities adapted to Norwegian conditions

[4521] The rationalization of materiel management in the Armed Forces will continue with high priority during the period

[4604] Infrastructure cooperation within NATO faces extensive challenges in terms of adapting to requirements resulting from new military strategies, but also from a growing environmental awareness within member states

[4605] In addition to the fact that new types of needs can be covered by infrastructure funds, there is uncertainty about the level of investment

[4606] A significant reduction in the budget framework for the infrastructure program has taken place

[4607] The situation for long-term planning is complicated by the fact that financial frameworks are no longer set for several years at a time

[4608] For Norway, it is a challenge to ensure continued financing of projects already underway in Norway, and to ensure adequate maintenance of the property stock in the future

[4609] Norway will work actively within NATO to ensure that the future infrastructure program takes on a form and scope that is most beneficial to the alliance, while also reasonably accommodating Norwegian interests

[4612] This has led to certain projects being implemented based on the desire for the lowest possible investment costs

[4613] The creation of an overarching resource management committee will enable a much more external and holistic assessment of various projects

[4614] At the same time, the aim is to work on new purchasing processes and systems, which will to a greater extent meet the need for standardization, spare parts supply, warranty schemes, etc

[4621] For smaller areas that may not fall under the impact assessment provisions in the Planning and Building Act, the need for assessment will be addressed through guidelines for environmental assessments in the planning process

[4622] For larger areas of regional importance, interests must be weighed and coordinated through county planning

[4627] If units are relocated or merged, this may in some places entail new space requirements that must be resolved by preparing spatial plans and acquiring land

[4628] Efforts will be made to ensure that such issues are clarified strategically through overall plans

[4629] Operation and maintenance

[4630] The Ministry of Defence has a goal of reducing operating expenses for construction and civil engineering to a level that will be approximately 25 percent lower in

[4631] With a view to reducing the costs of operating buildings and facilities, the Ministry envisages that the following measures could have an effect in the years to come

[4632] Phasing out/disposal of redundant, older, obsolete and maintenance-intensive real estate

[4634] At the same time, a consistent disposal of real estate must be carried out in order for the savings goals to be achieved

[4636] Increased useful life of buildings and facilities through improved maintenance, thereby alleviating the pressure of demands for new buildings and facilities

[4637] Decisions about increased service life can only be made after careful overall economic assessments to clarify the profitability of such priorities

[4638] Lowering operating costs through significantly more efficient energy use in the Armed Forces' buildings and facilities than is the case today

[4640] Lowering operating expenses through a continuous process of renegotiating agreements for the supply of electrical power

[4655] Target and performance management

[4656] Through the state renewal program "The New State", the government has put performance management on the agenda

[4657] This management philosophy concentrates management tasks on getting the most out of resources and achieving the goals set by the Storting for government activities

[4658] Report no. 54 (1987-88) heralded a turning point in the management of the Armed Forces' resources with a strong emphasis on internal efficiency

[4659] It was expressed that the Armed Forces, with its extensive structure and relatively centralized system, would face extensive restructuring in order to implement a transition to management by objectives and results

[4660] Implementation had to take place gradually and in line with the organization's ability to adopt and utilize the new management system

[4661] Through productivity-enhancing measures and result-oriented business plans, the goal was to achieve increased productivity, rationalization and efficiency

[4662] The introduction of performance management means that the nature of financial management is expanded from an accounting perspective to focus on decision-making processes and results

[4663] Major projects have been initiated to improve financial management and make the Armed Forces a target- and results-driven enterprise

[4664] The process will take place over a 5-year period

[4665] Given the challenges facing the Armed Forces in terms of resources made available and their utilization, it is absolutely crucial that financial management is put on the agenda and prioritized

[4666] DEFENCE MANAGEMENT CONCEPT

[4667] The purpose of introducing performance management in the Armed Forces is to achieve better resource utilization

[4668] The requirements of this form of governance revealed that the Armed Forces' organization, accounting system and reporting routines were not adapted to a new way of governing

[4669] The organization is divided into levels with unclear lines of responsibility, allocation, and follow-up

[4670] The accounting system is divided into categories, which makes it difficult to record results and follow up

[4671] To remedy these problems, the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces High Command have jointly developed a comprehensive concept for managing the Armed Forces' total resources in peacetime

[4672] The concept links goals and resource consumption by focusing on the connection between external framework conditions, performance targets, resource allocation and performance monitoring

[4673] The business plans will be a key tool in the internal performance management for the individual business

[4674] The concept consists of four principles and a governance model that elaborates on the consequences of the principles

[4675] They are set out and described in various official reports such as "The New State" and Parliamentary Proposal No. 53 (1990-91) "On certain organizational changes etc. in the Armed Forces

[4676] The overarching principles are

[4677] clarify responsibility and authority - delegate responsibility and authority as far as is appropriate - ensure that responsibility and authority are followed - enforce responsibility

[4678] The governance model is based on the Armed Forces' overall goals and the desired effects and end products of the Armed Forces' activities

[4679] Results monitoring assumes that it is possible to describe how resources are used

[4680] The model requires a precise definition of value creation in the Armed Forces, which elements are included and how these are interconnected

[4681] Value creation is made visible through the products and services that are produced

[4682] These must be able to be quantified or assessed qualitatively in a systematic manner

[4683] Another key element is a clarification of responsibility and authority

[4684] There should be a unified management line, and resources should follow the missions

[4685] Figure 1 shows the management lines today, with many uncoordinated lines from the ministry to different levels in the organization

[4686] A clean-up along these lines is an absolutely necessary condition for being able to place responsibility

[4687] Through this principle, one will highlight and define influenceable responsibility for resource use

[4688] In this regard, one must also define the relationships between the various units in value creation, because the interaction affects resource use

[4689] This applies to the relationship between superior and subordinate, and the relationship between primary activities (activities that contribute directly to solving the Armed Forces' tasks, e.g. operational and educational departments) and support activities (activities that produce goods and services for the Armed Forces' primary activities, e.g. administrations, joint institutions, workshops, etc

[4690] The implementation of the management concept is a prerequisite for the Ministry and the Armed Forces to be able to follow up on the long-term report, and to improve financial management in the Armed Forces in general

[4696] Systematic management towards goals requires a systematized division of goals and tasks

[4697] The four main goals outlined in Chapter 4.7 are primarily of importance when determining what the Armed Forces will produce and for analyzing afterwards whether the actual production was in accordance with the goals

[4698] Internally, value creation in the organization, the production side, will therefore be the management focus

[4699] The planning system and the annual business plans determine the tasks to be carried out during the year

[4701] The assignments are specified in a number of activities to be carried out

[4702] The results of the activities carried out are expressed as products

[4703] Through the assignments with the associated activities that are carried out, the direct resource consumption can be attributed to the products and followed up

[4704] The products are grouped and geared towards the results that the Storting expects from the Armed Forces' activities and that are stated in the tasks derived from the Armed Forces' target structure

[4705] By linking costs directly and indirectly to products, it is possible to link costs to goals

[4706] Only then will there be a basis for real political prioritization in the use of the Armed Forces' resources

[4707] This will strengthen political governance
