[4722] Management roles

[4723] Management responsibility The management concept for the Armed Forces necessitates that the management roles in all parts of the Armed Forces be clarified from the Ministry of Defence downwards

[4724] Management roles must be linked to real opportunities to influence at the various levels

[4725] Responsibility for achieving results and using resources must be defined accordingly

[4726] In connection with this, an assessment must be made of which functions must be managed centrally, and which can be delegated

[4727] Authority should be delegated to the extent appropriate

[4728] The Ministry of Defence's subordinate units shall be carried out at an overall strategic level

[4729] This means that the ministry must govern by clarifying goals and providing guidelines based on a balancing of military professional assessments and the overall societal interests that are affected

[4730] The Ministry shall determine the main features of the organization, personnel management and financial management of subordinate units

[4731] The Ministry's responsibility for operational management shall be safeguarded through an overall control function

[4732] This means that the ministry will conduct performance monitoring by following up on results and deviations in relation to long-term goals and political guidelines

[4733] By emphasizing the strategic management of subordinate units, the ministry will be strengthened as a secretariat for the political leadership

[4734] Being a secretariat for the political leadership means that the Ministry shall assist the Prime Minister and the Government in - studying and preparing - designing and formulating - implementing and carrying out - following up and controlling - adjusting and adapting the policy the Government wishes to pursue

[4735] The division of labor between the ministry and the military organization has similarities to a corporate model

[4736] The Minister of Defence has governance responsibility on behalf of the Government, with the Ministry as his staff, and shall ensure strategic management

[4737] The Chief of Defence, with the Armed Forces High Command as his staff, is responsible for implementing the policy that is determined in interaction with the ministry by proposing cost-effective and result-oriented solutions based on political guidelines and allocated resource frameworks

[4738] Such a clarification of roles and responsibilities in the management of the Armed Forces' activities and resources is a key requirement in the management concept

[4739] There should be a unified line of command between superiors and subordinates in the organization

[4740] This implies clear management from the ministry to the underlying units

[4741] Each level of leadership in the Armed Forces will have its respective roles defined in the same way

[4742] Overall management in the Armed Forces shall be of a coarse-grained nature

[4743] It is intended to ensure real management of the Armed Forces' critically important value creation from top to bottom in the organization

[4744] Requirements must be set and followed up

[4745] The management of the Armed Forces' primary activities shall primarily take place in a vertical superior/subordinate relationship

[4746] In the management of the Armed Forces' support activities, the use of resources will be made visible through horizontal trade, i.e. the client orders and receives goods and services that are charged to its own budget

[4747] The content of the vertical control will depend on the freedom of action the subordinate is given

[4748] The goal is to delegate authority so that the freedom to choose means and production methods is as great as possible without the supervisor losing significant influence on the results

[4749] Determining the degree of freedom, what results are to be achieved, what financial frameworks are to apply and how the results are to be followed up, are agreed upon in an annual management dialogue

[4750] Framework conditions are management signals of a more general and lasting nature that it is not natural to specify each time as part of the management dialogue

[4751] In addition to laws and general directives, these could include general norms for staffing and equipment of operational departments, requirements for standardization of equipment, requirements for security, uniforms and norms for welfare services

[4752] Vertical management will characterize the management of both the primary business and, to some extent, the support business

[4753] In primary activities, the performance requirements from supervisors will largely be directed towards specific characteristics of the value creation/production to be carried out

[4754] For support units, the requirements will be more focused on the quality/effect of the services provided to other departments, i.e. user satisfaction

[4755] For both types of businesses, it will also be relevant to set requirements for internal development in the department, for example productivity growth, building up expertise, etc

[4756] One of the challenges in improving governance is to ensure that support functions are maintained through cross-organizational communication and that this communication can contribute effectively to the achievement of overall goals

[4757] Demand mechanisms or horizontal trade refer to the relationship between different support units, and between support units and the primary activity

[4758] It is essential for effective management that the interests of the primary business are put in focus here and that these give assignments directly to the support units

[4759] An important tool for ensuring coordination and cost-effective utilization of resources in horizontal trade is the pricing of internal deliveries

[4760] This means that the user is charged for the goods and services he receives

[4761] By charging the user, he will be motivated to critically assess the use of resources and strive for efficient utilization of them

[4762] The delivery department, on the other hand, is forced to focus on fulfilling the user's wants and needs

[4763] Organizational changes The changes that come as a consequence of both the restructuring process and the new form of governance are in many ways a cultural revolution in the Armed Forces

[4764] Completely different and new demands are placed on the attitudes and behavior of employees at all levels in the organization

[4765] The only way the organization can achieve the goal of the changes and achieve better governance is through collaboration from top to bottom

[4766] The armed forces' personnel are consistently well motivated, and this is reflected in a strong corps spirit

[4767] This is a good starting point for the further development of organization and management methods

[4768] The introduction of goal- and results-oriented leadership and management in the Armed Forces has revealed unfortunate aspects of the established and traditional lines of responsibility and authority, planning routines, resource allocation lines and reporting systems

[4769] The management concept's assumptions of clearly defined management roles and unified management lines between the levels of the organization require that both the Ministry and the Chief of Defence clear up the lines of responsibility and adapt the organizational structure

[4770] This pressure is further reinforced by the demands for a goal- and results-oriented organization that are outlined in Parliamentary Proposal No. 53 (1990-91) "On certain organizational changes, etc. in the Armed Forces", and which are demands that the Storting has endorsed

[4771] This is also reflected in the existing strategies to achieve consistency between structure and access to resources

[4772] Some measures have been implemented, but significant organizational changes still remain

[4773] The consequences of not carrying out such a cleanup are major

[4774] Unclear lines of responsibility lead to poor governance

[4775] It will be impossible to fulfill the political requirement to make the Armed Forces a goal- and results-oriented organization where responsibility for resource use can be made visible and enforced

[4776] The consequence will be an organizational structure more or less similar to the existing one with unclear lines of management and responsibility

[4777] Organizational arrangements must be made to ensure that real cross-prioritization and coordinated resource allocation can be carried out between operational, force-producing and administrative activities

[4778] Therefore, the Storting decided, following the government's proposal that the defense-specific supply commands, the Armed Forces Joint Material Service (FFMT) and the Armed Forces Medical Services/Materials (FSAN/Materials) would be subordinated to the Chief of Defense from 1 January

[4779] Work is continuing to assess the organizational and management form, tasks and responsibilities for the administrations and joint institutions that are still subordinate to the ministry

[4780] The organizational and management structure should be developed so that it enables the organization to quickly change priorities and deploy resources where the need is greatest

[4781] The organization's ability to plan under uncertainty must be strengthened and the number of levels in the organization must be critically assessed

[4782] The organization should also be made less top-heavy

[4783] This means an assessment of the procedures for promotion and advancement

[4784] The Joint Staff of the Armed Forces High Command shall be strengthened and made more effective

[4785] It must be enabled to manage cross-prioritization within the given framework conditions and to manage the real management of the allocated resources

[4786] In terms of career, serving in the joint staff must become more attractive

[4787] In line with this, the Chief of Defence has carried out a clarification of the responsibilities and authority relationships within the Defence Forces' top management

[4788] This concerns responsibility and authority for resource management in peace

[4789] In accordance with the management concept's requirements for coordination and cross-prioritization of resource use, the Joint Staff in the Armed Forces High Command shall be responsible for all long-term planning

[4790] The executive responsibility for implementing the decisions in the budget year shall be based on a continuation of the current practice with the Inspectors General as the central link

[4791] Final clarification and specification of responsibilities between the joint staff and the defense border staffs remains

[4792] The Ministry requires that this clarification contribute to strengthening the joint staff's basis for planning and cross-prioritization

[4793] The Ministry of Defense is working to adapt its organization to the role of agency manager

[4794] The Ministry will be strengthened as a secretariat for the Prime Minister

[4795] This requires an organization based on the management role and management function that the Ministry should have towards subordinate units in a goal- and results-oriented organization, cf. section 10.4. The Ministry of Defence has appointed a committee to assess instruments for personnel reductions in the Armed Forces

[4796] The proposal was submitted in the summer

[4797] The committee is also working on an assessment of where responsibility and authority for personnel management in the Armed Forces should be placed based on the requirements of the management concept

[4798] Central management of all functions in personnel management is contrary to the principle in the management concept of delegating responsibility and authority as far as is appropriate

[4799] The Ministry will therefore consider how the Armed Forces' personnel management can be adapted to the management concept as soon as the committee's recommendation is available

[4800] The Ministry has also appointed a committee to assess the tasks and future organization of the financial and financial accounting service in the Armed Forces, which is currently handled by the Norwegian Defence Accounting Centre

[4801] The recommendation will be available by the end of the year

[4802] ACTIONS

[4803] AND PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT The Armed Forces' overall goals and other political management signals form the basis for the preparation of the Chief of Defence's financial and strategic plans

[4804] These plans are the starting point for the annual budget process and ongoing follow-up

[4805] The internal business plan that expresses the missions, performance targets, activities and budget is the basis for performance management in the individual department

[4806] In order for management at all levels to receive the necessary management information, good follow-up and information systems are required

[4807] These will be based on a number of common elements, making it possible to make comparisons, prepare analyses, assess results and resource use, etc. at a general level

[4808] Clear allocation of responsibility requires a system for how individuals are either rewarded or subject to sanctions in relation to the results achieved

[4809] Here there must be a close connection between the best interests of the individual and the organization

[4810] The means may be in the form of service statements, promotion policy, use of salary or reassignment of personnel

[4811] In addition, the Ministry will work to improve the conditions for exercising leadership in the Armed Forces, including by adjusting the framework conditions for education, reviewing the use of special agreements and strengthening the management level at the departments

[4812] In this regard, the finance function should be given a different status and priority than it has today

[4813] Today, the budget and government accounts are in focus in relation to systems and routines for follow-up and control

[4814] This can only be used for retrospective analysis of what has happened

[4815] The new routines and systems for performance management that are being established will place focus on decisions about the allocation of funds and resources

[4816] The Armed Forces must ensure that a procurement is appropriate before it is carried out, that overall design has been carried out, and that alternative resource uses have been considered before the resource is consumed

[4817] The criterion for determining at what level the decision must be made is therefore the whole in which the product is part

[4818] Whoever has sufficient authority to influence the overall outcome to the best advantage of the Armed Forces should make the most important decisions

[4819] This is in line with the overarching principle of delegating authority as far as is appropriate

[4820] Other measures include reviewing, simplifying and adapting instructions, agreements and regulations to a results-oriented and delegated management system

[4821] A leadership policy will be established to ensure that the Armed Forces have leaders who are motivated and prepared to take responsibility for results

[4822] Skills development and a new management salary system combined with measurable performance requirements are tools in this regard

[4823] DEFENCE PLAN

[4824] AND BUDGET PROCESS

[4825] The Armed Forces' planning process shall ensure targeted and resource-efficient management of allocated and anticipated resources in a sufficiently long-term perspective

[4826] The planning process is effective when, through a balance between structure and activity, consistency is achieved between objectives, allocation of funds, distribution and use of resources and the results achieved

[4827] Especially in tight budget constraints, an effective planning process as a basis for achieving results is of utmost importance

[4828] The Ministry has traditionally had little involvement in the Armed Forces' internal planning

[4829] This has led to the planning system having lived too much of its own life and not being able to capture political signals to a sufficient extent

[4830] As a consequence of this, there has been a significant discrepancy between the Armed Forces' internal planning and the resource reality

[4831] The Armed Forces' internal planning system is the central instrument for the Chief of Defence in managing the Armed Forces

[4832] It is therefore important that political requirements and guidelines are reflected in this plan and that it reflects realistic economic frameworks

[4833] The Ministry must therefore become more involved in the Armed Forces' internal planning by providing a framework and premises for its design

[4834] This also applies to defense studies that are conducted at regular intervals

[4835] The Chief of Defence will plan and lead the development and activities of the Armed Forces in accordance with the principles described

[4836] New governance and management will entail increased authority and responsibility for managers at all levels for the management of allocated financial resources, the use of other resources and for achieving results

[4837] It is a shared responsibility for the political and military leadership to facilitate an effective planning process by contributing to

[4838] the most concrete long-term political goals and requirements for results, - the greatest possible consistency between the allocation of annual appropriations and long-term performance targets, and - that the specific measures can be implemented in accordance with the assumptions in the plan

[4839] It is a prerequisite that the planning system provides flexibility to management by capturing changes

[4840] In recent times, security policy changes have occurred very rapidly

[4841] The Armed Forces must also expect considerable uncertainty regarding resource allocation and other framework conditions

[4842] The Chief of Defence is therefore in the process of strengthening his ability to continuously analyse the consequences of such changes, thereby improving the organisation's ability to plan under uncertainty

[4843] Planning under uncertainty means that senior management ensures freedom of action and agency in the planning process, including by strengthening cross-prioritization in the documents

[4844] The Norwegian Armed Forces' internal strategic plan is expressed in the Chief of Defence's Dok 1 (Perspective Plan) and Dok 2 (Programme Plan) with 18 and 6 year planning periods, respectively

[4845] The documents are internal management documents in the Armed Forces, in which the Chief of Defence sets specific long-term goals, instruments and milestones for the overall activities

[4846] The documents describe how the Chief of Defence will steer towards resource-efficient goal achievement

[4847] To reflect the entirety of the Armed Forces' activities, the documents also deal with planned resource use at the administrations and joint institutions that are currently subordinate to the Ministry of Defence in accordance with the Chief of Defence's directive authority

[4848] Given its long-term nature, Document 1 will be general in form and content

[4849] As the Armed Forces' structural plan, it will describe the starting point, main course and specific goals in the development

[4850] This means that DOK 1 is normally updated every 5 years, but it should be updated continuously and published as needed if the defense policy reality changes, or if long-term resource allocation or performance requirements for the Armed Forces change

[4851] Such changes and adjustments are normally regulated in the government's long-term reports for the Armed Forces

[4852] To the extent that such changes are anticipated, relevant impact assessments and associated defense studies will be conducted prior to or in parallel with the development of a long-term report

[4853] A defense study and a long-term report, as well as perspectives from the Ministry, would therefore ideally provide the main basis for the preparation of the Chief of Defense's DOK

[4854] DOK 2 will also in the future be an annual rolling plan with a planning period of 6 years

[4855] It will be based on the current DOK 1, guidelines from the ministry, other changes in framework conditions and new requirements for results

[4856] DOK 2 has its financial basis in allocations the year before the first year of the planning period

[4857] The document will, more specifically than DOK 1, account for the Chief of Defence's long-term performance targets for the years in the planning period

[4858] Adjustments in relation to 1's cross-prioritization between operational, force-producing and administrative activities are made in DOK

[4859] Based on this, control signals are given from the Chief of Defence to subordinate units and directives to the units that are currently under the control of the FD

[4860] Ongoing development of DOK 2 consists of an integration and concretization of the Armed Forces' performance targets in relation to the budget

[4861] The guidelines and performance targets from DOK 2 are incorporated into the budget directive

[4862] This forms the basis for the Chief of Defence's annual planning

[4863] Through the budget process, resources are allocated in relation to these performance targets

[4864] The final budget becomes the most important management instrument between the ministry and subordinate units

[4865] The allocation letter to subordinate units reflects this

[4868] The annual costs of following up on the investment programs are assessed in relation to the allocations to the Armed Forces for the individual year

[4869] Both centrally and locally, budgets will be focused to a much lesser extent than previously on individual input factors (cost types

[4910] The Armed Forces and Society 11.1 SOCIETY CONTACT AND

[4911] INFORMATION Maintaining a credible Norwegian defense requires broad support among the population

[4912] In a country based on conscription, this places a number of demands on public relations, information and transparency

[4913] The total defense concept remains in place

[4914] The Armed Forces need well-developed public relations both to capture feedback, to disseminate knowledge and to provide information about plans and measures

[4915] There is a need for active information about the Total Defence Force and the importance of non-military preparedness measures for the country's overall defence capability

[4916] Interaction with voluntary organizations has been a tool here

[4917] These organizations receive annual support from the defense budget for their activities

[4918] For the 1993 budget, a total of NOK 36 million has been allocated to 23 voluntary organizations

[4919] The Ministry has initiated work to assess the criteria for support to the organizations

[4920] This work is expected to be completed

[4921] Emphasis will be placed on following up on FK90's recommendation

[4922] FK90 stated that this cooperation should also include groups that have traditionally had an alternative view of Norwegian defense and security policy

[4923] The Norwegian Armed Forces base the development of its information activities on the following principles

[4924] Credibility Transparency Speed

[4925] The biggest challenge is to create understanding for a defense adapted to the new security policy situation

[4926] Furthermore, the need for a comprehensive restructuring of the Armed Forces must be explained

[4927] In a time without clear fronts and threats, it is important to maintain the will to defend, support for total defense, and understanding of necessary military dispositions and measures

[4928] Such understanding can best be achieved through greater openness and better access to relevant information, both about the actual military situation in Norway's immediate vicinity and the main features of Norwegian defense planning

[4929] A separate information strategy has been prepared for the Armed Forces' restructuring

[4930] The Armed Forces are facing a comprehensive restructuring process to adapt their structure and operations to lower resource constraints

[4931] The transition will take several years

[4932] It will require agility and drive to bring about comprehensive changes, which will include both organizational changes in the form of geographical relocation, closures and personnel reductions

[4933] A new management philosophy must be incorporated (see Chapter 10), and extensive and fundamental work must be done to add knowledge, change attitudes and behavior

[4934] The Government places great emphasis on employee safety and participation in restructuring in state-owned enterprises

[4935] Security is achieved through open planning processes where goals and consequences are known as far as possible, and through predictability with regard to mobility requirements

[4936] Such security is created, among other things, by providing information at the earliest possible point in the planning process and by using the information actively and purposefully in the subsequent process

[4937] The goal must be to create as much security as possible during the transition

[4938] If the transition information is to function satisfactorily, it will require a targeted action plan from the Armed Forces, in which leaders at different levels are trained in fulfilling their information responsibilities

[4939] This represents a major challenge for the Armed Forces, and appears to be crucial for a successful transition

[4940] Need for information technology expertise

[4941] If the Armed Forces are to be able to meet the new information challenges, the organization must be provided with information expertise in its press and information units

[4942] The main emphasis today is on media contact

[4943] This is unfortunate, especially in a situation where information challenges, particularly internally, are greater than ever

[4944] The Ministry of Defence will take initiatives to ensure that the Armed Forces have information technology expertise

[4945] Furthermore, emphasis will be placed on strengthening internal information in the Armed Forces

[4950] Intelligence activities related to research, product development, financial management, etc. will hardly be reduced to the same extent as is the case for purely military intelligence activities, where a reduction has been registered

[4951] In order to adapt the security requirements to a sober and realistic level in accordance with current technical and political developments, internal work has been initiated to assess the premises for secrecy

[4952] It must be assessed which information, in the context of total defense, must be protected for the sake of national security regardless of changing external conditions, and the harmful effects of any compromise must be assessed

[4953] Existing laws and directives will be assessed taking into account Norwegian obligations towards alliance partners and concluded agreements on arms control and disarmament

[4958] A preliminary project to design a study of the intelligence staff's activities in the period from

[4959] The Oversight Committee for the Surveillance and Security Service will conduct an investigation into the allegations of illegal wiretapping activities in the Armed Forces Intelligence Service

[4962] The measures will also provide a basis for considering any new guidelines for employees' political activities

[4966] RISK EFFECTS OF THE DEFENCE'S ORDINARY MILITARY ACTIVITIES

[4967] The breadth of the Armed Forces' activities has many ripple effects on civil society

[4968] The activity has great significance for regional politics, and for a number of municipalities, dependence on the Armed Forces' activities is essential for maintaining employment and public and private services

[4969] The restructuring of the Armed Forces' organization and activities will necessarily affect defense-dependent municipalities

[4970] In a societal context, the Armed Forces' activities are primarily focused on managing the resources made available by society in accordance with the defense policy goals that the Storting has endorsed

[4971] The defense appropriations will therefore be used primarily with a view to maintaining a strong national defense that contributes to preventing war, and to protecting Norway's freedom of action and ability to assert its own rights and interests

[4972] The resources allocated to the Armed Forces have therefore mainly been directed towards the Armed Forces' purely military function

[4973] However, the Storting has also ordered the Armed Forces to perform tasks of a more civilian nature

[4974] This primarily applies to tasks such as coast guard and rescue services

[4975] The government believes that the Armed Forces should continue to provide support in connection with disasters, major accidents and major national events

[4976] The Armed Forces can also provide assistance to the police in peacetime

[4977] This is stipulated in separate provisions

[4978] It has long been a goal for the Armed Forces to be able to provide such extensive support to civil society that is compatible with fulfilling the main tasks described

[4979] The Armed Forces represent an organization and expertise that can also make valuable contributions to the rest of society

[4980] The question in the new situation is what possible new tasks, and by extension what function, the Armed Forces should be given in addition to the tasks already assigned to the Armed Forces

[4981] The Government advocates that the Armed Forces should be assigned civilian tasks, and in this context will take into account whether these can be carried out in a socially more affordable manner by the Armed Forces, without the primary activities being significantly harmed

[4982] It is a prerequisite that the administrative principles in "A better organized state" are applied, see section 11.4.2. Employment/settlement/tax base

[4983] Military activity is not distributed evenly across the country

[4984] In relation to the population of Northern Norway, a large part of the Armed Forces' activities are therefore allocated to this part of the country

[4985] The armed forces are therefore of great importance for settlement, employment and other activities in a number of municipalities and local communities, particularly in Northern Norway, but also in certain places in Southern Norway

[4986] The regional political significance is often reinforced by the fact that the Armed Forces' establishments are located in areas with scattered settlements and rather poorly developed business and industry

[4987] A reduction in the Armed Forces' activities in municipalities that are particularly dependent on defence will, in the short term, inevitably lead to the loss of jobs directly related to the Armed Forces and some relocation as a result of a reduction in the number of conscripts and a general reduction in demand for goods and services both locally and regionally

[4988] In isolation, this could lead to reduced employment in other businesses and thus a reduction in municipal tax revenues

[4989] Reducing public services could also lead to further emigration in the long term

[4990] Resources that are linked to the Armed Forces' activities today (buildings, areas, labor, etc.) could have alternative uses in other locally based activities

[4991] However, this depends on regional conditions, such as population and industry structure

[4992] The effects of a reduction in the activities of the Armed Forces could be compensated by an increase in other public activities and/or by stimulating increased private activities

[4993] The actual effects will primarily be largely up to the municipalities themselves, in light of which measures and projects they can initiate or launch

[4994] There will undoubtedly be a need for special measures in areas that are particularly affected by reduced activities in the Armed Forces

[4995] The Armed Forces' schools provide education primarily to meet the Armed Forces' needs for qualified personnel

[5042] Coordination of military and civilian air routes The traffic base for the civilian air routes, especially in Northern Norway, is relatively modest and has yielded poor earnings

[5043] It has therefore been argued on several occasions that the traffic base should be increased by closing the fixed military charter routes and by transferring Armed Forces personnel to civilian scheduled flights as far as possible

[5047] The commercial significance of the Armed Forces' procurement of materiel, buildings and facilities The Armed Forces' nationwide activities also have beneficial spin-off effects of an commercial nature

[5048] The Armed Forces' procurement of goods, equipment and services makes a significant contribution to maintaining a diverse business community in many parts of the country

[5049] This applies particularly to economically weak areas in rural Norway

[5050] Procurement activities in the Armed Forces are very extensive

[5051] For the 1992 budget period, a total of approximately NOK 14.2 billion was allocated for new investments in equipment, buildings and structures, and the procurement of goods and services

[5052] Of this, just under NOK 5.5 billion was investments in new equipment and approximately NOK 3.2 billion

[5053] NOK procurement of goods and services related to the operation of equipment

[5054] Just over NOK 1 billion was allocated for investments in nationally financed buildings and facilities, while just under NOK 1.3 billion went to jointly financed buildings and facilities

[5055] In addition to the above, there are other procurements of goods and services for the Armed Forces' daily operations, amounting to around NOK 3.5 billion

[5056] Procurement activities are of great importance to Norwegian business

[5057] In many cases, it also has a decisive impact on both employment and the economic structure of many local communities

[5058] Not least, the Armed Forces' operating expenses are used to a significant extent locally and regionally in the departments' purchases of goods and services

[5059] Investments in equipment are made by the central administrations with both Norwegian and foreign suppliers

[5060] Norwegian businesses also benefit from the larger acquisitions that take place abroad by entering into buyback agreements that ensure significant deliveries from and transfer of advanced technology to Norwegian companies

[5061] This collaboration in turn forms the basis for the establishment of strategic alliances between Norwegian and foreign industry

[5062] In the long term, this could give Norwegian companies the opportunity to participate in the development and production of advanced equipment both for defense purposes and for use in the civilian sector

[5063] Approximately 29 percent of the Armed Forces' operating expenses are spent in Northern Norway

[5064] This is also a regional pattern that corresponds roughly to the employment distribution in the Armed Forces

[5065] The central Eastern Norway region (Oslo, Akershus, Østfold and Vestfold) has a similarly large share, approximately 29 percent, of the Armed Forces' total operating costs excluding salaries

[5066] Other parts of the country that represent an important share of total operating expenses are the counties of Trøndelag, Hordaland, Rogaland, Vest-Agder and Buskerud

[5067] Capital investments generally have a completely different regional distribution

[5068] Nearly half of these expenses are imports

[5069] The remaining part of the material investments is distributed by counties where the supplier is located, and not, as for operating expenses, by where the Armed Forces have their operations

[5070] Norwegian industry's deliveries to the defense market cover a very broad product and technology spectrum and represent direct employment in the order of 10-12,000 jobs

[5071] Norwegian industry's turnover on the defense market amounted to approximately NOK 4.3 billion in 1989, of which just over NOK 1.7 billion was exports

[5072] Geographically, the defense industry is distributed across most of the country, but with clear centers of gravity in Oslo/Akershus, Buskerud and Oppland

[5073] The differences between individual companies in terms of size, organization, expertise and corporate culture are so great that it is difficult to provide a clear description of this industry

[5075] In order to promote and further develop attitudes and concrete measures with the aim of raising the quality level within Norwegian industry in general, the defense industry has therefore played a significant role as a driving force

[5076] The more advanced part of the defense industry plays the same locomotive role in a number of technological areas, and there are several examples of this having yielded results in the form of profitable production of equipment for civilian applications

[5090] General impact assessment and future measures Impacts on the districts - compensation measures

[5091] Many municipalities that have traditionally been described as defense-dependent will be affected as a result of the reductions and closures of activities that the proposed structure entails

[5092] The loss of jobs in the Armed Forces could have a dramatic effect on employment and tax revenues in some municipalities

[5093] The negative effects on other businesses in some municipalities and regions can also be serious, so the overall picture will entail major restructuring efforts for many municipalities

[5094] FK90 appointed three subcommittees tasked with assessing the consequences that restructuring the Armed Forces' activities could have

[5095] One of the subcommittees looked at the regional political consequences of the defense restructuring

[5096] It was found that several municipalities are highly dependent on the activities of the Armed Forces, and could be seriously affected by restructuring and reductions in the activities of the Armed Forces if this were found necessary in some of these municipalities

[5097] A more detailed study has been carried out, in which the Research Foundation at the University of Tromsø (FORUT) has been engaged to provide more knowledge about the effects of restructuring and reductions in the Armed Forces' activities on certain selected, defense-dependent municipalities

[5098] In this work, analytical models have been established that can provide an overview of the real consequences for employment and the economy in the municipalities of specific restructuring and reduction measures, both related to possible reductions in the number of officers, civilian employees and conscripts, and to reductions in operations and investments

[5099] The study has focused on both the consequences of given restructuring and reductions for employment in the municipalities, and the consequences for the municipalities' revenues

[5226] USE OF DEFENSE RESOURCES FOR CIVILIAN TASKS

[5227] TRADITIONAL AND NEW TASKS

[5228] In Norwegian society, it has traditionally been seen as a task for the Armed Forces to provide assistance when certain civilian needs arise

[5229] A guideline for changing governments has been that in peacetime the Armed Forces should perform or support civilian tasks where this falls naturally and can be combined with the Armed Forces' activities

[5230] In some cases, the use of the Armed Forces' resources for civilian tasks has appeared to be the most rational use of society's resources

[5231] The military has certain advantages in terms of

[5232] to be able to perform some civil duties in society

[5233] For these reasons, the Armed Forces are required to perform peacetime tasks such as coast guard service and rescue services, etc

[5234] The Government is committed to ensuring that the Armed Forces continue to assist civil society in carrying out important tasks

[5235] This contribution should also be able to be expanded somewhat in order to achieve the best possible overall utilization of society's resources

[5236] However, the question of using the Armed Forces' resources and expertise for civilian tasks raises important questions that affect both the design of the future defense structure and the very concept of what role and function the Armed Forces should have

[5237] Which tasks and to what extent the Armed Forces should be given responsibility for performing must be weighed against economics and the consideration of preserving the Armed Forces as an effective military organization

[5238] The Government's starting point for assigning the Armed Forces increased responsibility for carrying out civilian tasks

[5239] The government is pursuing an active economic policy to meet economic development

[5240] The difficult economic development is manifested, among other things, in the form of a sharply increasing deficit in the state budget, which in the somewhat longer term could lead to a serious limitation on the state's financial freedom of action

[5241] This places strong pressure on prioritization on the expenditure side of the state budget, where special emphasis is placed on economic growth and restructuring, alongside the ability to handle the consequences of high unemployment

[5242] In addition to the uncertainty this creates regarding what development profile the defense budget will be given in the annual budget prioritization, this also provides a strong incentive for the best possible socioeconomic total utilization of the resources allocated to the Armed Forces

[5243] Against this background, the Government is considering to what extent and in what way the Armed Forces can be given increased responsibility in solving civilian peacetime tasks

[5244] As part of an assessment of which tasks might be relevant in this regard, the Government appointed an interdepartmental study committee on 6 April 1992, under the leadership of the Ministry of Finance

[5245] The committee is assessing the possibilities for better coordination of coastal management

[5246] In the assessment of giving the Armed Forces increased responsibility for civilian peacetime tasks, a decisive criterion appears to be whether a socio-economic benefit can be achieved by giving the Armed Forces funds and responsibility for carrying out given tasks

[5247] The Armed Forces, with its organization, expertise and equipment, will be able to carry out specified civilian tasks that must be fulfilled under all circumstances

[5248] The question, however, is to what extent this can be done at lower costs than would be the case for alternative civilian bodies

[5249] To that extent

[5250] If the Armed Forces can solve tasks at a lower cost, it will be possible to reduce or not increase the budgets of other ministries

[5251] In this context, it will be a prerequisite that the principles of "A Better Organized State" are taken as a basis

[5252] This means that the clients will be charged the actual costs

[5253] The Armed Forces will have to carry out a given mission

[5254] Against this background, the extent of demand for the Armed Forces' services will be subject to a real needs assessment

[5255] This is a prerequisite for good economy of state resources

[5256] A number of factors must be taken into account when assessing which civilian tasks the Armed Forces can be given responsibility for, without coming into significant conflict with the military tasks the Armed Forces must cover in peacetime in order to produce an effective defense structure in war

[5257] Important considerations in this context are the consequences for the Armed Forces' organization, the personnel's level of competence, as well as the level of defense equipment and the personnel's ability to operate and utilize defense equipment effectively

[5258] The unique nature of defense tasks places special demands

[5259] The primary tasks of the Armed Forces in peacetime are to be the production apparatus for the war structure that, together with other, non-measurable factors such as leadership and morale, creates combat capability in crisis and war

[5260] War and conflict place special demands on organization, management and support staff, personnel training and equipment

[5261] Technological developments are contributing to increasing the demands on personnel's ability to operate and coordinate different weapons systems

[5262] More time and resources will have to be used for this purpose

[5263] An increasing degree of specialization is one of the results of the introduction of new weapons technology

[5264] Specialization will, in some areas, make it more difficult to apply military expertise for non-military tasks

[5265] UN service, especially peacekeeping operations and participation in multinational NATO forces, imposes special demands in peacetime, which limits freedom of action in terms of

[5266] to align organization, equipment and training to a significant extent towards civilian tasks

[5267] This is because the conscription and mobilization system mean that the Armed Forces are in a continuous state of training

[5268] While professional soldiers can be deployed for other tasks with far less harmful effects, a conscription defense is critically dependent on making the best possible use of the service time available for acquiring military skills and competence so that military tasks can be solved if a crisis or conflict should occur at a later date

[5269] The differentiation of service time that was adopted through St.prp

[5270] No. 98 (1991-92), collects an assumed efficiency gain and tightens the requirement for more efficient utilization of training time

[5271] The fact that war tasks, UN missions and participation in the NATO response force place special demands, not only in terms of material and training, but also organizationally, means that the Armed Forces must have specialized expertise that is not necessarily suitable for solving a wide range of civilian tasks

[5272] In order to achieve a socio-economic benefit, the civilian tasks must initially be able to be solved by the Armed Forces without having to build up specially organized, equipped and trained units

[5273] However, when special circumstances warrant it, it may be appropriate to establish separate, specialized units

[5274] The Armed Forces provide significant support to society and carry out civilian tasks

[5275] If the Armed Forces are considered to be given increased responsibility for civilian tasks at the expense of defense tasks, it will be important to carefully consider which tasks and to what extent so that the effects on the ability to solve defense tasks do not become unacceptably large

[5276] The Armed Forces' crisis prevention effect is linked to the credibility the Armed Forces have in relation to the outside world

[5277] This credibility depends on the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its assigned military tasks

[5351] Access to compete for civil contracts on a commercial basis

[5352] The downsizing of the Norwegian Armed Forces' peacekeeping organization outlined in this report can be countered to some extent by allowing the Norwegian Armed Forces' administrative and joint institutions to take on assignments on a commercial basis

[5353] Such an opening for access to income-generating assignments on a commercial basis, in both the public and private sectors, could contribute to the possibility of maintaining an appropriately large support system

[5354] It could also contribute to smaller personnel reductions than a direct dimensioning in relation to the Armed Forces' primary function

[5355] The starting point for such an assessment must be the distinction between the Armed Forces' primary and support functions, i.e. between the units that produce combat capability and the administrative/joint institutions that provide significant support to combat units

[5356] In the security and defence policy introduction to this report, cf. chapters 3 and 4, the uncertainty and unpredictability of current international developments are emphasized

[5357] The reduction in the Norwegian Armed Forces' war structure described in the report is combined with an assessment of the possibilities for rebuilding the Norwegian Armed Forces if security policy developments require it

[5358] A larger support system than the budget level would otherwise allow will be an important basis for a possible force build-up, not least in light of the fact that such a build-up of the defence organisation will require both time and resources, as this report explains in chapter

[5359] The larger the basic organization, the easier it will be to adapt the organization to any future escalation of the international situation

[5360] Opening up access to take on income-generating assignments outside the Armed Forces may require exemption from the appropriation regulations' requirement for gross budgeting, and it brings into question other organizational forms for service institutions in the Armed Forces, such as Forsvarets forskningsinstitutt (Forsvarets Forskningsinstitutt) and the State Canteens

[5361] A potential source of income also lies in giving the Armed Forces' workshops the opportunity to take on assignments outside the Armed Forces on a commercial basis

[5362] There will be intersecting political considerations in exploiting such an opportunity related to competition and the risk of conflict of interest with the private sector

[5363] In its further investigation, the Ministry will require that units that undertake assignments outside the Armed Forces have an internal management and organizational structure, including an accounting system, that makes the costs within the business visible

[5364] In this context, both the organizational forms of the relevant businesses and the basis on which they can undertake commercial assignments are assessed
